Job.CustomJobTypeName: Loss Control Consultant, Risk Management / Loss Control
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Erie, PA
  • Education: High school diploma or GED
  • Physical: Lifting up to 20 lbs

About this job

Summer internship in risk control with Erie Insurance's Future Focus program, running May-August 2027 in Erie, Pennsylvania. Includes mentorship, shadowing risk control consultants, research and data analysis projects, and networking with senior leaders.

Good fit if you are a college sophomore, junior, or senior pursuing a four-year degree, have a 3.0 GPA or higher, and can work onsite in Erie, Pennsylvania.

Full job description

Please Note: We are only considering US workers for this position. We are unable to offer this position to individuals who will require current or future immigration sponsorship for employment.

At Erie Insurance, we believe in professional and personal development. With our Future Focus Internship Program, both are provided in abundance. Not only do we offer the opportunity to gain professional experience in a challenging and competitive setting, but we welcome you as part of the ERIE family. We ensure that our interns receive the best internship experience possible, which includes multiple educational, developmental, professional, social and networking opportunities. The esteem ERIE holds in its Future Focus Internship Program is evident at every level of the organization, defined even further by multiple opportunities for socializing with high level leaders, up to and including our President and CEO. Are you ready for the internship experience of a lifetime? Look no further.

2027 Future Focus Internship Program Start Dates: Monday, May 17th and Monday, May 24th, 2027

2027 Future Focus Internship Program End Date: Friday, August 6th, 2027

Opportunity to join our Future Focus Internship Program as a Risk Control Intern

Erie Insurance is committed to helping you learn and grow with a challenging internship position that will offer you relevant and real-world business experience. We are currently seeking applicants who are interested in being considered for our upcoming summer internship program as potential Risk Control Interns!

Who should apply?

  • Applications are accepted from college students currently enrolled at an accredited college or university to pursue a four-year degree or to complete a master's degree program full-time
  • A four-year degree student should be completing sophomore, junior, or senior year (graduating in spring 2027 through spring 2029)
  • A minimum cumulative grade point average of 3.0 is highly preferred

About the Internship: The internship includes orientation to the company and the insurance industry through:

  • A variety of challenging assignments in a stimulating work environment
  • A personal mentor
  • A variety of educational, social and community service events with other interns
  • Social events and other networking activities with senior leaders including the CEO
  • Relocation assistance may be available to those who qualify
  • We have multiple talent programs and initiatives focused on attracting underrepresented students for internships and other job opportunities here at ERIE Insurance.

Position Summary

Under close supervision, performs functional duties for assigned division. Performs special projects as required.

Risk Control Interns will not only perform project related work that impacts our business and operations, but they will also spend time shadowing our Risk Control Consultants in real-world business cases and in-person visits. Projects can be research, data analysis, problem solving, and project management where creative thinking is encouraged.

  • Use your safety knowledge to evaluate and analyze accident and insurance claim trends
  • Propose solutions to reduce risk and accidents by identifying hazards and developing best practices
  • Research emerging commercial business operations for risk, safety, and insurance
  • Job shadow by participating in scheduled meetings and calls to learn our business
  • Learn fundamentals of the insurance industry, different insurance coverages, and professional business etiquette

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Performs various tasks related to the achievement of division objectives.
  • Conducts research and gathers information and assists in creating presentations as required.
  • Analyzes data and reports findings.
  • Verifies and enters data into appropriate system, and updates electronic files.
  • Provides clerical and administrative support as needed.
  • Completes special projects as required.


The first four duties listed are the functions identified as essential to the job. Essential functions are those job duties that must be performed in order for the job to be accomplished.

Regular and predictable attendance is an essential job function. For certain positions at ERIE, including leadership roles, regular and predictable onsite presence may also be an essential job function based on business and operational needs.


This position description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the incumbent. Employees are required to follow any other job-related instruction and to perform any other duties as requested by their supervisor, or as become evident.

Capabilities

  • Values Diversity
  • Information Management Skills
  • Nimble Learning
  • Self-Development
  • Job-Specific Knowledge
  • Collaborates
  • Customer Focus
  • Cultivates Innovation
  • Instills Trust
  • Optimizes Work Processes (IC)
  • Ensures Accountability
  • Decision Quality

Qualifications

Minimum Educational Requirements

  • High school diploma, or equivalent, required.
  • Pursuit of Bachelor's degree with completion of sophomore year in a relevant field required.


Additional Experience

  • Minimum 3.0 GPA preferred.
  • Working knowledge of word processing, spreadsheet and presentation software preferred.

Physical Requirements

  • Lifting/Moving 0-20 lbs; Often (20-50%)
  • Lifting/Moving 20-50 lbs; Occasional (<20%)
  • Ability to move over 50 lbs using lifting aide equipment; Occasional (<20%)
  • Driving; Rarely
  • Pushing/Pulling/moving objects, equipment with wheels; Occasional (<20%)
  • Manual Keying/Data Entry/inputting information/computer use; Frequent (50-80%)
  • Climbing/accessing heights; Rarely


Nearest Major Market: Erie

Quick facts

  • Pay: $122,400 to $204,400 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Remote
  • Experience: 8+ years

About this job

Lead Assurant's global trade compliance program, overseeing import, export, sanctions, and customs regulations for mobile devices and related technologies across global markets. Reports to AVP of Connected Living Compliance and manages a small team.

Good fit if you have 8+ years in global trade compliance, 5+ years leading teams, and experience with customs or export programs in tech or mobile device industries.

Full job description

Overview of Position


Reporting to the AVP, Connected Living Compliance, this position is responsible for leading Assurant's global trade compliance program and ensuring compliance with all applicable import, export, sanctions, and customs regulations. In addition to enterprise related trade activities, this role actively supports the movement of mobile devices, device components, service parts, accessories, and related technologies across global markets while enabling efficient customer, carrier, OEM, repair, refurbishment, and logistics operations.


The Director serves as a strategic advisor to Connected Living leadership and business stakeholders, balancing compliance obligations with customer commitments, operational efficiency, and commercial objectives.


This role will also partner, coordinate, and align global trade compliance activities and strategies with the Director, Global Supply Chain Compliance.


What will my duties and responsibilities be in this job?


Global Trade Compliance Leadership (45%)


  • Develop, implement, and continuously improve Assurant's global trade compliance program.
  • Establish governance, policies, procedures, and internal controls covering import, export, sanctions, and customs compliance.
  • Ensure compliance with:
    • U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR)
    • OFAC sanctions requirements
    • U.S. Customs regulations
    • International customs laws and regulations
    • Foreign trade regulations in countries where Assurant operates
  • Provide strategic guidance to executive leadership on global trade risks and opportunities.
  • Identify and implement value-creation opportunities, including duty drawback, free trade agreements, foreign trade zones, tariff engineering, and other lawful duty mitigation strategies.

Import Compliance and Customs Management (20%)


  • Oversee global customs compliance for mobile devices, service parts, accessories, and technology.
  • Ensure accurate:
    • HTS classifications
    • Country-of-origin determinations
    • Customs valuation
    • Duty assessment
  • Manage customs brokers and trade service providers.
    • Identify and implement duty savings strategies and opportunities.
  • Support optimization of global supply chain costs and customs efficiency.

Export Controls and Sanctions Compliance (20%)


  • Oversee export classification activities for devices, components, software, and technology.
  • Ensure compliance with export controls.
  • Lead restricted-party screening and sanctions compliance programs.
  • Provide guidance regarding cross-border shipments, technology transfers, and international business transactions.
  • Manage export licensing requirements and government authorizations when required.
  • Drive global alignment for HTS classification, country of origin, customs valuation, and Export Control Classification Number (ECCN) determinations.
  • Maintain awareness of export-controlled technology, software, encryption, and restricted-access information requirements applicable to Assurant operations.
  • Assess and manage export control risks involving restricted destinations, restricted parties, military end users, military end uses, and controlled technologies, software, or technical data; develop procedures for end-use/end-user due diligence, escalation, licensing analysis, and transaction holds where required.

Risk Management and Compliance Governance (10%)


  • Conduct enterprise-wide trade compliance risk assessments.
  • Develop and maintain trade compliance controls and monitoring programs.
  • Lead internal audits and compliance reviews.
  • Establish compliance metrics, dashboards, and executive reporting.
  • Investigate compliance incidents and manage corrective actions.
  • Lead government audits, inquiries, disclosures, and remediation activities.
  • Assists in remediating trade compliance issues as necessary, including but not limited to putting together project plans, connecting resources to find solutions, documenting resolutions, and documenting remediation plans.
  • Supports internal compliance audits and assists with managing external audits or inquiries from government agencies Maintains accurate data and recordkeeping to include collecting and retaining records in response to third-party inquiries relating to Assurant compliance practices and business activities.

Training and Culture (5%)


  • Develop and deliver trade compliance training and awareness programs.
  • Ensure employees understand their responsibilities related to international trade activities.
  • Maintain training records and support audit readiness.

Number of Direct Reports


  • 1-2 including a Compliance Analyst

Financial Responsibility


  • Signoff on responsible expenses, input on annual budget.

What are the requirements needed for this position?


Experience


  • Minimum of 8 years of progressive experience in global trade compliance.
  • At least 5 years of leadership experience.
  • Experience supporting multinational import/export operations.
  • Experience managing customs and export compliance programs.
  • Experience supporting technology, telecommunications, consumer electronics, mobile device, repair/refurbishment, or logistics industries preferred.

Education & Certifications


  • Bachelors' degree required, Master's or JD preferred

Preferred Certifications


  • Licensed Customs Broker (LCB)
  • Certified Export Specialist (CES)
  • Certified Customs Specialist (CCS)
  • Certified U.S. Export Compliance Officer (CUSECO)

Preferred Technical Expertise


  • EAR
  • OFAC sanctions compliance
  • Customs valuation
  • HTS classification
  • Country-of-origin analysis
  • Free Trade Agreements
  • Duty drawback
  • Foreign Trade Zones (FTZ)
  • Reverse logistics operations
  • Mobile device repair and refurbishment supply chains

Leadership Competencies

The candidate will be able to provide examples of successfully demonstrating the following leadership competencies:


  • Internal client-orientation with a constructive approach to resolution of issues. A style which builds alliances within the organization.
  • Ability to establish credibility with business owners, including senior and executive leadership, and influence through professional communication, work product, etc.
  • Solutions-oriented, demonstrated growth mindset.
  • Proven ability to build and maintain effective cross-functional relationships with clients, colleagues and stakeholders of various levels and areas throughout the organization.
  • Ability to lead change efforts through effective communication and persuasion.
  • Creative, resilient, and flexible style and approach to handling complex issues with high tolerance for ambiguity
  • Demonstrated leadership experience on leveraging data to drive actionable insights for risk or compliance programs
  • Clear written, visual and verbal communication skills, including ability to adjust messages dependent on audiences ranging from front-line employees to executive
  • Cultural competency and executive-level presence to work with the business and regional leadership teams around the world
  • Strong analytical, organizational, problem-solving, and follow-up skills. Ability to interpret rules and guidelines, and then conceptualize and implement into policies, procedures, and controls.
  • Excellent and demonstrated project management skills, and attention to detail in leading projects and activities in a global organization. Ability to prioritize and simultaneously execute on multiple projects and ability to organize and analyze complex information and data
  • Sound and independent judgment, and demonstrated prudence and maturity
  • Commitment to driving a culture of ethics and integrity
  • Cultivate a high-performing trade compliance team through coaching, mentoring, accountability, and development of trade compliance professionals.

Skills


The candidate will be able to demonstrate proficiency in the following skills:


  • Proficiency in the Microsoft Office Suite with specific emphasis in Word, Excel, PowerPoint
  • The ability to work in a fast-paced environment with several simultaneous deliverables
  • Program of project management skills

What other skills/experience would be helpful to have?


  • Experience in mobile or technology industries
  • Ability to use AI tools such as Copilot, ChatGPT, etc
  • Supply chain and vendor risk management experience

#AssurantProudMS


Pay Range

$122,400.00 - $204,400.00

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Insurance Customer Service Representative, Customer Service / Account Support
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: York, PA
  • Education: High school diploma or GED
  • Benefits: Paid holidays, tuition assistance

About this job

Assistant Account Manager providing day-to-day support to the Commercial Lines team at a major managing general agency. Responsibilities include quoting and rating policies, maintaining client records in Epic, issuing certificates of insurance, and supporting account managers with client service.

Good fit if you have commercial lines retail insurance agency experience and a PA Property & Casualty license or can obtain one within three months.

Full job description

Who We Are

For over 70 years, Glatfelter Insurance Group has believed in doing the right thing for our clients, agents, communities and associates. This founding principle has enabled Glatfelter to grow from the kitchen-table, one-man-operation as it began, to one of the largest managing general agencies in the U.S. with nearly 500 associates across the country, a distribution network of over 4,500 independent brokers and more than 30,000 clients. It is what drives us to innovate—the desire to deliver the best for our clients. Founded as The Glatfelter Agency, which is still in operation, the program basis of Glatfelter Insurance Group, Volunteer Firemen's Insurance Services (VFIS), was founded in 1969. Description

Claims Coverage Counsel/Claims Coverage Administrator

Hybrid Work Schedule

Buffalo, NY

Merchants Insurance Group is a leading Property and Casualty Insurer in the Northeast and is looking for an experienced Claims Coverage Counsel or Claims Coverage Administrator for our Corporate Claim Legal Team located in Buffalo, NY.

We are seeking individuals with previous experience in insurance coverage analysis/determination/disposition for at least five years. While a law degree is preferred, we are also considering individuals without a law degree that have deep technical experience in significant and complex coverage scenarios to include New York construction/labor law and other commercial claims.

This position will be responsible for preparing coverage opinions and coverage position letters for claims involving complex coverage issues or disputes. This role will also assist claims professionals in the evaluation of risk transfer opportunities, priority of coverage, and tender strategies. Coverage Counsel/Coverage Administrator is responsible for assessing and directing coverage litigation strategy in conjunction with outside counsel and the claims professional, including developing and executing a plan to manage the coverage litigation through final resolution. This individual may also provide legal support to underwriting, product development and regulatory compliance programs (JD candidate only).

This position is responsible for both first- and third-party coverage review, analysis and decisions for all levels of claims, including those involved in litigation. In addition, the individual will provide claim, policy, regulatory and legal expertise, if or as appropriate, to all levels of management up to and including senior management. The role will also review all policy forms for updates and revisions, ensuring compliance with state regulations, as well as applicable statutes and case law. The position will also require training for all levels of claims staff in matters of policy interpretation, investigatory processes, regulatory compliance and good faith claims practices across multiple venues.

Merchants Insurance Group is rated A- (Excellent) with a stable outlook by A.M. Best and is consistently recognized as a top employer and high-performing organization. Recent honors include:

  • Fast Track Company (2019–2025) and Top Private Company (2019–2025)
  • Ward's 50® top-performing property-casualty insurer (2021–2024)
  • Ivans Spark Award for Innovation (2024–2025)
  • Named to Newsweek and Statista's America's Most Reliable Companies list (2025), ranked among the top 300 of 1,500 B2B organizations evaluated

We offer a hybrid work schedule, requiring two full days per week in the office, with flexibility to work remotely or in office the remaining days. This model supports collaboration while providing flexibility and work-life balance.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Prepares coverage communication consistent with internal quality standards and applicable state regulations.
  • Works collaboratively with front-line claims professionals and managers to provide coverage analysis and preparation or review of coverage position letters for claims involving complex coverage issues or disputes.
  • Provides legal or coverage guidance to claim professionals handling declaratory judgment actions in which Merchants is a named party.
  • Directs outside counsel on litigation strategy.
  • Leads claim staff in training involving legal or coverage matters.
  • Provides claim legal support to underwriting and product development teams. Also assists in regulatory compliance programs by providing supplementary research regarding statutes and regulations impacting our business.

Benefits That Go Beyond The Basics

We strive to be Above all in Service® to our customers—and to our employees. That's why Erie Insurance offers you an exceptional benefits package, including:

  • Premier health, prescription, dental, and vision benefits for you and your dependents. Coverage begins your first day of work.

  • Pension. We are one of only 13 Fortune 500 companies to offer a traditional pension plan. Full-time employees are vested after five years of service.
  • 401(k) with up to 4% contribution match. The 401(k) is offered in addition to the pension.

Position Summary

This is a high-impact leadership role where you'll develop agents and District Sales Managers, help shape regional growth strategies, and make your mark at one of the most respected companies in the industry.

The ideal candidate will live in the state of Illinois while working remotely. This position comes with a company car with paid gas card.

What You'll Do

  • Partner with branch leaders to set and achieve growth, profitability, and agency development goals.

  • Serve as a hands-on mentor to Agents and District Sales Managers, building expertise in ERIE's commercial lines products and underwriting practices.

  • Evaluate complex commercial accounts, make underwriting and pricing decisions within authority, and collaborate with senior underwriters on larger risks.

  • Foster strong relationships with Agents, branch teams, and Home Office underwriting partners.

  • Represent ERIE in the community and maintain positive relationships with policyholders and stakeholders.

Who You Are

You're a strategic thinker who leads with influence, not just authority. You enjoy rolling up your sleeves to develop others and have the commercial acumen to guide agents toward success. You're comfortable making judgment calls on complex accounts and thrive on balancing growth with sound underwriting.

In addition, this position trains, develops and guides Agents and district sales managers (DSM) in a designated branch territory in the promotion and sale of commercial lines products, providing assistance in the areas of production, product knowledge and application, and underwriting. Establishes and maintains relationships with branch managers and Agents to improve Agent willingness and ability to pursue and place quality commercial business with the ERIE.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Assists branch managers in establishing short- and long-range objectives related to commercial lines sales, with an emphasis on growth, underwriting profitability and agency development and training.
  • Provides hands-on training and guidance to Agents on ERIE's commercial lines products, resources, and services, including identifying web-based resources and training programs for Agent use. Builds commercial expertise of new and existing Agents for increased independence and sound judgment when pursuing commercial business.
  • Provides hands-on training and guidance to branch DSMs on ERIE's commercial lines products, resources, and services, including identifying web-based resources and training programs. Builds commercial expertise of new and existing DSMs for increased independence and sound judgment when working with Agents to pursue commercial business.
  • Identifies Agents requiring additional guidance and interaction from their DSMs on commercial lines products and services. Works directly with DSMs, branch managers, and commercial underwriting staff to develop a plan to deliver that guidance and interaction as appropriate.
  • Contacts and visits Agents regularly to evaluate quotations and applications for multiple commercial lines to determine acceptability, including larger, more complex commercial accounts.
  • Makes acceptability and pricing decisions on risks within defined binding authority. Refers risks that are beyond binding authority to a senior commercial lines underwriter, risk analyst or underwriting supervisor.
  • Develops and maintains effective relationships and contact with Home Office commercial lines underwriting management and production underwriters.
  • Serves as a company representative in maintaining favorable Policyholder relationships. Works closely with adjusters and other claims personnel on matters of mutual concern.
  • Develops and maintains strong working knowledge of ERIE's commercial product lines, including policy features and key endorsements and sources of information on ERIE's products.
  • Represents the company in community relations activities as directed.
  • For branch office accounts, handles insurance agency business as a licensed, non-commission company Agent.

Senior Process Engineer at a high-volume, highly automated manufacturing facility in Mt. Juliet, Tennessee. Drives operational excellence through process optimization, continuous improvement initiatives, and cross-functional project leadership Monday through Friday, 8AM-5PM.

Good fit if you have a bachelor's degree in engineering, 3+ years in high-volume manufacturing, experience with Lean and Six Sigma, and strong project management skills.

Full job description

The Senior Process Engineer is responsible for driving operational excellence across a high-volume, highly automated manufacturing facility. This role provides technical leadership for manufacturing processes, equipment optimization, new product introductions, and large-scale continuous improvement initiatives to achieve world-class safety, quality, delivery, and cost performance.


The Senior Process Engineer leads cross-functional projects from concept through implementation, develops standardized manufacturing processes, and serves as a technical mentor to Process Engineers and Operations teams. This position partners closely with Operations, Maintenance, Quality, Automation, Supply Chain, and customers to improve manufacturing capability while supporting production performance and business objectives.


This is an onsite role in our Mt. Juliet TN facility with a schedule of Monday - Friday, 8AM – 5PM.


What will be my duties and responsibilities in this job?


Manufacturing Process Leadership

  • Provide technical leadership and engineering support for all production operations.
  • Develop, optimize, and standardize manufacturing processes to improve safety, quality, productivity, and cost.
  • Design and maintain manufacturing work instructions, process documentation, and standard operating procedures.
  • Establish best practices that improve process consistency and manufacturing reliability.
  • Support new product introductions, equipment launches, and production transfers.

Project Management

  • Lead complex, cross-functional capital and operational improvement projects.
  • Develop project timelines, budgets, resource plans, launch curves, and risk mitigation strategies.
  • Create project dashboards and tracking systems to ensure milestones, deliverables, and financial targets are achieved.
  • Coordinate activities between Engineering, Operations, Quality, Automation, Supply Chain, Maintenance, and external suppliers.
  • Present project status and business results to plant leadership.

Continuous Improvement

  • Lead Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, and Value Stream Mapping initiatives throughout the facility.
  • Identify opportunities to reduce manufacturing cost, improve throughput, eliminate waste, and increase equipment utilization.
  • Utilize data analytics to identify process bottlenecks and prioritize improvement opportunities.

Root Cause Analysis & Problem Solving

  • Lead structured problem-solving activities utilizing:
    • DMAIC
    • 8D
    • 5 Why
    • Fishbone Analysis
    • FMEA
  • Investigate manufacturing failures, field returns, and customer complaints.
  • Validate corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) to eliminate recurring issues.
  • Support production during critical downtime events and major quality issues.

Data Analysis

  • Analyze manufacturing KPIs including:
    • Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE)
    • First Pass Yield (FPY)
    • Throughput
    • Cycle Time
    • Scrap
    • Rework
    • Labor Efficiency
    • Cost per Unit
    • Capacity Utilization
  • Utilize statistical analysis and manufacturing data to drive operational decisions.

Cross Functional Leadership

Exercises independent discretion or judgment in handling all types of property claims. Also assists or acts on behalf of the claims supervisor when required.

About this job

Supply Chain Manager overseeing material flow, inventory control, and cost reduction in a reverse logistics depot in Irving, Texas. Leads inventory control teams, manages KPIs, and coordinates work across multiple shifts to ensure production runs smoothly.

Good fit if you have 7+ years logistics/distribution experience, 5+ years leadership managing supervisors, and 2+ years inventory management experience.

Full job description

The Supply Chain Manager is responsible for ensuring the smooth flow of materials and products necessary for production and operational success within the depots. In addition to managing the entire lifecycle of materials, from procurement to distribution, ensuring that production processes run smoothly, maintains optimal inventory levels to prevent shortages or excess, which can disrupt production or tie up capital unnecessarily, and implement strategies to reduce costs while maintaining quality and supply continuity. This is accomplished through the development of lean processes and procedures that meet internal and external customer requirements and the effective leadership of Inventory Control resources through clear and precise communications of responsibilities and goals.

This is an onsite role in our Irving, TX facility. Multiple shifts and positions are available.

This job posting is part of our ongoing efforts to build a strong talent network for current and future opportunities. We invite you to apply, and qualified candidates will be contacted as roles become available.

What will be my duties and responsibilities in this job?

  • Effective operation by working with the supervisors to complete customer priorities based on demand schedules, assigning tasks/projects as needed, coordinating the flow of work, oversee completion of work, monitor key performance metrics (KPI), managing labor efficiency across the area of responsibility, mentor/coach leaders and manage headcount
  • Ensure adherence to company policies and process standards, while maintaining employee morale and overseeing the training of new and existing staff for the department
  • Establish, track, and analyze departmental reports/measurements and present findings as appropriate
  • Work with senior management to establish department and company goals, and rely on experience, judgment and innovation to achieve them
  • Identify process improvements for the department along with the design of KPIs and coordinate new model introductions
  • Create and utilize reports to accurately represent product flow and task completion rates and percentages
  • Develop and utilize reporting to ensure SLAs are achieved
  • Manage cycle counts and inventory control processes to ensure inventory accuracy maintained
  • Liaison between teams, shifts, and departments, and partners with vendor/customer/client representatives while fostering true partner relationships that allow us to manage change and growth within the individual business
  • Monitor inventory of stock and ensure adequate levels are maintained
  • Provides technical and operational support during the business development process and new customer acquisition
  • Maintain a clean, organized and safe work environment for personnel to work in while ensuring all safety and environmental regulations are followed
  • Develop and establish document controls to ensure accuracy of inventory
  • Hires, develops, evaluates, and (when necessary) disciplines and discharges subordinates' personnel or makes authoritative recommendations in such matters
  • Develops function-specific orientation and training programs for area personnel
  • Establishes standards for effective job performance and evaluates subordinates according to such standards

What are the requirements needed for this position?

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent in any business or related discipline
  • Minimum seven (7) years' experience required in a logistics/distribution, fast paced, high volume manufacturing environment with at least five (5) years of data interpretation/analysis and logistics experience and 2 of inventory management experience
  • Minimum of five (5) years leadership experience with at least five (5) years' experience managing supervisory personnel

What other skills/experience would be helpful to have?

  • APICS CPIM designation
  • Working knowledge and understanding of MRP/ERP systems, WIP & Planning, Preferred knowledge with Oracle
  • Experience with Microsoft Great Plains
  • Highly skilled inventory control leader with extensive strategic and tactical experience, results-oriented, high energy, high urgency, and embraces effective change
  • High level of customer interaction; frequent interruptions and re-prioritization of projects based upon customer needs, working under deadlines, creative thinking, working on multiple projects simultaneously, and ability making decisions based on various levels of information
  • Working knowledge of Visio
  • Ability to interact and understand IT issues related to business processes and systems changes
  • Knowledge of inventory and warehousing processing procedures
  • Experience in, manufacturing, automation, electronics, systems integration, life cycle modeling, new product introduction, process development and deployment, leveraging Lean/6 Sigma tools, project and resource planning, and systems implementation

About this job

Troubleshoot insurance claims and order management processes at Assurant's Irving facility. Use Oracle and technical tools to manage order flow, coordinate with multiple departments, and ensure timely device shipment within service level agreements.

Good fit if you have 2+ years in distribution and logistics, strong Excel skills, and Oracle experience preferred.

Full job description

Perform troubleshooting on all insurance claims and other order types and assist to identify and execute various enhancements to all order management processes. Ensure compliance with all company and business policies and administer all and ensure appropriate order flow.

This is an onsite role in our Irving TX facility with a schedule of Monday - Thursday, 6AM – 4.30PM.

What will be my duties and responsibilities in this job?

  • This is a highly technical job, where understanding of order flow, process flow and above average knowledge of the Operating system is crucial for successful performance
  • Manage all communication with Materials, Operations and Fulfilment centers and in order to satisfy and process all insurance orders and timely shipment of devices within SLA.
  • Using current warehouse management system (Oracle) to modify, migrate and push orders using technical knowledge in order to facilitate order flow until shipment.
  • Verify all order lines and prepare reports on everyday basis and manage all shipment and respond to all inquiries for all status order and resolve all order issues
  • Monitor and evaluate all order issues and resolve using tools available
  • Work in tandem with Purchasing department in order to resolve escalations for claims which can't be satisfied based on current stock availability
  • Using tools available, this position is responsible to generate multiple reports in order to send priority and urgency to other departments. For example: Priorities needed to satisfy backorders. Receiving daily priorities, Kitting Priorities
  • Technical research for current claims needing migration of existing models and execute those migrations in order to satisfy claims within SLA.
  • Communicate with the Planning Department on devices that need to be prioritized from Production lines for all programs.
  • Ensure FIFO is followed to satisfy older claims
  • Depending on program and customer additional research will be needed in order to move orders from Entered status into Booked status, allowing the orders to be cascaded within the system
  • Create different feedback reports to monitor overall SLA attainment on a daily/monthly basis and publish this data to stakeholders
  • Create reports of status, pending shipment, and overall status of claims at a model level for all programs and the action items needed to fulfil and troubleshoot orders
  • Other duties as assigned

What are the requirements needed for this position?

  • High School Diploma or equivalent. BS/BA on a technical field preferred
  • 2+ years of distribution and logistics background.
  • MS Excel proficiency in order to manage large amount of data
  • MS Word proficiency in order to create basic documents and reports
  • Good communication skills in order to interact and influence others

What other skills/experience would be helpful to have?

  • Oracle experience a plus.
  • Experience in inventory control, material management/movement of more than 2 years desired

What are the working conditions and physical requirements of this job?

  • Occasional: bending, squatting, kneeling, reaching, twisting, exposure to changes in temperature, being near moving machinery, and office machinery
  • This position requires incumbents to regularly sit at a desk and operate standard office equipment such as a computer and phone
  • Employee is occasionally required to stand and walk, lift, carry and/or move up to 40 pounds
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus
  • Ability to talk and hear
  • Required to use hands and fingers, handle, or feel objects, tools, or controls. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions

At Assurant, our Customer Care Representatives are the voice of our organization and the first point of contact for our valued customers. We are deeply invested in your success and committed to providing a supportive, inclusive, and growth-oriented environment.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Chicago, IL

About this job

Virtual mentorship program for college sophomores to learn about actuarial consulting careers at Aon from February to April 2027. Selected participants can be fast-tracked to interview for Summer 2028 internship positions in Health, Wealth, Risk, or Reinsurance.

Good fit if you are a current sophomore with 3.0 GPA or higher, majoring in actuarial science, mathematics, statistics, economics, or related field

Full job description

Job Description

Early Careers: Sophomore Actuarial Career Discovery Program

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What is the Sophomore Actuarial Career Discovery Program?

College Sophomores have the unique opportunity to connect with an advisor working in the actuarial field at Aon to learn more about a consulting career from one of our solutions team from either Health, Wealth, Risk, or Reinsurance and practice real-world scenarios during the discovery program.

How this opportunity is different

This mentorship opportunity gives students considering a career in actuarial science to connect with professionals and peers throughout this virtual program. This program is designed for sophomores and used as a direct pipeline to our Summer 2028 Actuarial Intern opportunities!

At the end of the program, selected mentees will have the opportunity to be fast-tracked to a final round interview for consideration for our intern program. While the mentor program is virtual, candidates would select location preferences that are aligned with their interests for Summer 2028 internship opportunities.

Program Dates: February 2027 - April 2027

Recruitment Window:

- Application Deadline: November 2026

- Review Process: November - December 2026

- Program Acceptance: December 2026 - January 2027

Skills and experience that will lead to success

We're looking for collaborators, critical thinkers, problem solvers, excellent teammates, effective communicators, relationship builders and future leaders.

Education: Preferred Majors in Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, or related. All majors welcome to apply.

Applicants for this event should be current sophomores, graduating between December 2028 - June 2029, with a GPA of 3.0 and above

How we support our colleagues

Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant, and more valued.

Aon values an innovative, diverse workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. Aon is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

Aon provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran, marital, domestic partner status, or other legally protected status. People with criminal histories are encouraged to apply.

We welcome applications from all and provide individuals with disabilities with reasonable adjustments to participate in the job application, interview process and to perform essential job functions once onboard. This Financial Planning & Analysis Specialist will perform and deliver on routine assignments and projects while leveraging and applying knowledge of FP&A principles to support Lincoln Financial Distributors (LFD). Job Description

Our Commercial Risk team in Denver is looking for an Account Executive IV!

We are looking for a leader who is responsible for the overall strategy as well as the day-to-day, account management of Aon's relationships with assigned clients as their primary role. You will lead client service teams to identify and meet client needs and thereby retain and grow a profitable book of business. Through service, pricing, consultation, and reporting, you will promote the value Aon delivers to clients.

This is a hybrid role out of our office in Denver, CO.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

  • Retains and grows Aon's business, cultivating relationships with senior-most client decision-makers in the client organization as well as with day-to-day client contacts.
  • Drives the renewal process, assembling the appropriate team to develop and implement the client-specific renewal strategy.
  • Coordinates with Brokers in the development and delivery of renewal strategies.
  • Facilitates critical relationships between clients, Aon and insurers.
  • Ensures client service team understanding of client needs, service delivery methods, and the economic framework relevant to services delivered.
  • Leads stewardship planning and delivery.
  • Ensures overall account profitability with a value-based approach for the scope of service and costs associated with the Client Promise Plan.
  • Arranges Aon compensation for services, whether fee or commission-based, accordingly.
  • Educates clients in risk management, risk transfer, market issues and relevant trends including appropriate data and analytics.
  • Marshals appropriate Aon resources to support clients in unusual circumstances such as large claims, etc.
  • Involves others across geographic (including international), functional and business unit boundaries to define interdependent responses to opportunities to grow the business.
  • Manages input to and follow-up on invoicing and receivables process for assigned clients, ensuring timely collections.

Skills and experience that will lead to success

  • Must have a minimum of 15 years of appropriate risk insurance experience coupled with project and account management experience on large accounts.
  • Strong sales skills
  • Organizational, interpersonal, and project management skills with an ability to multi-task and prioritize workload with attention to detail.
  • Critical thinking skills with the ability to clearly express thoughts and concepts at various levels.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite products such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook
  • Must have an active Property & Casualty license.

Education: Bachelor's degree preferred or equivalent years of industry experience.

Compensation:

The salary range for this position is $205,000 – $285,000 annually. This salary range is an estimate and the actual salary will vary based on applicant's education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant's geographic location.

This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon's annual incentive plans. The amount of the incentive varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan.

How we support our colleagues

Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon's discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance. This role does not accrue vacation. Rather, this role is eligible to take paid time off at the discretion of the employee and management in accordance with company policy and practices. Various other types of leaves of absence; paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies.

In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce. Plus, our agile environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions for our colleagues as well.

Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant, and more valued.

Aon values an innovative and inclusive workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. Aon is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

Aon provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran, marital, domestic partner status, or other legally protected status. At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of the Senior Managing Litigation Attorney is to oversee a team of attorneys ranging from entry level to seasoned senior litigation management attorneys. This position is responsible for overseeing and reviewing work performed by attorneys to ensure compliance with defense counsel guidelines. The role works to improve processes, as well as assists with budget planning, financial measures and results. The Senior Managing Attorney will identify and lead initiatives to improve the team's efficiency and ensures effective communication between the legal and business teams. This role acts as both a Litigation Attorney with a reduced case count and manages a staff of Litigation attorneys. The position works autonomously and under the general supervision of the Litigation Management's department Director.

This is a hybrid position, offering the flexibility to work from both home and the office. Candidates must be able to work from one of our California branch offices in San Diego, Pasadena, or Rancho Cordova.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Directs the operations of law office personnel providing litigation and legal services.

  • Oversees the law office activities to ensure efficient operations of In-House Counsel.

  • Determines the intake and assignment of cases to ensure distribution based on each attorney's level of expertise and associated location (region or county).

  • Achieves the departments and company goals by making strategic business decisions.

  • Ensures the firm is achieving its client satisfaction goals by evaluating productivity and quality of service.

  • Identifies, makes recommendations for work process improvements and follows through to implement remediations.

  • Works with leadership to ensure the department meets financial and ROI goals, identifies trends, prepares reports, and implements modifications as needed.

  • Mentors less experienced attorneys and ensures the team continues to expand their job-related knowledge, skills and abilities.

  • Regularly reviews cases and provides feedback on legal strategies, compliance with deadlines, timeliness on response, and maximizing the department's core goals.

Provides litigation services and is responsible for all aspects of assigned Workers' Compensation matters.

  • Handles a reduced caseload of litigated files and ensures files are fully worked and moved to resolution.

  • Litigates workers' compensation cases in California before all state and federal courts, administrative boards, and other court proceedings.

  • Represents ICW Group, its related entities and insureds before administrative boards, state and federal courts, Court of Appeal, and the California Supreme Court.

  • Analyzes complex legal and factual issues; conducts extensive, well-reasoned legal research, as necessary; independently develops and presents defense strategies on behalf of ICW Group.

  • Provides strategic legal advice, recommendation, and implementation of clear, cost-effective, and efficient plans of action.

  • Assists in analyzing, reviewing, and distributing information on new legislation, regulations, and court decisions.

Provides oversight of a team of Litigation Management professionals.

  • Oversees the entire employee lifecycle from identifying, training, coaching and retaining talent.

  • Supervises and evaluates, mentors, motivates, and develops attorneys to strengthen the legal team.

  • Communicates clear performance expectations for the assigned team as well as providing support and guidance for achieving the department's metric, billable hours and expectations.

  • Communicates and enforces team values including mission statement of In-House Counsel (IHC) and ICW.

  • Establishes and maintains the overall work cadence and, in partnership with Department leadership, ensures performance and outcomes strive for excellence in delivery and customer experience.

  • Acts as a resource for team members to answer questions and assist in the solution to complex problems.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

Directly supervises employees within the Litigation Management team and carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policies and applicable laws. These responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; conducting performance and salary reviews; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems; coaching, mentoring, and developing team members to further their skills and knowledge; creating and monitoring development plans; setting performance expectations/goals; forecasting staffing needs and planning for peak times and absences; enforcing department policies and procedures.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's degree from four-year college or university required. Juris Doctorate from an accredited law school required.

  • Minimum 10 years' workers' compensation legal experience handling complex cases along with a minimum of 2 years' experience managing associate through senior litigation attorneys.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Licensed and in good standing with the State Bar of California with no history of public or private reprisals.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Good computer skills with MS Office (including MS Excel with the ability to create financial/performance reports).

  • Proficient in the use of applications/programs to create automated reports, templates, systems and data retrieval of high quality and reliability.

  • Expert knowledge litigating California workers' compensation matters with trial experience and prior experience handling cases with varying degrees of complexity.

  • Deep understanding of workers' compensation administrative rules, laws, statutes, legal principles and practices.

  • Excellent communication skills (verbal/written).

  • Ability to communicate effectively with external and internal team members, clients, businesses, and members of the State Bar and Judiciary, including effectively responding to concerns and sensitive matters.

  • Ability to effectively present information, verbally and in writing, to clients, claims personnel, top management, public groups, Board of Directors, mediators, arbitrators, judges, and juries.

  • Skilled at logical thinking to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions.

  • Consistently maintains professional and appropriate demeanor, works harmoniously with others and responds positively to feedback.

  • Demonstrated experience in working independently under minimal supervision, maintaining a strong work ethic, and exercising initiative.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

This position operates in an office, home, and court environment and requires frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, scanner, and other standard office equipment. The position requires traveling to various court locations and works at one of the offices of In-House Counsel on a weekly basis.

This description is a general statement of essential job functions and responsibilities. The position may include other duties as assigned.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

The Role at a Glance

We're seeking an experienced AVP, Sr. Counsel, Leave Management & Statutory Disability to lead a team responsible for providing legal guidance and compliance support for Group Protection's leave management and statutory disability products. In this role, you will provide strategic leadership, legal expertise, and regulatory oversight while partnering across the organization to support business objectives, ensure compliance, and drive innovation in a rapidly evolving regulatory environment.

As a trusted advisor you will collaborate with partners across Product, Operations, Finance, Marketing, Underwriting, Claims, and Compliance to manage legal risk, support product development, and maintain compliance with federal and state leave laws. You will also represent Lincoln in interactions with regulators, industry groups, customers, and other external stakeholders.

What you'll be doing

• Providing leadership and development opportunities to a team responsible for legal and compliance support for Group Protection's leave management and statutory disability products.
• Monitoring and analyzing legislative and regulatory developments affecting leave and statutory disability programs, assessing the business impact, and advising stakeholders on emerging risks and opportunities.
• Partnering with internal and external stakeholders to ensure products, services, and processes remain compliant with applicable federal and state laws and regulations.
• Providing legal counsel on complex leave-related matters, including claims escalations, policy interpretation, leave agreements, and operational inquiries.
• Conducting legal research and analysis regarding proposed and existing laws and regulations, and providing practical, business-focused recommendations.
• Supporting multiple business functions that serve or impact leave management and statutory disability products.
• Contributing to enterprise and business unit strategies involving leave-related legal, regulatory, and compliance matters.
• Building and maintaining strong partnerships with business leaders through active engagement, consultation, and project participation.
• Representing the organization in discussions with regulators, industry associations, and other external stakeholders on leave and statutory disability matters.
• Preparing and delivering presentations to customers, brokers, industry groups, and internal audiences.
• Serving as a subject matter expert on leave management, statutory disability programs, and related legal and regulatory requirements.
• Identifying, assessing, and communicating legal, regulatory, and compliance risks to senior leadership in a timely and proactive manner.
• Drafting, negotiating, reviewing, and approving customer agreements and other contracts related to leave programs.
• Managing dispute resolution matters, regulatory inquiries, and commercial claims.
• Providing strategic legal and business counsel to senior management and key stakeholders.
• Supporting compliance programs and initiatives within Group Protection and across the enterprise.
• Fostering a culture of compliance, integrity, accountability, and ethical decision-making.

What we're looking for

Must Have:

• 7+ years of legal experience in a large law firm, corporate legal department, or a combination of both.
• J.D. from an ABA-accredited law school.
• Active membership in at least one state bar and in good standing.
• Strong legal research, analytical, negotiation, and problem-solving skills.
• Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
• Demonstrated ability to influence and collaborate effectively with legal colleagues, business partners, and senior leaders.
• Proven ability to manage complex legal matters and balance business objectives with legal and regulatory requirements.

Nice to Have:

• Experience advising on leave management and statutory disability products.
• Knowledge of federal and state leave laws and the broader leave services regulatory framework.
• Understanding of leave administration concepts, industry trends, and market developments.
• Experience supporting insurance, employee benefits, or related financial services products.

Job Description

Do you have a passion for using your ambition and creativity to build new relationships? Do you want to be part of a sales culture where producers are recognized, valued and perform significantly better than their industry peer group? Aon has exciting opportunities to join our Commercial Risk team as a Producer in Dallas.

Aon is in the business of better decisions.

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

  • Showcase connections and networking capabilities to generate new business
  • Influence and collaborate with others to create strategic plans and present a variation of risk solutions to meet client needs
  • Broaden your consultative reach by engaging prospects and providing creative and applicable advice across all of Aon's solutions.
  • Solve complex business issues using the data and analytics available at your fingertips from Aon's research teams combining your eye for business and understanding of current trends
  • Support a team in the management of a portfolio of prospects' business

How this opportunity is different:

Aon is the leading global professional services firm providing advice and solutions in Risk, Retirement and Health at a time when those topics have never been more important to the global economy. Aon develops insights - driven by data and delivered by experts - that reduce the volatility our clients face and help them enhance their performance.

Skills and experience that will lead to success

  • 5-10+ years of experience in insurance, consulting or enterprise products and/or services
  • Demonstrated capability to adhere to and champion a successful sales process
  • Current have or willingness to obtain Life and Health and/or P&C license(s)

Education: Bachelor's degree or equivalent years of industry experience.

Pay Transparency Laws

The salary range for this position is $125,000 - $200,000 annually. This salary range is an estimate, and the actual salary will vary based on applicant's education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant's geographic location.

This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon's annual incentive plans to receive production incentives in addition to base salary. The amount of any production incentives varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan.

How we support our colleagues

Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon's discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies.

In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce. Plus, our agile environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions for our colleagues as well.

Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant, and more valued.

Aon values an innovative and inclusive workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. Aon is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

The Analyst on the Funds Strategy Team is a key contributor supporting fund strategy, analytics, project management, and business reporting across Lincoln's manager-of-managers investment platform. The analyst will help maintain and evaluate fund lineups supporting Lincoln's insurance and retirement products, conduct quantitative analysis using internal and external data sources, and develop reports and presentations that communicate strategic recommendations to senior leadership, board stakeholders, and business partners. The position supports assets across equity, fixed income, multi-asset funds, and Lincoln's proprietary variable insurance trust mutual funds.

What you'll be doing

  • Support and coordinate cross-functional projects from planning through execution, managing timelines, deliverables, dependencies, and stakeholder communications.
  • Maintain, monitor, and analyze fund lineups for insurance and retirement products, including performance, fees, risk metrics, product guideline compliance, and fund change activity.
  • Perform quantitative analysis using large and complex datasets and identify meaningful trends and insights.
  • Develop executive-ready reports, presentations, dashboards, and recommendations for leadership and business stakeholders.

Advanced Excel skills and experience working with large datasets are required. Ability to understand which data points are most meaningful when analyzing mutual funds or investment strategies.
  • Strong Written and Verbal Communication: Ability to translate complex investment and data-driven concepts into concise, polished communications, reports, and presentations. Proven relationship management skills, attention to detail, and the ability to influence, persuade, and manage competing stakeholder priorities.

  • Experience with Investment Data Vendors: Knowledge of Morningstar and other investment data providers, with the ability to validate and reconcile information across vendor platforms, SEC filings, and internal sources.

Job.JobTitle: Business Analyst I, II, III (Personal & Commercial Residential Insurance)
Job.JobDescription:
Position Summary:

We are seeking an experienced Business Analyst with solid expertise in personal and/or commercial residential property insurance to support and enhance our Policy and/or Claims Administration systems. This role will partner with business stakeholders and technology teams to analyze workflows, define requirements, support system enhancements, and resolve production issues that impact critical insurance operations.

This position may be filled at the BA I, BA II, or BA III level, depending on the candidate's experience, skills, and demonstrated ability to work independently, lead initiatives, and influence outcomes. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, proactive, and comfortable operating in a dynamic, regulated environment with evolving priorities.

Essential Functions:

Business & Systems Analysis

  • Partner directly with Underwriting, Product, Operations, Compliance, Claims, and Technology teams to gather and document business requirements
  • Translate underwriting and/or claims guidelines, eligibility rules, rates, forms, endorsements, and workflows into functional system requirements
  • Support enhancements and configuration of online quote/bind applications and policy/claims administration systems
  • Create user stories, business process flows, requirement documentation, acceptance criteria, and traceability artifacts
  • Analyze impacts of product or regulatory changes to system functionality and business processes
  • Perform other related duties and responsibilities as assigned to support business objectives.

Project Delivery & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Participate in or lead requirements workshops, discovery sessions, and backlog refinement meetings.
  • Manage changing priorities and scope while ensuring requirements remain clear, documented, and approved.
  • Participate in testing validation, defect triage, and production implementation activities
  • Provide clear, timely communication and status updates to stakeholders.

Documentation & Quality Assurance

  • Create and maintain documentation while ensuring Confluence is consistently updated and serves as the single source of truth for requirements including workflows, business rules, system behaviors, and configuration details.
  • Develop and execute test plans, track defects and coordinate fixes.
  • Ensure delivered solutions meet business requirements, quality standards, and compliance expectations.

Production Support & Issue Resolution

  • Troubleshoot system issues, identify root cause, and coordinate resolution with IT and development teams.
  • Support production incidents and escalated help desk tickets related to our systems.
  • Communicate issue status, risks, and resolution progress effectively to business partners.
  • Review escalated Service Desk tickets to identify opportunities for process improvement, knowledge base development, and training, facilitating the transition of repeatable support activities and issue resolution from higher support tiers to Level 1 Service Desk teams.

Why Windward Risk Managers:

  • Windward Risk Managers is proud to be recognized on Fortune's 2026 Best Medium Workplaces list, ranking #28 among the Top 100 companies
  • 100% employer paid health insurance for employees
  • Up to 6% 401(k) match with immediate vesting
  • Long-term and short-term disability insurance
  • 3 weeks PTO to start + generous paid holidays
  • Tuition reimbursement and continuing education support
  • Collaborative and growth focused culture

Qualifications

Required Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience.
  • Professional experience in the Property & Casualty Homeowners and/or Residential Commercial insurance industry functioning in a Business Analyst capacity, including requirements elicitation, documentation, and collaboration with technical teams to implement changes to insurance or policy administration systems.
  • Proven experience analyzing business problems, troubleshooting issues, and applying logical, detail-oriented approaches to develop effective solutions with limited supervision.
  • Demonstrated experience managing multiple assignments simultaneously, prioritizing work, managing scope, and driving work to completion with minimal supervision in a fast-paced, results-driven environment.
  • Demonstrated experience working with cross-functional teams, business stakeholders, and technical resources, with strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience working in Agile / Scrum or sprint-based delivery environments.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of professional experience in a Business Analyst role within the Property & Casualty insurance industry.
  • Experience supporting Homeowners and/or Residential Commercial lines of business for Florida, Texas, and/or California risks, including familiarity with state-specific products, forms, rating, underwriting, or regulatory requirements.
  • Experience with Duck Creek.
  • Familiarity with regulated environments such as Florida and/or Texas.
  • Insurance carrier or MGA background strongly preferred.
  • Business Analyst certification (CBAP, CCBA, PMI-PBA) a plus.

Essential Skills:

  • Ability to understand technical concepts and communicate effectively with developers and system vendors.
  • Strong attention to detail especially when working with policy, forms, rating, claims, or billing system changes.
  • Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to evaluate business needs and translate them into clear, well-defined requirements.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision while maintaining accountability for quality and timeliness of deliverables.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, including the ability to research issues, recreate steps, identify root causes, and recommend practical solutions.
  • Ability to understand complex business processes, system workflows, and dependencies.
  • Proficiency with business analysis, documentation, and collaboration tools used to support project delivery.

Due to current business and operational considerations, we currently hire employees residing in the following states at this time: AL, AR, CA, CT, FL, GA, KY, MO, NC, NV, OH, SC, TN, TX, VA, and WI.

  • This role requires permanent U.S. work authorization and does not offer employer sponsorship now or in the future.

The Role at a Glance

As a Facilities Technician, you will work independently and within a team to ensure the efficient operation, maintenance and repair of two of the 4 technical skill areas; electrical systems, plumbing, control systems, and HVAC systems under the direction of the Senior Facilities Technician.

What you'll be doing

Technical and Preventive Maintenance

• Independently performing emergency repairs, preventive maintenance, installation and/or operation, projects and troubleshooting in assigned areas of responsibility, which may involve two of the four technical skill areas.

Systems

• Performing electronic/controls work including building automation systems, fire and security, energy management systems, monitoring systems, lighting controls, HVAC controls, sound systems, UPS and associated power equipment, and access control systems, etc.
• Performing electrical systems work including distribution systems, circuit wiring and terminations, central distribution gear, intermediate gear, breaker panels, lighting systems, high voltage transformers, emergency power generation equipment, motor control centers, power conditioning, etc.
• Performing plumbing work including hot water and steam boiler systems, steam and hydronic distribution systems, domestic water systems, chilled water plumbing, sanitary systems, pumping and injection systems, and fuel delivery systems.
• Performing HVAC systems work including the operation, maintenance and repair of heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems and controls. This includes all air delivery systems, chillers, DX cooling systems, air handlers, evaporative cooling, cooling towers, heat exchangers and all associated control systems.

Projects and Troubleshooting

• Acting as project lead on small projects and/or assisting the senior technician on major projects.
• Independently performing service calls, troubleshooting and repairing systems as needed and handling emergency repairs in all skill areas.
• Checking work of less experienced team members.
• Performing general maintenance functions and backup in support of critical systems or projects.
• Participating as part of the on-call rotation.

Knowledge and Skills

• Demonstrating complex level of knowledge in the primary technical area required with a demonstrated skill resolving potentially high risk maintenance and building emergencies.
• Maitaining working knowledge of all other technical skill areas.
• Using of hand tools safely and effectively.
• Demonstrating knowledge and understanding of OSHA and general work place safety.
• Demonstrating willingness to be on-call and adjust shifts to meet emergencies and project requirements.

What we're looking for

Educational

• Basic math and measurement skills

Experience

• 2-3 years of experience/training in HVAC, Electrical, Plumbing, and Control Systems

• Attendance of specialized training in two of the four technical skill areas: HVAC, Electrical, Plumbing, and Control Systems.
