What Is the Opportunity?

Travelers is seeking a Senior Software Engineer, Guidewire BillingCenter, to join our organization as we grow and transform our billing technology landscape. We are looking for a Guidewire BillingCenter engineer with strong integration development and configuration experience. The individual will complete advanced, end-to-end engineering tasks within Guidewire BillingCenter and related integrations, including designing, developing, configuring, analyzing, testing, debugging, troubleshooting, documenting, health monitoring/alerting, and implementing solutions based on user or system specifications. The individual will also consult with users and partners to define functional and technical specifications for Guidewire BillingCenter, manage the effective use of resources, act as a subject matter expert for BillingCenter and associated services, leverage deep Guidewire and business knowledge to drive the planning and execution of complex billing modernization initiatives, actively participate in the design and development process, and provide technical leadership to the broader Guidewire delivery team. The role also includes working with business and technical teams to clarify requirements, investigate defects, and deliver reliable solutions, and it requires the ability to work in a fast-paced, high-demand, visible environment across multiple teams.

What Will You Do?

  • Perform complex analysis, advanced level design and configuration, and develop functionality within Guidewire BillingCenter for high visibility, high impact initiatives.
  • Configure, troubleshoot, and support multiple BillingCenter functional areas.
  • Take the lead on designing and implementing solutions for moderately complex, loosely scoped billing and payments problems aligned with team and business goals.
  • Serve as a Technical Lead on key initiatives, delivering efforts both independently and by leading other team members.
  • Play a key role in a large 2027 transformation program, migrating from an in-house, mainframe-based billing platform to Guidewire BillingCenter.
  • Lead investigation, diagnosis, and resolution efforts for critical, high impact problems, defects, and incidents within BillingCenter and related integrations, while working with business and technical teams to clarify requirements.
  • Act as a technology advocate, identifying opportunities to leverage Guidewire capabilities, cloud technologies, and, where applicable, AI to improve billing processes and business outcomes.
  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship on Guidewire BillingCenter and modern engineering practices while fostering a collaborative, Agile team environment.
  • Apply knowledge of Guidewire events, batch processing, and integration patterns, as well as current industry and cloud trends, to design and deliver effective solutions.
  • Seek opportunities to continuously expand your technical knowledge of Guidewire, AWS, and Agile delivery practices.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • 5+ years of hands-on programming/development experience.
  • 5+ years of experience with Guidewire BillingCenter, including configuration and integration.
  • Technical Skills & Domain Expertise
    • Deep experience with Guidewire BillingCenter configuration, integrations, and extension.
    • Hands-on experience developing and supporting integrations with Guidewire BillingCenter.
    • Experience with commission calculation configuration and troubleshooting, invoice logic and document mapping, and payment management, including configuration and issue resolution.
    • Strong knowledge of Guidewire events and batch processing.
    • Experience acting as a Technical Lead on complex initiatives, ideally in billing, payments, or policy administration domains.
    • Experience working in Agile environments (e.g., Scrum/Kanban) and using modern DevOps practices (CI/CD, automated testing).
    • Experience with AWS (or another major cloud provider), including designing, deploying, or supporting cloud-hosted applications and integrations.
    • Experience with Java and/or GOSU for Guidewire development.
    • Exposure to or hands-on experience with AI/ML capabilities and how they can be applied to billing or financial operations.
    • Prior experience with or understanding of mainframe-based systems, especially in modernization or migration to Guidewire.
  • DeliveryAdvanced delivery skills, including the ability to:
    • Determine the software design strategy and methodology for Guidewire BillingCenter efforts.
    • Use automated tests, analysis, and informed feedback loops to ensure quality and production readiness before release.
    • Monitor the health of BillingCenter components and adjacent systems, addressing issues proactively.
  • Problem SolvingStrong problem solving skills, including the ability to:
    • Use data, experimentation, and proofs of concept to find creative solutions to complex billing and integration challenges.
    • Reflect on implemented solutions, measure their impact, and use those insights to iterate and optimize.
    • Make sound decisions that involve multiple complex factors and broad business/technical implications.
  • CommunicationExcellent communication skills, including the ability to:
    • Translate Guidewire and cloud technical concepts into language that is clear and meaningful to business partners.
    • Document initiatives in a concise, clear, and structured manner.
    • Collaborate effectively with engineers, product owners, architects, and business stakeholders across multiple teams.
    • Quickly identify and articulate core issues in discussions and meetings.
    • Give and receive constructive feedback, raise issues and challenges constructively, offer support when asked, and ensure all voices are heard; listen attentively and with empathy.
  • LeadershipAdvanced leadership skills, including the ability to:
    • Take ownership and drive work forward even when there is no clearly defined owner.
    • Lead and mentor engineers in Guidewire BillingCenter and modern engineering practices.
    • Inspire, motivate, and align team members around common goals, particularly during large transformation efforts.

What is a Must Have?

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, related STEM field, or its equivalent in education and/or work experience.
  • 6 additional years of software engineering experience.

What Is the Opportunity?

As an Outside Auto Appraiser, you are responsible for physically inspecting damaged vehicles, estimating repair costs, working closely with repair facilities, and determining and settling the actual cash value of total loss vehicles to ensure accurate and timely claim settlements. In this customer-facing role, you will need to have a high level of technical expertise in vehicle damage assessment, strong customer service skills, and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment. This position will serve as a technical resource for auto claim staff and will provide advice and direction to claim professionals on claim damages to achieve optimal outcomes. This position is based remotely with work at residential and/or commercial locations with a combination of mobile work, work from your primary residence, or the nearest Travelers office.

What Will You Do?

  • Inspect and assess vehicle damage resulting from accidents, weather events, or other covered losses by conducting thorough virtual or on-site inspections at body shops or customer locations.
  • Perform estimate review work, conduct virtual inspections, and collaborate with repair facilities to ensure accuracy, consistency, and quality across claims.
  • Prepare accurate repair estimates using industry-standard estimating software to determine the cost of parts, labor, and materials required to restore vehicles to pre-loss condition.
  • Evaluate and settle vehicle total losses by determining actual cash value (ACV) through market research, comparable vehicle analysis, and application of appropriate valuation tools and methodologies.
  • Negotiate repair costs and settlements with body shops, customers, and third-party claimants to reach fair and timely resolutions while maintaining quality repair standards.
  • Identify and document pre-existing damage, prior repairs, and potential fraud indicators to ensure accurate claim evaluation and protect company interests.
  • Collaborate with claim representatives, body shops, and vendors to coordinate repairs, authorize supplements, and resolve coverage or repair-related issues.
  • Provide exceptional customer service by explaining the appraisal process, answering questions, assisting in moving claims towards timely resolution, and keeping vehicle owners informed throughout the claim lifecycle.
  • Adapt to new technology implementations, system upgrades, and digital tool rollouts, particularly in the areas of AI while maintaining productivity and service quality.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree.
  • Active adjuster license, where applicable.
  • Two years of auto physical damage appraisal experience.
  • Proficient in claims management and estimating software, with advanced skills in Microsoft Office and enterprise technology systems and platforms.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to convey information clearly and professionally.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgement and make effective decisions.
  • Exceptional customer service skills and commitment to providing a positive experience for customers throughout the claim process.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills; ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated conflict resolution skills; ability to facilitate productive discussions and reach equitable outcomes.
  • Ability to manage stress, navigate difficult situations, and maintain composure and professionalism under pressure while always taking accountability for decisions.
  • Basic understanding of insurance principles and terminology, state insurance regulations and claim handling requirements.
  • Ability to quickly learn from experience and apply it to new situations with speed and flexibility.

  • High School Diploma or GED required.
  • One year of auto physical damage appraisal or comparable claim related experience or successful completion of required Travelers Claim Representative training program.
  • Valid driver's license.

What Is the Opportunity?

As a Data Engineer I at Travelers, you'll contribute to how Business Insurance General Liability (GL) and CMP pricing decisions are powered by data. Working alongside Actuarial and Data Science partners, you'll help turn analytical ideas into trusted, production-grade assets that directly influence pricing outcomes across core insurance products.
You'll build growing domain expertise in GL and CMP while contributing to modernization efforts and evolving pricing capabilities. Through high-visibility initiatives, your work will help strengthen data reliability, model readiness, and long-term scalability across pricing platforms.
The ideal candidate is eager to grow as a data engineer, curious about the insurance domain, and energized by cross-functional collaboration. You'll be supported by experienced engineers and leaders who are invested in your development. Your contributions will help advance Travelers' pricing strategies in a dynamic and evolving insurance marketplace.

What Will You Do?

  • Build and operationalize complex data solutions, correct problems, apply transformations, and recommend data cleansing/quality solutions.
  • Design data solutions.
  • Analyze sources to determine value and recommend data to include in analytical processes.
  • Incorporate core data management competencies including data governance, data security and data quality.
  • Collaborate within and across teams to support delivery and educate end users on data products/analytic environment.
  • Perform data and system analysis, assessment and resolution for defects and incidents of moderate complexity and correct as appropriate.
  • Test data movement, transformation code, and data components.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree in STEM related field or equivalent.
  • Six years of related experience.
  • Deep, hands-on experience with modern engineering tools and practices, including:
    • Cloud platforms (preferably AWS) and model implementation in the cloud
    • Programming in Python and SQL
    • Working with data engineering concepts and building/maintaining data pipelines
    • AI-native solutions and modern software engineering practices (e.g., APIs, microservices, test automation)
  • Proven ability to deliver high-quality solutions at a steady, predictable pace:
    • Breaks work into small, releasable increments
    • Delivers complete, robust solutions while effectively managing tradeoffs
  • Demonstrated domain expertise, including:
    • Strong understanding of relevant technical concepts and industry trends
    • In-depth knowledge of the systems you've worked on and familiarity with adjacent systems
  • Strong problem-solving skills with a focus on building resilient, long-lived systems and finding innovative ways to resolve issues.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with engineers, product partners, and business stakeholders.
  • Proven experience leading or mentoring other engineers and helping to create a safe, inclusive environment where others can learn and grow.
  • Self-motivated, with a track record of proactively identifying opportunities, driving improvements, and following through on team efforts.
  • Preferred, Not Required:
    • Experience in or exposure to the insurance industry, or a strong desire to learn the domain.
    • Experience with Infrastructure as Code and DevOps tooling, such as Terraform and CI/CD pipelines.

What is a Must Have?

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, related STEM field, or its equivalent in education and/or work experience.
  • 2 additional years of software/data engineering experience.

  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

What Is the Opportunity?

As a Technical Specialist, General Liability, you will be responsible for managing and investigating moderate complexity injury and/or property damage claims including customer contact, determining coverage, evaluating liability, assessing damages, establishing timely reserves, and issue timely and accurate payments within appropriate authority and oversight. In this technical role, you will leverage your expertise in claims management, investigative techniques, coverage evaluation, and settlement negotiation to ensure timely and fair resolution. You will foster positive, professional relationships with customers and stakeholders on claims that may involve significant litigation or span extended periods. You will provide guidance and mentorship to Claim Reps and Associate Claim Reps, sharing knowledge and best practices to support their development.

What Will You Do?

  • Independently manage an active caseload of injury and/or property damage claims and litigation from first notice of loss through resolution within level of authority. Typically, handles personal and/or business insurance high complexity liability claims which may include coverage disputes and contractual indemnity issues.
  • Gather and thoroughly investigate information by contacting all relevant parties to determine coverage, evaluate liability exposure, assess bodily injury and/or property damage, and establish appropriate reserves in accordance with policy terms and management guidance.
  • Provide timely and professional communication to customers, representatives, opposing counsel, third-party vendors, and internal stakeholders.
  • Leverage resolution strategies and coordinate internal and external resources to conduct comprehensive claim investigations and evaluations.
  • Actively negotiate with multiple constituents (e.g., claimants, attorneys, contractors, representatives) and convey claim settlements within authority and issue payments timely and accurately.
  • Assist in coordinating with Counsel to support litigation management strategies.
  • Maintain accurate records of claim activity in claim management systems.
  • Identify areas in which we can improve or enhance current best practices and offer creative solutions.
  • Adapt to new technology implementations, system upgrades, and digital tool rollouts, particularly in the areas of AI while maintaining productivity and service quality.
  • Acquire and maintain relevant Insurance License(s) to comply with state and Travelers' requirements within three months of starting the job.
  • May require travel, including overnight stays, to attend mediations, trials, arbitration, etc.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree.
  • Three years of liability, bodily injury or comparable claim experience.
  • Two years of litigation claim experience.
  • Active adjuster license, where required by state law.
  • Experience with claims management systems, with advanced skills in Microsoft Office and enterprise technology systems and platforms.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to comprehend, synthesize, and clearly articulate complex information to multiple stakeholders.
  • Ability to analyze complex situations, exercise sound judgement, and make effective decisions independently.
  • Exceptional customer service skills and commitment to providing a positive experience for customers; ability to manage difficult conversations with empathy and professionalism.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills with the ability to manage a high-volume workload and prioritize effectively.
  • Proven conflict resolution and negotiation skills; ability to handle complex or disputed claims, negotiate settlements, and manage litigation.
  • Ability to manage stress, navigate difficult situations, and maintain composure and professionalism under pressure while always taking accountability for decisions.
  • Thorough understanding of insurance principles and terminology, state insurance regulations, fair claims practices, and legal requirements applicable to claim handling.
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret, apply, and clearly articulate complex policy language, endorsements, exclusions to assess coverage and claim eligibility.
  • Ability to quickly learn from experience and apply it to new situations with speed and flexibility.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • Two years of bodily injury liability, property damage liability, or comparable claim related experience.

Helping People Thrive in a Connected World
Connect with us. Bring us your best work and your brightest ideas. And we'll bring you a place where you can thrive. Learn more at jobs.assurant.com.

Our unique culture is a big reason why talented people choose Assurant. About this job

Director role leading commercial mortgage investment originations of $2 billion annually and managing a $17 billion portfolio at Lincoln Financial Group. In-office Monday-Thursday in Charlotte or Greensboro, with responsibility for underwriting, business development, and mentoring junior analysts.

Good fit if you have 7+ years in commercial real estate finance, strong Excel and PowerPoint skills, and experience with asset lending transactions and real estate valuation.

Work Arrangement:

In Office : Employees will work in a Lincoln office with a designated workspace.

The Role at a Glance

In office Monday - Thursday with flexibility to work from home on Friday

We are looking to add a Director to the Commercial Mortgage and Real Estate Investments team.


In this position, within the Loan Production Team, you will directly contribute to the annual origination of $2 billion of commercial mortgage investments. Additional responsibilities involve the ongoing management of the $17 billion commercial mortgage portfolio. The ideal candidate is looking for increased origination responsibilities and to contribute as a leader providing guidance to junior analysts.

What you'll be doing

•Lead business development through mortgage banking relationships within assigned geographic territory.
•Review and underwrite new commercial real estate loans and present analysis and investment recommendations to the Managing Director(s) and Head of Origination.
•Draft term sheets, application/commitment letters, and other transaction related documents.
•Complete due diligence including review of leases, rent rolls, third party reports, estoppels, and other business-related matters.
•Work with legal counsel to negotiate transaction documents.
•Draft investment committee memos and present for approval to the Head of Real Estate.
•Serve as business liaison throughout the loan closing process working collaboratively with appropriate internal/external stakeholders to effectuate a timely closing.
•Actively involved in training and oversight of junior team members.
•Travel independently on due diligence and business development trips.
•Support Portfolio Management through surveillance of existing loan portfolio.
•Additional investment support may include equity and credit fund investments.
•Handle special servicing requests as requested.

What we're looking for

Must- have experience:


•4 Year/Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience (4 years of experience in lieu of Bachelor's) - Minimum Required
•7+ Years' experience required in commercial real estate finance and/or commercial real estate investment and analysis that aligns with the specific responsibilities for this position.
•Experience analyzing asset lending transactions.
•Knowledge of commercial real estate principles and valuation methods.
•Knowledge of national commercial real estate markets and macro-economic trends that affect those markets.

Job.JobTitle: Senior Business Development Underwriter - Indianapolis/Northern IN
Job.JobDescription:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of this job is to establish collaborative relationships with agencies and producers to understand external marketplace and underwrites within established performance standards. This role evaluates complex business for risk acceptability; matching price to exposure, loss frequency and severity for profitability, and rating plans/modifications for renewal retention. This role exists to ensure that the Company's marketing and producer management objectives are met, through the generation and maintenance of a profitable book of business in accordance with Company goals and guidelines.

LOCATION: Candidates located in Indianapolis area or northern Indiana are preferred, as this role supports a territory covering that region.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Drives and manages a profitable and growing book of business.

  • Sells, services and maintains a producer force that can sell and control a profitable and growing book of business.

  • Monitors the production and quality of assigned producers.

  • Drives profitable sale of the Company's products including increasing sales of existing products, and the introduction and selling of new products as they are developed.

  • Develops the assigned producer group to improve the quality and quantity of the business we obtain from assigned producers.

  • Serves as the primary Company contact and representative with existing and prospective producers.

  • Keeps alert to industry changes, including WCIRB/NCCI rulings, forms, and coverage changes.

Prospects and develops new business.

  • Prospects and prequalifies new producers to determine working relationship.

  • Appoints new quality producers; sets and monitors production expectations with each Agency.

  • Maintains a thorough knowledge of the geographic territory assigned with regard to production sources, competitor activity, and economic and demographic idiosyncrasies.

  • Directs activities pertaining to industry affairs and trade show events including exhibiting, special events and lead generation follow up.

  • Manages marketing research to help identify opportunities for management, product enhancements, new distribution channels and new geographic markets with growth potential.

  • Supports strategic programs to promote new products, reposition existing products and integrate diverse corporate philosophies to support overall marketing and Underwriting efforts.

  • Utilizes high level underwriting authority to effectively price Company's products.

  • Accepts or rejects complex risks, evaluating all risk characteristics (operations, financials, management, employees, prior experience, etc.) as compared to the average in its class and prices for profit within Company Underwriting guidelines.

  • Quotes retro, deductible plans, and other more complex pricing products and has a solid understanding of their various components.

  • Conducts customer presentations explaining these plans in detail.

Delivers superior customer service through collaborative relationships.

  • Provides production support through producer visitations and by participating in underwriting and production presentations.

  • Provides personal assistance to agents and insureds through regular visits to outside locations such as producer's offices.

  • Utilizes company technology to be available to customers when needed.

  • Effectively communicates decisions and resolves agent/customer concerns promptly.

  • Presents Agency Management solutions to agency principals and ICW management team.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have direct reports but may mentor and/or train junior team members.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's degree from four-year college or university in Business, Accounting, Statistics or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

  • Minimum 5 years of related experience in underwriting required, 7 years preferred.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Current driver's license required.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Demonstrated success servicing the Company's clients and building and maintaining relationships with production sources.

  • Proven sales and effective relationship management skills.

  • Ability to apply fundamental to advanced Underwriting concepts, practices, and procedures in an area of specialization.

  • Ability to read and interpret documents such as submissions, loss control reports, and standard policy form/endorsements.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead special projects.

  • Ability to mentor and train professional and support staff.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.

  • Role requires 40-50% travel to meet with clients, attend industry events, and develop new business opportunities.

  • Travel is usually limited to automobile, but occasional air travel is required.

  • Requires regular visits to outside locations such as producer's offices.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • This remote/Indiana field position operates in a home office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

We are currently not offering employment sponsorship for this opportunity

#LI-KK1 #LI-REMOTE


The current range for this position is

$104,125.20 - $175,599.98

This range is exclusive of fringe benefits and potential bonuses. If hired at ICW Group, your final base salary compensation will be determined by factors unique to each candidate, including experience, education and the location of the role and considers employees performing substantially similar work.


WHY JOIN ICW GROUP?

  • Challenging work and the ability to make a difference
  • You will have a voice and feel a sense of belonging
  • We offer a competitive benefits package, with generous medical, dental, and vision plans as well as 401K retirement plans and company match
  • Bonus potential for all positions
  • Paid Time Off
  • Paid holidays throughout the calendar year
  • Want to continue learning? We'll support you 100%


ICW Group is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. ICW Group will not discriminate against an applicant or employee on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex/gender, age, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

___________________

Job Category

Underwriting

Job.JobTitle: Operational Risk Analyst (Group Benefits and Retirement)
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Risk Manager, Risk Management / Loss Control
Job.JobDescription:
Alternate Locations: Charlotte, NC (North Carolina); Fort Wayne, IN (Indiana); Omaha, NE (Nebraska); Radnor, PA (Pennsylvania)

Hybrid : Employee will work 3 days a week in a Lincoln office

Relocation assistance: is not available for this opportunity.

The Role at a Glance

As an Operational Risk Analyst within our Group Protection and Retirement Plan Services (RPS) organization, you will provide subject matter expertise on design and effectiveness of financial and operational controls for various vendor services. You will partner with internal and external stakeholders and auditors to ensure the control environment aligns with the service vendor audit program. You will develop and execute on more complex audit testing to evaluate the effectiveness and efficiency of operations and controls, reliability of SOC-1 reporting, and compliance with applicable law. You will also provide control expertise, risk assessment analysis, and implement risk mitigation recommendations for complex projects, processes, and major financial and operational control initiatives.

Success in this role requires a balance of technical depth, cross-functional influence, and clear communication as well as strong accountability to deliver positive outcomes. You will drive the evaluation of the control environments, coordinate closely with external auditors on SOC-1 outcomes, and shape risk assessments for senior audiences. From executing complex audit testing to driving risk mitigation across major initiatives, you'll play a key role in keeping the ORM team's control environment sound, informed, and audit ready.

What you'll be doing

  • You will serve as the business unit SOC 1 Program Owner, responsible for maintaining accurate control inventories, ensuring control ownership is appropriately documented, and leading interactions between external auditors and internal control owners and subject matter experts.
  • Serves as the liaison for the annual SOC1 & SOC2 audit work between the business and external stakeholders by working with internal partners to develop action plans as needed, updating the report for issuance, and communicating report outcomes with business partners and management.
  • You will manage report development, review, and issuance; manage report validation and distribution process; and maintain all business records.
  • You will assist internal stakeholders to strengthen the control environment by establishing complex action plans to address financial & operational control deficiencies. You will track and monitor progress against these action plans to ensure timely risk mitigation resolution.
  • You will act as the Internal Audit liaison for the business units by ensuring business engagement, responsiveness to audit requests, issue management, communication management, and management action plan execution.
  • Maintains knowledge on current and emerging developments/trends, assesses the impact, and collaborates with management to incorporate new trends and developments in current and future solutions.
  • Champions and enhances organizational initiatives by positively influencing and supporting change management and/or departmental/enterprise initiatives.
  • Serves as a resource to team members and applicable internal/external stakeholders on more complex assignments/projects.
  • Identifies and recommends process improvements that significantly reduce workloads or improve quality.
  • Maintains and maps key procedural controls to defined risk scenarios for each operational risk category and documents process flows as defined through interviews with subject matter experts.
  • Partners with appropriate internal stakeholders and management to strengthen the control environment and to address financial and operational control deficiencies.
  • Tracks and monitors progress against corrective action plans. Develops and reviews test plans to ensure mitigation strategies are consistently followed.
  • Works with management across departments to implement key initiatives to ensure the proper financial and operational controls are contemplated, initiated, executed, and maintained.
  • Carries out duties in compliance with all state and federal regulations and guidelines. Complies with all company policies and procedures.
  • Proactively liaises with internal stakeholders and management to anticipate and address internal risks before they become an issue.
  • Serves as a first alert system to keep management and other internal stakeholders aware of unanticipated problems to be addressed and/or opportunities to be considered.
  • Communicates with management on internal control activity and serves as a resource during projects & process reviews to advise on implications regarding internal controls.
  • Partners with internal stakeholders to educate and implement industry best practices on existing and new quality assurance programs, including system support.

What we're looking for

Must-haves:

  • 5-7+ years of experience with SOC-1 and/or financial/operation controls or other control environment experience within a compliance or audit team that directly aligned to the specific responsibilities of this position.
  • 4 Year/bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience (4 years of experience in lieu of Bachelor's) in Accounting, Finance, Compliance, or Risk Management

Nice- to-haves:

  • License/Designations: CPA and/or CFE
  • Direct vendor management and/or risk management experience
  • NAIC general knowledge
  • Experience creating audit or regulatory work papers
  • Ability to identify and recommend process improvements

Application Deadline

Applications for this position will be accepted through 11/20/2026, subject to earlier closure due to applicant volume

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Charlotte, NC
  • Experience: 4+ years
  • Benefits: 401(k), paid time off, tuition assistance

About this job

Senior Associate role administering and servicing commercial mortgage loan portfolios for Lincoln Financial's multi-billion-dollar portfolio. Position offers 4 days in-office in Charlotte or Greensboro with Friday remote option, requiring someone comfortable with technology, AI tools, and process improvement.

Good fit if you have 3+ years commercial loan or mortgage servicing experience, a bachelor's degree or equivalent work history, and are comfortable learning AI and automation tools.

Full job description

Alternate Locations: Charlotte, NC (North Carolina); Greensboro, NC (North Carolina)

In Office : Employees will work in a Lincoln office with a designated workspace.

Relocation assistance: is not available for this opportunity.

Requisition #: 76604

The Role at a Glance

We are looking to add a Senior Associate to our Commercial Mortgage and Real Estate Investments Team to work in the Charlotte or Greensboro office 4 days per week with an option to work remotely on Fridays. In this role, you will provide day-to-day administration and servicing of our commercial mortgage loan portfolio, working closely with relationship managers, mortgage bankers, production, closers, legal, and accounting to keep loan operations running smoothly. Beyond the core servicing work, we're looking for someone who is genuinely comfortable with technology and change — someone who can learn our current systems and processes quickly, get fluent with the AI and automation tools we use, and, once up to speed, feel empowered to point out where things could work better. As the ideal candidate, you will bring both strong servicing fundamentals and a fresh, tech-forward perspective to a well-established commercial mortgage servicing team managing a multi-billion-dollar loan portfolio.

What you'll be doing

•Administering and servicing the commercial loan portfolio, including processing payments, advances, and payoffs.
•Monitoring loan covenants, insurance, and other compliance requirements throughout the loan lifecycle.
•Maintaining and updating loan documentation and records in our loan servicing system(s).
•Managing escrow accounts and insurance/tax tracking.
•Preparing and distributing reports for management, investment accounting, and regulatory agencies.
•Coordinating with borrowers, correspondents, relationship managers, and internal teams to identify and resolve servicing issues.
•Processing requests for lender consent, loan modifications, renewals, extensions, and payoff calculations.
•Responding to borrower, correspondent and internal inquiries accurately and in a timely manner.
•Assisting with audits and regulatory examinations as needed.
•Learning and actively using AI-enabled and automation tools (e.g., document extraction, data validation, reporting assistants) as part of day-to-day servicing work.
•Identifying inefficiencies or gaps in current servicing workflows and proposing practical improvements, drawing on prior experience and available technology.
•Supporting the evaluation and rollout of new servicing tools, templates, or process changes as the team modernizes its workflows.
•Working on projects and team initiatives as requested.

What we're looking for

•4 Year/Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience (4 years of experience in lieu of Bachelor's) – Minimum Required
•3+ Years' experience in commercial loan servicing, commercial mortgage servicing, or commercial banking that aligns with the specific responsibilities for this position.
•Able to work a minimum of 40 hours per week, with a minimum of 4 days in the office.
•Working knowledge of commercial lending practices, loan documents, and applicable regulations.
•Working knowledge of escrow administration and insurance/tax tracking requirements.
•Critical thinking skills.
•Must be detail oriented.
•Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple loans and work independently in a time-sensitive environment where meeting established deadlines is critical.
•Strong interpersonal/customer service skills with the ability to create/build and maintain relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
•Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
•Working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite (Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook).
•Demonstrated adaptability — comfortable with change, new systems, and evolving processes, with a track record (or clear inclination) of suggesting process improvements once familiar with how a team operates.
•Experience with AI platforms (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, Claude, etc.) is preferred.
•Familiarity with regulatory and reporting requirements relevant to insurance company general account lending (e.g., NAIC schedules) is preferred.

The VP, Client Supply Chain Solutions leads the development, execution, and expansion of the strategic account plan for the client, with specific responsibility for identifying, positioning, and selling Assurant's supply chain capabilities as a core value driver within the broader client relationship. This senior commercial leader serves as a trusted advisor, connecting client's business priorities with Assurant solutions across supply chain, device lifecycle, logistics, reverse logistics, repair, refurbishment, fulfillment, inventory management, and operational optimization.

This role is accountable for expanding the relationship beyond existing programs by shaping growth opportunities, influencing senior client stakeholders, and translating Assurant's operational capabilities into compelling commercial solutions. The successful candidate will improve client outcomes, support profitable revenue growth, and strengthen the long-term strategic partnership.

The VP will engage senior and mid-level client leaders across business, operations, supply chain, finance, product, and executive stakeholder groups, while leading direct and matrixed teams across Assurant. This role will be based on site at our Irving, Texas location.

What will be my duties and responsibilities in this job?

  • Lead the creation and execution of the strategic account plan for the client, with a focus on expanding revenue, strengthening executive engagement, and identifying new opportunities to position Assurant supply chain capabilities.
  • Build and cultivate senior-level relationships across the client business, operations, supply chain, finance, product, and executive stakeholder groups to understand priorities, anticipate needs, and position Assurant as a strategic partner.
  • Identify, develop, and advance commercial opportunities related to device lifecycle management, logistics, reverse logistics, repair, refurbishment, fulfillment, inventory management, operational efficiency, and related value-added services.
  • Translate client business objectives and operational challenges into compelling solution opportunities, partnering with internal supply chain, operations, product, finance, legal, pricing, and implementation teams to develop client-ready proposals and business cases.
  • Lead cross-functional selling efforts for new supply chain solutions, clearly articulating client value, financial impact, service performance, scalability, and alignment with the client's strategic priorities.
  • Guide direct and matrixed teams in the development of annual business plans, client business reviews, growth roadmaps, and executive-level presentations that demonstrate performance, highlight operational value, and advance mutual revenue goals.
  • Develop, negotiate, and execute complex commercial agreements, renewals, expansions, and amendments that support Assurant growth objectives and the client's evolving supply chain and customer experience needs.
  • Partner with operational leaders to ensure sold solutions are executable, scalable, and aligned with contracted service expectations, while driving accountability for performance, service utilization, and client satisfaction.
  • Lead the prioritization and coordination of client initiatives, including supply chain capability launches, operational enhancements, product or service expansions, and implementation of new client solutions.
  • Anticipate and resolve client issues by engaging appropriate cross-functional leaders, driving operational process improvements, and ensuring supply chain performance supports the overall health and growth of the relationship.
  • Monitor account financial performance, opportunity pipeline, margin considerations, contract economics, and mutual business outcomes to ensure growth opportunities are commercially sound and strategically aligned.
  • Mentor account management leaders and cross-functional partners on strategic client engagement, executive communication, consultative selling, and positioning supply chain capabilities as part of an integrated client growth strategy.

What are the requirements needed for this position?

  • BS/BA degree; MBA preferred.
  • 15+ years of sales and/or marketing experience.
  • 15+ years of experience interacting with large, complex mobile industry clients and developing strategic relationships.
  • 7+ years of experience directly leading the work of others, including direct people leadership and supervision.
  • Demonstrated industry experience and deep knowledge of mobile supply chain, device lifecycle, logistics, reverse logistics, repair, refurbishment, fulfillment, inventory management, or related services.
  • Experience developing and executing long-term strategic plans spanning three or more years.
  • Experience managing complex commercial opportunities, account financial performance, pricing, margin considerations, contract economics, and revenue growth.

Core Capabilities

  • Deep understanding of complex deals and contracts, with advanced negotiation skills.
  • Advanced business and financial acumen, including the ability to build and evaluate compelling business cases.
  • Expert ability to cultivate strategic relationships and influence senior and C-suite leaders.
  • Advanced written and verbal communication skills, including executive presentations and commercial pitches.
  • Ability to translate client needs and operational challenges into clear, scalable, and financially viable solutions.
  • Strong organizational skills and disciplined management of multiple priorities, stakeholders, and initiatives.
  • Ability to lead cross-functional teams and collaborate effectively at all levels of the organization.
  • Strong judgment balancing client advocacy, operational feasibility, commercial value, and long-term partnership objectives.

Communication & Leadership

  • Proven ability to serve as a trusted advisor to senior client and internal stakeholders.
  • Ability to influence without authority and align direct and matrixed teams around shared priorities.
  • Confidence leading difficult conversations, resolving escalations, and presenting recommendations to executives.
  • Demonstrated ability to mentor account management leaders and elevate consultative selling and executive engagement capabilities.

Analytical & Operational Skills

  • Ability to assess account performance, opportunity pipeline, financial trends, operational data, and client feedback to identify risks and growth opportunities.
  • Ability to connect service performance and operational capabilities with measurable client and financial outcomes.
  • Proficiency with business software, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and project management tools.

About this job

Claims Operations Team Lead for AIG's Warranty division in Atlanta. Handles property and casualty insurance claims for major clients, supervises claims agents, and ensures compliance with fair claims practices and state regulations.

Good fit if you have 2+ years of P&C adjusting experience, a home state adjuster's license, and can lead a team while handling day-to-day claims work.

Full job description

Who we are

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. Building on 100 years of experience, today AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance, life insurance, retirement solutions, and other financial services to customers in more than 80 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets, manage risks and provide for retirement security.


Get to know the business

General Insurance is a leading provider of insurance products and services for commercial and personal insurance customers. It includes one of the world's most far-reaching property casualty networks. General Insurance offers a broad range of products to customers through a diversified, multichannel distribution network.


AIG Warranty delivers a full range of service solutions including warranty management administration, extended service programs, customer service support, service network management, claims processing services, and service contract underwriting.

With over 20+ years of experience, we are one of the warranty and service industry's leading providers, which is why many of the world's largest and most respected brands choose us. When retailers or manufacturers want flexible and innovative service solutions that will ensure the focus of building customer retention and customer satisfaction, they turn to us.


About the Role

Reporting to a Claims Team Manager, the Claims Operations Lead works directly with the insured, service contractors, clients, and other internal and external stakeholders to support the Warranty claims team. Senior Examiners are responsible for the handling of all Warranty Property and Casualty insurance claims for major clients in our diverse portfolio. Our portfolio consists of a diverse range of products from the home warranty, consumer electronics, and mobile industries.


What you need to know

The Claims Operations Leads are the ones our clients turn to in times of need and will act with speed, composure, compassion and knowledge to solve problems and the work they do every day is the heart of AIG's business. The successful candidate that we seek will need to meet the minimum criteria to fully support and engage in the full range of duties expected.


What we're looking for:


  • Answer incoming phone calls, emails, and other correspondence concerning insurance claims.
  • Ability to interface with the insured and other stakeholders concerning claims related matters.
  • Ask the right questions about the claim, evaluating each request to determine if AIG should approve or deny a claim.
  • Adjudicate and settle claim according to fair claims practices.
  • Be familiar with state statues concerning claims practices.
  • Train, mentor, and coach other claims agents to support the adjusting and settlement practices.
  • Audit claims files and authority use of other Agents to ensure claims best practices are being follower.
  • Maintain knowledge of industry and asset coverage types.
  • Handle research assignments and reporting as delegated by management.
  • Maintain good working relationship during all contacts with clients, even during difficult conversations.
  • Answer claims and coverage questions from other departments.
  • Take responsibility for continuously improving processes and product knowledge, understanding of program coverage and exclusions.
  • Act professionally at all times.
  • Perform additional duties and work as assigned.

Required Qualifications:

  • At minimum, the successful candidate must have their home state Adjuster's license and must be willing to complete all requirements for all states within the first 120-days of employment.
  • 2+ years of P&C adjusting experience.
  • Ability to lead and support a team while remaining hands-on with day-to-day claims.
  • A record of providing outstanding customer service (can be within a sale, retail, pharmacy, equipment repair, insurance, etc., environment)
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skill
  • Experience in conflict resolution, or the ability to de-escalate tense situations, and comfortable in a role that requires some negotiations
  • Analytical skills and the ability to search the internet for answers and market data
  • Results oriented, and able to work well under pressure
  • Excellent organizational skills- flexible with moving from project to project while keeping track of progress
  • Professionalism and demonstrate and maintain strong ethics
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Basic Excel, Word, and Outlook skills
  • Great interpersonal communication
  • Ability to consistently meet deadlines
  • High School Diploma or equivalent required

Your actual compensation will be dependent on your skills, experience, and qualifications. If your compensation expectations are above the posted range, we still encourage you to apply—your unique background matters to us. In addition, we're proud to offer a range of competitive benefits, a summary of which can be viewed here: US Benefits Overview.


Veterans are encouraged to apply.

At AIG, our people are our greatest asset. We know how important it is to protect and invest in what's most important to you. That is why we created our Total Rewards Program, a comprehensive benefits package that extends beyond time spent at work to offer benefits focused on your health, wellbeing and financial security—as well as your professional development—to bring peace of mind to you and your family.

Job.JobDescription:
Job Description

We're seeking a Project Workers Compensation Administrator!

This is an exciting opportunity to help manage complex workers' compensation programs supporting large-scale projects while partnering with project leadership, insurers, medical professionals, and legal teams to deliver positive claim outcomes and reduce organizational risk.

This is a fully onsite role, working directly with the client at their Port Arthur, TX location.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

How this opportunity is different

The Claims Administrator is responsible for implementing all aspects of the project workers' compensation program (statutory and USL&H) for Port Arthur LNG and all Contractor

Coordinated Insurance Program (CCIP) enrollees. This position will also assist with the

Administration of auto and other insured claims. Position is located at the project

construction site with an anticipated work schedule of 48 hours per week. While this is an Aon position, the employee is seconded to Bechtel. The Claims Administrator works under the direction of Bechtel's Head of Workers'

Compensation and the Aon Claims Director, acting independently to manage routine

Matters while keeping Bechtel Insured Claims team fully informed at all stages.

What the day will look like

  • Communicates effectively with injured workers, medical professionals, insurers, brokers, internal/external counsel, corporate management, and various related regulatory agencies.
  • Develops and maintains project-specific workers' compensation claims manual, medical panel, related processes and procedures for statutory and USL&H claims. Implements improvements based on lessons learned, legislative changes or Court decisions, and Bechtel operating imperatives.
  • Assists with subcontractor CCIP enrollment and provides workers' compensation orientation to subcontractors.
  • Develops and provides onsite training related to workers' compensation.
  • Under the guidance of the Workers' Compensation Risk Manager, develops and prepares regular reports outlining project claims performance. Monitors claims activity to identify early negative claim trends or other issues that may negatively impact project performance.
  • Is responsible for oversight and processing of workers' compensation claims:
  • Responsible for initiating, preparing, and maintaining all documentation associated with claims.
  • Investigates and documents eligibility for workers' compensation benefits and communicates same to insurer and related interested parties.
  • Assists with investigation and coordination of issues surrounding subrogation.
  • Interprets laws and regulations, determines appropriate courses of action, and presents solutions to resolve the claims.
  • Identifies potential subrogation issues.
  • Monitors claim resolution activities implemented by insurer(s) and employers.
  • Maintains Project Risk Management Information System (RMIS).
  • Directs and monitors the activities and performance of Bechtel's insurance provider to ensure compliance with applicable regulations.
  • Implements, monitors, and ensures compliance of “Special Account” requirements.
  • Conducts regular claim reviews, claim audits and prepares related reports.
  • Interfaces with insurer to effectively manage claims, including but not limited to authorizing claim reserve changes, authorizing insurer referral to outside counsel, and assessing and approving settlement strategies.
  • Coordinates and supports early return to work.
  • Manages relationships with onsite clinic, panel/network physicians and other medical providers, to ensure effective claims management and return to work.
  • Works with injured worker and supervision on developing and implementing return to work plan.
  • Assists in management fitness for duty and ADA accommodation issues as needed.
  • Assists Bechtel Risk Management in the defense of litigation or other complex case support. (i.e., responding to interrogatories and other discovery requests).
  • Assists with gathering information and filing auto and other insured claims. Assists with administration of auto and other insured claims as needed.
  • Performs other tasks as required by Bechtel Risk Management.

Skills and experience that will lead to success

  • 5+ years of experience in the field or in a related area or in a related area.
  • Extensive knowledge of / experience with workers' compensation and occupational rehabilitation procedures, practices and processes.
  • Extensive knowledge of claim's resolution techniques and strategies, legal principles related to claim resolution and familiarity with all phases of the litigation process.
  • Working knowledge of / experience with bodily injury and 1st and 3rd party property damage claims practices and processes.
  • Working knowledge of / experience with auto and other insured claims practices and procedures.
  • Relies on experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals.
  • Highly skilled in written and verbal communication.
  • Bilingual language proficiency (i.e., English and Spanish) is a plus.

Education: Bachelor's degree or equivalent years of industry Workers' Compensation experience.

For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances.

Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate.

Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time.

Pay Transparency Laws:

The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $60,000 to $80,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant's education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant's geographic location.

This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon's annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan.

A summary of all the benefits offered for this position:

Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon's discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Westfield Center, OH

About this job

Lead underwriting and sales strategy for a regional middle market territory at Westfield. Accountable for profitable growth, business development, underwriting execution, and portfolio management while partnering across multiple departments.

Good fit if you have experience leading underwriting and sales teams and can develop regional business strategies.

Full job description

Job Summary:
The Middle Market Underwriting and Sales Region Leader is accountable for developing and executing the underwriting and sales strategy for an assigned region to achieve profitable growth and targeted financial results. The role leads regional business development, underwriting execution, and portfolio management while partnering with Distribution, Product Management, Marketing, and Underwriting Operations to achieve territory objectives.

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as an Underwriting Specialist in our new Contract Extra division and play a key role in launching and growing this exciting new initiative within Western World. It's an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

For more than 50 years, Western World has provided wholesale distribution partners with innovative non-admitted insurance solutions. Combined with the strength and capabilities of Lexington Insurance, Western World offers a broad suite of E&S products that help agents and address complex risks ranging from Main Street businesses to sophisticated middle market accounts.


This is a unique opportunity for a highly experienced E&S casualty underwriter to help shape the future of a growing business segment while serving as a technical casualty expert and mentor to others within the organization.


How you will create an impact

  • Underwrite and manage a profitable portfolio of casualty & package business, including new and renewal submissions.
  • Analyze exposures, loss history, financial information, and underwriting data to make sound risk selection and pricing decisions.
  • Negotiate terms, conditions, pricing, and coverage structures with wholesale partners.
  • Maintain underwriting authority while ensuring compliance with company guidelines, risk appetite, and regulatory requirements.
  • Serve as the casualty subject matter expert for the division, providing guidance and technical support to less experienced underwriters.
  • Partner with leadership to drive casualty growth initiatives and execute business strategies within targeted segments and industries.
  • Help identify trends in production, retention, rate achievement, and loss performance, recommending actions to improve portfolio results.
  • Build and strengthen relationships with key agency partners through regular engagement, joint business planning, and agency visits.
  • Mentor and develop less experienced underwriters through coaching, training, and sharing of underwriting best practices.
  • Monitor marketplace conditions, competitive activity, and emerging casualty exposures to identify growth opportunities and potential risks.
  • Conduct agency visits and represent Western World at industry events and marketing functions


What you'll need to succeed


  • Minimum of 7+ years of E&S Casualty underwriting experience, including experience handling middle market and larger accounts.
  • Strong technical expertise in casualty underwriting, including General Liability, Products liability and Excess Liability. Some property experience is a plus.
  • Proven ability to evaluate complex risks and make sound underwriting decisions.
  • Proven ability to mentor less experienced underwriters
  • Strong negotiation, communication, and relationship-building skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience underwriting package business, including working knowledge of commercial property coverages and exposures.
  • Existing relationships within the wholesale brokerage community.
  • CPCU, AU, ARM, ASLI, or other relevant professional designations.
  • Experience working within delegated underwriting authority environments and the E&S marketplace.

Ready to maximize your impact? We would love to hear from you.

For positions based in New Jersey, the base salary range is $150,000-$185,000 and the position is eligible for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan. Your actual compensation will be dependent on your skills, experience, and qualifications. If your compensation expectations are above the posted range, we still encourage you to apply—your unique background matters to us. In addition, we're proud to offer a range of competitive benefits, a summary of which can be viewed here: US Benefits Overview.

Job.JobDescription:
AIG is reimagining the way we help customers manage risk. Join us as a Analyst in the Actuarial department to play your part in that transformation with opportunities to learn and grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

About Us (already included in Workday job description template)

At AIG, helping organizations and people discover new potential is our purpose. As a global risk leader, we do this for our clients every day. Through our deep expertise in their industries and our innovative solutions that help them smartly manage risk, we enable their growth in ways they never thought possible.

But we also do the same thing for our colleagues, because we know our people are our greatest strength – the source of every insight, every idea and every innovation. When we're working as one team to do what's right for our colleagues and our communities, we can achieve excellence together. We encourage colleagues to give back to the causes they care most about, supporting these efforts through our Volunteer Time Off and Matching Grants Programs.

Make your mark in Actuarial

Our Actuaries are on the front lines, quantifying risk, pricing insurance and reserving losses for AIG's major insurance operating companies, globally. We collaborate with Finance, Claims, Operations, Marketing and Risk Management, among other functions. As an AIG actuary, you will be challenged and encouraged to reach your greatest potential to help improve how we predict, manage and mitigate risk.

How you will make an impact

When you join AIG, you will be part of a connected cohort community of early career talent participating in a program that equips you with learning experiences and skills needed to launch your career. From day one, you will develop your knowledge and understanding of AIG and the insurance industry and learn new skills through meaningful on-the-job experiences and instructor-led masterclasses. Through exposure to senior leaders, mentoring circles, networking and volunteering, you will build connections with colleagues across the organization. Collectively, these different experiences are designed to enable you to make an impact and build a rewarding and successful career. 

 

Actuarial Development Program Overview  

Actuarial Development Program: The Program encourages and supports the education and training of Actuarial Students pursuing actuarial examinations in the knowledge and professional skills relating to actuarial practices and to develop future leaders for AIG.  Benefits of the program include: 

  • Dedicated study time – Up to 30 hours of company-provided study time per exam hour for each first attempt at a given exam 
  • Exam-related expenses, including study material 
  • Compensation  
  • Association Meetings for Conferral of Designation 
  • Professional Actuarial Association Membership Dues 
  • Continuing Education 
  • Rotations (following the actuarial program) – We are excited to provide a variety of professional opportunities for Actuarial Students to develop an advanced and well-rounded actuarial skillset following their 2 years with us in the Actuarial Development Program. Actuarial Students will gain valuable work experience through exposure to multiple rotations. Upon completion of the Actuarial Development Program and further rotations, the newly credentialed actuaries will have gained a variety of relevant work experiences enabling them to have a broader organizational perspective 

Responsibilities

  • Analyze data and apply actuarial techniques to help quantify risk, price insurance products, and support loss reserving.
  • Assist with actuarial analyses, models, forecasts, and reports that support business and financial decisions.
  • Partner with experienced actuaries and teams across Finance, Claims, Operations, Risk Management, and other business areas.
  • Monitor trends and evaluate financial and insurance data to identify insights and support recommendations.
  • Communicate actuarial findings and analyses clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Develop technical and business expertise while progressing through AIG's Actuarial Development Program and actuarial examinations.

Minimum Qualifications

Our Early Careers programs are designed for students and recent graduates who are beginning their professional careers, generally within one year of completing their degree.

Education Requirements

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree to be received no later than June 2027 (unofficial transcript required upon application).

Program Requirements

  • Available to start the Program on July 26, 2027.
  • Analyst positions are in-person opportunities, requiring employees to work in the office at least four days per week.

Core Qualifications

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively in a professional environment.
  • Demonstrated analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills, with strong attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively, manage multiple priorities, and adapt in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Preferred Majors include Actuarial Science, Mathematics, or Statistics
  • Completion of, or demonstrated progress toward, actuarial examinations is preferred.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel; exposure to analytical or programming tools such as Python, R, SQL, or similar technologies is a plus.
  • Demonstrated interest in pursuing an actuarial career and progressing toward professional actuarial credentials.
  • Demonstrated outstanding academic and extracurricular achievement.
  • Excelled in previous work experience

Application Deadline

Applications will be accepted through October 31, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and we encourage candidates to apply early. We reserve the right to close this posting prior to the application deadline based on application volume.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $120,000 to $150,000 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Philadelphia, PA
  • Experience: 5+ years

About this job

Associate Actuary role supporting North America Property pricing at AIG. Responsibilities include developing pricing strategies, improving pricing systems, coordinating with catastrophe modeling and reserving teams, and providing analytical recommendations to senior management.

Good fit if you have ACAS and 5+ years commercial lines actuarial experience, preferably in property pricing, with strong communication skills.

Full job description

Associate Actuary - North America Property Pricing

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Associate Actuary - North America Property Pricing to take on key responsibilities within a world-class actuarial function.


Make your mark in Actuarial

Our Actuaries are on the front lines, quantifying risk, pricing insurance and reserving losses for AIG's major insurance operating companies, globally. We collaborate with Finance, Claims, Operations, Marketing and Risk Management, among other functions. As an AIG actuary, you will be challenged and encouraged to reach your greatest potential to help improve how we predict, manage and mitigate risk.


How you will create an impact
We are seeking an actuarial professional to support North America Property, including Retail, Lexington, and Canada. The individual will work to streamline processes across the different Property segments. They will also partner with other pricing actuaries in implementing best practices analytical techniques, catastrophe modelers to incorporate results into pricing and quantify portfolio risk, and reserving actuaries in assessing the impact of loss trends and claims emergence.


  • Work closely with the Chief Underwriting Office to develop pricing and underwriting strategies and identify pockets of opportunity for profitable growth as well as profitability-challenged areas.
  • Review the parameters in the pricing systems, actively work to improve the pricing systems, and monitor underwriter adherence to pricing procedures and methodologies
  • Coordinate pricing, planning, and accumulation management efforts with cat modeling team to ensure adequate risk-adjusted returns contemplating expected loss, reinsurance costs, and increased capital needs associated with cat-prone business
  • Develop analytical tools to help underwriters assess the risks posed by insureds, aligning the pricing framework across the different underwriting platforms and business classes written in Lexington's property operations.
  • Work closely with reserving actuaries to understand sources of reserve development and ensure appropriate recognition of pricing and underwriting actions impacting those estimates.
  • Provide recommendations on rating methodologies, parameters and tools to improve accuracy of technical pricing reflecting latest market and economic conditions and product offerings.
  • Ensure alignment of tools, reporting metrics and goals with other property teams organizationally to optimize team efficiency while maximizing value and consistency across the property portfolios

What we are looking for

  • At least an Associate of the Casualty Actuarial Society (ACAS)
  • At least 5 years of commercial lines actuarial experience, preferably with significant commercial property pricing experience.
  • Exceptional communication skills, including ability to develop and present clear and concise analysis and recommendations to senior management.
  • Willing and able to continuously learn and adapt in a dynamic and fast changing environment.
  • Solid understanding of catastrophe modeling fundamentals
  • Timeliness and attention to detail.
