About this job

AIG seeks a Category Manager for Travel, Meetings & Events to develop sourcing strategies across corporate travel, hotels, airlines, ground transportation, and event services. The role involves negotiating supplier agreements, analyzing spend data, and partnering with stakeholders to optimize costs while maintaining service quality.

Good fit if you have 5+ years in strategic sourcing or category management, preferably in travel, meetings, events or hospitality, and can work 4 days per week in Atlanta.

Full job description

We are seeking an experienced Sourcing Category Manager – Travel, Meetings & Events to join our Global Sourcing & Procurement organization. This role will support the Travel, Meetings & Events category, partnering with business stakeholders and suppliers to deliver competitive commercial outcomes, service excellence, supplier performance, innovation, and risk mitigation.

The ideal candidate will bring strong strategic sourcing and category management experience, preferably within corporate travel, meetings and events, hospitality, or related indirect services. This individual will be comfortable navigating a diverse supplier landscape that may include travel management companies, airlines, hotels, car rental and ground transportation providers, meetings and events agencies, venue sourcing partners, and travel and event technology providers.

Success in this role requires strong commercial and analytical skills, excellent stakeholder management capabilities, and the ability to balance cost optimization with service quality, traveler and attendee experience, operational requirements, and business needs.

This role requires 4 days per week in our Atlanta office.


Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute category strategies across Travel, Meetings & Events, with a focus on cost optimization, service quality, supplier performance, innovation, risk management, and overall business value.
  • Lead strategic initiatives across areas such as corporate travel, travel management services, air, hotel, car rental, ground transportation, meetings and events services, venue sourcing, and travel and event technology.
  • Negotiate meetings and events services, including event management, venue sourcing, hotel and meeting-related agreements, event technology, and other supporting services.
  • Analyze category spend, supplier performance, market intelligence, and business requirements to identify opportunities for cost savings, cost avoidance, demand management, supplier optimization, process improvement, and innovation.
  • Monitor Travel, Meetings & Events market dynamics and emerging trends, including changes in air and hotel pricing, supplier capacity, technology, distribution models, and business travel and meetings trends, and translate those insights into sourcing strategies. Identify opportunities to improve the overall economics and effectiveness of the Travel, Meetings & Events program.
  • Partner with Travel, Meetings & Events program leadership, Finance, Legal, business stakeholders, regional teams, and other cross-functional partners to understand requirements and develop solutions aligned with business objectives.
  • Develop and maintain strategic supplier relationships and establish effective supplier governance through business reviews, KPI and SLA management, issue resolution, performance improvement, and innovation discussions.
  • Support both global and regional initiatives, taking into consideration differences in local markets, supplier capabilities, business requirements, and regulatory environments.
  • Partner with stakeholders to support adoption of preferred suppliers and maximize value from negotiated programs and agreements.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, category management, procurement, or a related discipline within a complex corporate environment.
  • Experience sourcing Travel, Meetings & Events, hospitality, or closely related indirect service categories strongly preferred.
  • Understanding of the corporate Travel, Meetings & Events supplier ecosystem, which may include travel management companies, airlines, hotels, car rental and ground transportation providers, meeting and event management companies, venue sourcing partners, and travel/event technology providers.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and executing sourcing strategies that deliver measurable cost savings, cost avoidance, service improvements, supplier innovation, and risk mitigation.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with experience leveraging spend data, supplier data, benchmarking, market intelligence, and commercial analysis to inform sourcing decisions.
  • Ability to balance commercial objectives with service quality, operational requirements, and traveler and attendee experience.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to build relationships, influence decisions, and collaborate effectively with stakeholders across functions and geographies.
  • Strong supplier relationship management capabilities, including experience with KPIs, SLAs, supplier business reviews, performance management, and continuous improvement.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, presentation, negotiation, and interpersonal skills.
  • Proficiency with sourcing, procurement, contract management, spend analytics, and related technology platforms.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Chicago, IL

About this job

Summer internship in forensic accounting applying accounting principles and financial analysis to evaluate complex commercial insurance losses. Includes mentoring, masterclasses, and networking with senior leaders across AIG's Claims organization.

Good fit if you are pursuing a Master's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field, graduating by May 2027, and can work in-person four days per week starting July 26, 2027.

Full job description

AIG is reimagining the way we help customers manage risk. Join us as a Summer Intern in the Forensic Accounting department to play your part in that transformation with opportunities to learn and grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

About Us

At AIG, helping organizations and people discover new potential is our purpose. As a global risk leader, we do this for our clients every day. Through our deep expertise in their industries and our innovative solutions that help them smartly manage risk, we enable their growth in ways they never thought possible.

But we also do the same thing for our colleagues, because we know our people are our greatest strength – the source of every insight, every idea and every innovation. When we're working as one team to do what's right for our colleagues and our communities, we can achieve excellence together. We encourage colleagues to give back to the causes they care most about, supporting these efforts through our Volunteer Time Off and Matching Grants Programs.

Make your mark in Forensic Accounting

AIG's Forensic Accounting Unit within Claims applies accounting and financial analysis to help evaluate and quantify complex commercial insurance losses. The team works across a variety of businesses and claims, using financial data, accounting principles, and investigative techniques to support accurate loss measurement and informed claims decisions.


As a Forensic Analyst, you will work alongside experienced forensic accountants, claims professionals, and other subject matter experts to analyze financial information, evaluate business losses, and contribute to the resolution of complex claims. This role offers the opportunity to build expertise in forensic accounting, commercial insurance, and financial analysis while developing a strong foundation within AIG's Claims organization.

How you will make an impact

When you join AIG, you will be part of a connected cohort community of early career talent participating in a program that equips you with learning experiences and skills needed to launch your career. From day one, you will develop your knowledge and understanding of AIG and the insurance industry and learn new skills through meaningful on-the-job experiences and instructor-led masterclasses. Through exposure to senior leaders, mentoring circles, networking and volunteering, you will build connections with colleagues across the organization. Collectively, these different experiences are designed to enable you to make an impact and build a rewarding and successful career.

Responsibilities

  • Apply accounting principles and analytical techniques to collect, interpret, and analyze financial and business data related to commercial insurance claims.

About this job

Senior Product Manager leading strategic direction for commercial lines insurance products across distribution channels and brands. Drives product strategy, roadmap, and lifecycle management while monitoring performance against revenue and profit targets.

Good fit if you have product management experience in insurance, strong analytical skills, and can collaborate across underwriting, actuarial, marketing, and compliance functions.

Full job description

Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of the position is to partner with key stakeholders to drive the strategic direction for a portfolio of insurance product line(s) across all distribution channels and brands. This position helps define product strategy and roadmap and champions the strategy and monitors product progression throughout the full life cycle. The position is responsible for monitoring and influencing all aspects of product performance to achieve Company revenue and performance targets.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Ideates and develops business initiatives using product knowledge and results.

  • Leads and participates in collaborations with the head of product line underwriting unit(s) to develop product strategy and action plan to achieve growth and profit objectives.
  • Owns inputs to bi-annual premium and exposure projections supporting financial budgeting and pro-forma processes and understand projection framework.
  • Provides expert insights regarding profitability, retention, and growth strategies through the integration of the underwriting, marketing, policyholder services, distribution, claims, actuarial, data analytics, customer, and digital experience.
  • Collaborates with other functional departments to coordinate timelines for delivery, maximize the effectiveness of programs, direct implementation of product strategies, and drive cross-functional alignment and engagement for initiatives supporting product objectives.
  • Develops and maintains templates to perform competitive research and deliver competitive analyses.
  • Utilizes and trains others in the use of internal analytical tools (spanning underwriting, marketing, customer behavior, and claims).
  • Performs and reviews data analyses concerning loss patterns, market forces, risk distributions, and agency management to evaluate the success of current strategies to either modify or create new strategies targeting production, product pricing, underwriting, contract changes, or agency changes.
  • Assesses the impact of changes on the in-force book, new business production, and agency force.

Develops and drives initiatives for strategic product development.

  • Applies business content knowledge in identifying priorities and executing strategic product initiatives to achieve business objectives.
  • Monitors the marketplace to identify competitor and industry changes impacting effectiveness or compliance of current and proposed programs.
  • Partners with Actuarial team to determine and implement appropriate pricing and program structure to achieve product goals, and design and execute product rate plan and state level enhancements across jurisdictions ensuring all changes are communicated to field services, operations, underwriting, marketing, and system technology teams.
  • Partners with Underwriting team to facilitate changes to processes or systems, or respond to questions, and ensuring communication to affected parties.
  • Analyzes the performance of existing products; develops and leads the creation of business cases for the development of changes to existing products or development of new products.
  • Maintains knowledge of available internal and external data sources, including accuracy and completeness, to select the proper data set(s) for evaluation.
  • Organizes and structures product definitions to ensure efficiencies in downstream reporting processes.
  • Directs the implementation of underwriting guideline changes.
  • Collaborates with strategic planning groups to incorporate enterprise class system solutions supporting the future product roadmap.

Acts as product leader and subject matter expert in the maintenance of current products, filed product changes, and design and delivery of new products in development.

  • Develops internal partnerships and collaborates with Enterprise Marketing, Legal, Compliance, Underwriting, and Actuarial Departments to manage the implementation of all ratemaking bureau rules, forms and coverage changes, and company-initiated changes including coordination with the rate filing analyst.
  • Keeps abreast of distribution channel needs through involvement in agency facing initiatives, and regular reporting on direct to market strategies available in the industry.
  • Possesses expert knowledge of ratemaking bureau underwriting manuals and company exception rules and maintains knowledge of any changes. Documents and memorializes changes.
  • Researches issues or concerns around underwriting rules, including historical company filings in independent ratemaking bureaus to confirm adherence and direct changes.
  • Maintains knowledge of rules, regulations, nuances in states of operation and engage with product line underwriting unit(s) to invoke needed changes or identify training in support of a self-sustaining culture.
  • Proactively engages with Underwriting and Legal to ensure insurance policy provisions comply with state law.
  • Partners with Compliance Department to identify and close any gaps in rules, respond to changes in rules, and remediate across systems, processes, reporting.
  • Participates in regulatory approval of filings, market conduct exams, and internal responses to any state filing objections to facilitate modifications.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position has no supervisory responsibilities but may mentor and train junior team members.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's degree from a college or university required with a major or emphasis in Business, Computer Science, Math, or related field or equivalent combination of education and experience. MBA is a plus.
  • Minimum 6 years of experience in insurance product management. Insurance industry knowledge and demonstrated work experience required.
  • Exposure to industry recognized product management curriculum, or demonstrated experience required.
  • Experience managing complex, large-scale, high risk product development projects preferred.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Extensive knowledge of insurance industry; workers compensation or commercial lines required based on role designation.
  • Resourcefulness to research industry topics and develop proficient knowledge of internal systems and constraints to aid in managing individual state compliance.
  • Knowledge of actuarial practice area is a plus.
  • Highly developed quantitative analysis, decision making, and project management skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to solve complex business problems, consistent with a deep understanding of the strategic direction of the business.
  • Deep knowledge of the insurance product lifecycle, financial drivers of profitability, insurance regulations and general insurance operations and business processes.
  • Ability to synthesize analytical results to guide business decisions. Strong leadership, written and oral communication, and teamwork skills required. Strong organizational skills.
  • Ability to hold effective meetings, including setting agendas and attendees, time management, and documentation of meeting outcomes.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Chartered Property Casualty Underwriter (CPCU) preferred.


PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit or periodically stand and work on a computer for 80-90% of time. The employee is occasionally required to reach with hands and arms and climb or balance. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 5 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.


WORK ENVIRONMENT

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

The purpose of the Product Business Support Specialist is to partner cross functionally in the execution of insurance product design, implementation, and project management. This role will facilitate effective planning and execution of product business solutions that align to overall department and company strategy. This role will serve as a liaison between business and technology subject matter experts to coordinate and implement projects and solutions to meet business needs.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Provides project management for product business solutions, from end-to-end, to ensure that project objectives are met.

Coordinates Product and Actuarial user acceptance testing (UAT) and user access to appropriate environments.

  • Coordinates test case documentation with UW and Product and logs test case results.

  • Provides support for UAT and test defect resolution. Coordinates and documents test cases and results to ensure accurate and timely reporting and re-testing of issues.

Supports implementation of product business solutions and provides post-implementation support of deployed business solutions.

  • Participates in coordinating the deployment and implementation of business solutions for product changes as they relate to rates, rules, and forms.

  • Assigns, documents, and tracks business issues as they evolve through the entire implementation life cycle, ensuring resolution. Escalates delays and roadblocks and works with SMEs to ensure system implementation and business processes are aligned on effective dates and filed and approved for rates, rules, and forms.

This role does not have supervisory responsibilities.

  • Expertise in project management techniques is foundational.

  • Strong analytical skills, ability to create compelling business cases; Team-oriented focus; ability to conduct effective meetings with business and project teams; ability to create and interpret business user needs into specifications.
  • Understanding of the insurance product implementation lifecycles and experience in writing business requirements and business test specifications.
  • Working knowledge of Jira, Confluence and Visio preferred.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

As Domicile Leader for Phoenix, you will be responsible for the day-to-day leadership and continued development of Aon's captive management operation in Arizona.

Working closely with colleagues across Captive & Insurance Management, you will help ensure we continue to deliver a high-quality service to our clients, develop our people and identify opportunities to grow the business.

Make your mark in Underwriting

How you will create an impact


This role underwrites Financial Lines products under general supervision, issuing quotes and policies while ensuring standards and compliance guidelines are met. These individuals will analyze information and have the opportunity to connect with clients and brokers.


Responsibilities include:

  • Evaluating, prioritizing and selecting submissions to be underwritten.

  • Analyzing claims and quantifying losses.
  • Adhering to guidelines and underwriting discipline to minimize exposure and appropriately price risks.
  • Ensuring underwriting files and services standards and compliance guidelines are adhered to on assigned accounts.

  • Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university.

  • Excellent interpersonal, communication and analytical skills.

Enterprise IAM Architect, Global

Location: can be based in one of our AIG offices in London (UK), Dublin (Ireland), Reston, VA (USA), or Charlotte, NC (USA)

Make your mark in Information Technology

At AIG, technology is at the heart of everything we do, from underwriting risks to processing claims. The Information Security Office (ISO) works closely with the Information Technology (IT) team equipping our colleagues with the latest tools to complete their work efficiently, with the highest standards of excellence. The team is responsible for shielding the company's systems from security risks, while designing technology strategies that enable AIG's businesses to achieve their goals. Innovation in IT drives innovation across the organization.

How you will create an impact

The Enterprise IAM Architect is accountable for defining and governing the enterprise Identity and Access Management (IAM) target state and shaping the transformation portfolio required to achieve it. This role sits within the Information Security Office (ISO), within the Enterprise Security Architecture function, focusing on process design, risk reduction, control effectiveness, and measurable business value.

AIG currently operates an identity ecosystem that includes (as representative examples) technologies such as Microsoft Entra ID, hybrid Active Directory, Okta (Workforce and Customer Identity), SailPoint IdentityIQ (IIQ), Microsoft Intune, Windows Hello for Business, and HYPR. These are examples of the current operating environment; however, the role is not product-bound and is expected to remain outcome- and value-led.

Delivery & Engagement Model

IAM delivery execution is managed through the ISO Program Management Office (PMO) in partnership with the relevant engineering, operational teams (e.g. IAM, security, infrastructure, and applications) and the business. This role shapes and governs delivery by defining architectural intent, control outcomes, sequencing, and design governance—ensuring initiatives remain aligned to roadmap objectives and value/risk outcomes.

The Global, Enterprise IAM Architect will focus on group managed entities (e.g. US, EMEA and UK) and will support and guide the non-group managed entities (e.g. Israel, China).

Strategic Accountability

You will be accountable for:

  • Defining and maintaining the workforce IAM and customer IAM (CIAM) strategy and target-state architecture

  • Developing and governing multi-year roadmaps, including transition states and sequencing

  • Working with other domain leads and architects to define IAM-related projects and transformation initiatives

  • Translating capability gaps and risk exposure into structured, fundable initiatives aligned to enterprise priorities

  • Establishing outcome measures and architectural guardrails to ensure initiatives deliver measurable risk and control improvements

  • Providing architectural governance and approval for identity-related initiatives, including standards, patterns, design reviews, and exception management

  • Ensuring alignment with wider enterprise security architecture direction, risk appetite, and regulatory obligations

Owned Accountability

In collaboration with other domain leads, architects, delivery stakeholders, operations, engineering and the ISO PMO, you own the development of identity-related project and program charters, including:

  • Strategic rationale and business justification

  • Risk reduction objectives and control outcomes

  • Scope boundaries, assumptions, and architectural intent

  • Success metrics and measurable value realization

  • Dependencies, sequencing, and transition planning

  • Alignment to enterprise portfolio/funding governance processes

  • You will ensure initiatives are well-framed, justifiable, architecturally coherent, and outcome-based before entering execution.

Core Responsibilities

  • Identity & Access Architecture & Control Design

    • Define the workforce IAM and CIAM target state architectures, controls, standards, principles, and design patterns

    • Develop identity response strategies for emerging technologies, including IAM implications for Agentic AI and autonomous systems (e.g. non-human identities)

  • Authentication & Endpoint-Integrated Identity

    • Define and steer phishing-resistant and passwordless strategy (e.g., FIDO2/WebAuthn, device-bound authentication, platform authenticators)

    • Define endpoint-integrated trust models in partnership with endpoint/EUC teams (e.g., Intune device posture, compliant device enforcement, conditional access integration)

  • Technology Optimization, Value Realization & ROSI

    • As part of ongoing architecture governance, continuously evaluate and re-evaluate identity technologies and investments to maximise Return on Security Investment (ROSI), drive cost efficiency, identify optimisation opportunities, and ensure spend is aligned to measurable risk and control outcomes

    • Ensure business cases and charters quantify expected value (risk reduction, incident reduction, operational efficiencies, productivity improvements, audit outcomes)

  • IAM Sourcing & Operating Model

    • Play an active role in defining and shaping the IAM sourcing approach and operating model

    • Define architecture-led evaluation criteria and control outcomes to support build/buy/partner decisions

    • Define and validate service boundaries, accountabilities (RACI), and governance forums

    • Shape system integrator and managed service engagement models (where applicable) to ensure quality, control effectiveness, auditability, and sustainable run-state operations

  • Governance & Partner Oversight

    • Provide architectural oversight of system integration partners and consultancies, validating deliverables and ensuring alignment to enterprise standards and target-state intent

    • Ensure alignment to enterprise security architecture frameworks (e.g., SABSA, TOGAF) and industry frameworks (e.g., NIST, ISO/IEC), producing audit-defensible designs

Required Experience and Qualifications

  • in depth experience in cybersecurity and/or identity architecture (IAM/CIAM), including enterprise-scale transformation

  • Proven experience defining enterprise IAM/CIAM strategy, target-state architecture, and roadmaps

  • Demonstrable experience shaping initiatives and developing project/program charters for portfolio governance and funding

  • Experience working effectively with PMO/program governance functions

  • Experience working with system integrators and consultancies, including architectural oversight and design authority engagement

  • Strong knowledge of workforce and/or customer identity platforms and controls—examples include Entra ID, hybrid AD, Intune, Windows Hello for Business, Okta, SailPoint IIQ, HYPR (or equivalent)

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Senior Complex Director to play your part in that transformation. It's an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

Make your mark in Excess Casualty Claims

Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair and professional service with empathy and efficiency.

How you will create an impact

Are you interested in handling some of the largest and most complex Casualty claims in the industry? Your deep technical claims expertise will be put to the test in the investigation, evaluation and disposition of new and existing 3rd party property and casualty claims. These multimillion-dollar claims include multi-vehicle auto accidents, plant explosions, catastrophic product liability claims and other complex losses. You will be required to review coverage under Excess Commercial General liability and auto policies and participate in the investigation of the claim. You will direct the litigation, attend mediations and trials, assess liability and damages, and recommend reserves. It will be necessary to present the large value cases to senior management. You will need excellent customer service skills in communicating with insureds, brokers, attorneys, and claimants. Only the most highly skilled negotiators will succeed in resolving these claims in the toughest venues against the most elite plaintiff attorneys.

  • Determining the scope and extent of available coverage.

  • The investigation, evaluation and disposition of new and existing 3rd party property and casualty claims.

  • Preparation and execution of investigation strategies which identify critical issues effecting liability, causation and damages and assess risk transfer and contribution opportunities.

  • Clear and concise communication and contact with internal and external customers, including insureds, brokers and underwriters, to provide guidance and manage expectations.

  • Proper documentation of exposure evaluation and resolution strategy.

  • Presentation to senior management of claim disposition recommendations.

  • Obtain the appropriate authority to independently negotiate multimillion-dollar claims with the top plaintiff attorneys nationwide. Document evaluation, thought process, and strategy. Utilize ADR as appropriate and necessary.

What you will need to succeed

  • 8+ years of Commercial/Industry claims experience preferred.

  • Excellent communication ability (verbal/written) and strong negotiation skills.

  • JD helpful but not required.

  • Property and Casualty adjusting licenses required and must be obtained within 6 months.

  • Interest in the potential for an upwardly mobile career path.

​Ready to take your career to the next level? We would love to hear from you.

About this job

Chief Financial Officer overseeing financial operations for two Berkley insurance operating units. Leads accounting, financial reporting, strategic planning, and manages a team of three while partnering with senior leadership on cost optimization and financial strategy.

Full job description

Company Details

Berkley Mid-Atlantic Group (BMAG) is a property and casualty insurance provider serving the Mid-Atlantic. We are a member of W. R. Berkley Corporation, one of the largest commercial lines property and casualty insurance holding companies in the United States. With the resources of a large Fortune 500® corporation and the ability to operate with the closeness and flexibility of a small company, we exclusively work with select independent agents to insure the future of business.

Our culture is one that empowers employees to question the status quo and seek innovative ways to continue to exceed the expectations of our customers. We practice collaboration, creativity, and teamwork on a daily basis, with a commitment to innovation and high performance.

The company is an equal opportunity employer.

Responsibilities

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) serves as a vital member of the Senior Leadership team, overseeing all financial activities for two Berkley Operating Units- Berkley Mid Atlantic and Berkley Fire and Marine. This role is responsible for planning, implementing, managing, and directing functions such as accounting, financial reporting, information analysis, expense control, annual statements, and financial planning/forecasting. The CFO develops and enforces financial and accounting controls to ensure compliance with internal and external standards and plays a key role in strategic business planning to support the financial success of each operating unit.

Key Functions/Duties of Position: Describe the overall job responsibilities (including any decision-making authority) for this position.

  • Serve as a strategic finance/operations leader and active member of the Senior Leadership team.
  • Partner with the President to accelerate execution, optimize outcomes and reduce costs.
  • Provide executive management with advice and analysis on the financial implications of business activities.
  • Provides leadership in the development and continuous evaluation of short and long-term strategic financial objectives.
  • Directs the development and implementation of cost-effective financial reporting and accounting activities.
  • Formulates effective financial oversight and internal accounting standards that comply with company and regulatory requirements.
  • Contributes to the achievement of business objectives through the accurate and timely identification and resolution of accounting issues/opportunities.
  • Directs the monthly reporting process and delivers accurate/timely monthly reports through effective utilization of all management information tools to optimize revenue and minimize financial exposure.
  • Manage and direct the expense and general ledger process.
  • Monitors financial transactions to ensure that expenses are in line with company expenses and profit objectives and are consistent with company policies.
  • Drives innovation, including taking advantage of automation opportunities and new ways to streamline and make processes more efficient.
  • Development of direct and indirect reports in both behavioral and job skills is crucial and a key component of the position. This includes regular career aspiration discussions.
  • Responds to all activities related to corporate accounting/reporting requirements.
  • Ensures that effective internal controls are in place and ensures compliance with GAAP and applicable federal, state, and local regulatory laws and rules for financial and tax reporting. Provides high-level analysis and recommendations for corrective action as necessary.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years in progressively responsible financial leadership roles
  • Property & Casualty Insurance experience required, including experience in Statutory and GAAP insurance reporting.
  • PC proficiency is essential (Windows environment) and a strong working knowledge of all financial systems, preferably Oracle and Peoplesoft, and Excel is preferred.
  • Financial reporting and planning experience; expense management skills; expert financial analysis, reporting and accounting skills necessary to meet established and stretch business goals.
  • Familiarity with direct and agency billing
  • Able to recognize and act on reporting/accounting issues and problems.

  • A proven leader who drives engagement and enables their employees. Will manage 3 direct reports.
  • Solid understanding of business objectives to drive bottom-line results; acts in a decisive manner to achieve appropriate results.
  • Strong strategic thinker and decision-maker; and consistently sets clear direction by defining goals and priorities; develops trust through demonstrated personal integrity.
  • Establishes and maintains an environment that encourages everyone to act in the best interest of the company.
  • Demonstrates strong written and oral communications skills.
  • Ability to draft communications that are clear, concise, complete, and professional.
  • Ability to interact with all levels of the organization and demonstrate organizational skills while working on multiple projects.
  • Ability to travel as needed in the performance of duties.

Job Summary

The Cloud Security Architect serves as the cloud security subject matter expert within the Senior Solution Architect role. This position works directly with cloud platform, application, infrastructure, data, and cybersecurity teams to design secure solutions across AWS, Azure, GCP, SaaS, and hybrid environments.

The role translates business, technical, risk, and regulatory requirements into implementable cloud security designs. Key areas of focus include Zero Trust architecture, cloud identity and access, workload protection, network security, data protection, security observability, and the secure adoption of artificial intelligence.

Essential Tasks & Leadership Philosophy

  • Design security architectures for cloud-hosted applications, platforms, data services, and infrastructure across AWS, Azure, GCP, SaaS, and hybrid environments.
  • Apply Zero Trust principles to solution designs, including identity-centric access, least privilege, workload segmentation, continuous verification, data protection, and security telemetry.
  • Provide hands-on security architecture support throughout solution design and delivery, including design reviews, threat modeling, risk analysis, control selection, and remediation guidance.
  • Design secure architectures for generative AI, machine learning, AI agents, and other AI-enabled solutions, with particular attention to identity, authorization, enterprise data access, secrets, model integration, agent actions, monitoring, and human oversight.
  • Work with platform and engineering teams to integrate security controls into cloud services, infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD pipelines, APIs, and application delivery processes.
  • Evaluate proposed technologies and designs, document security risks and trade-offs, and recommend practical solutions that balance security, delivery objectives, operational supportability, and cost.
  • Support the development and implementation of AI-enabled cybersecurity capabilities, including opportunities to improve security analysis, control validation, vulnerability prioritization, threat detection, and risk reporting.
  • Provide technical guidance and mentoring to architects and engineers on cloud security, Zero Trust, and secure AI design practices.

First Year Success Factors

Within the first year, the Cloud Security Architect will:

  • Establish effective working relationships with cloud platform, application, infrastructure, data, AI, and cybersecurity teams and become a trusted security architecture partner for priority initiatives.
  • Lead the security architecture and design of assigned cloud and AI solutions, providing clear requirements, documented design decisions, actionable risk guidance, and timely support through implementation.
  • Develop or improve a focused set of reusable solution designs for recurring cloud security needs, such as cloud identity, workload access, network segmentation, secrets management, data protection, logging, and security monitoring.
  • Apply Zero Trust principles to priority solution designs and demonstrate how identity, least privilege, segmentation, data protection, and continuous monitoring reduce risk within those solutions.
  • Support priority enterprise AI initiatives by defining and applying practical security controls for AI identities, enterprise data access, model and application integration, AI agent actions, monitoring, and human oversight.
  • Identify and help implement at least one practical use of AI or automation that improves a cybersecurity capability or architecture process, such as threat modeling, control analysis, vulnerability prioritization, design review, or risk reporting.
  • Demonstrate measurable value through secure solution delivery, improved design consistency, earlier identification of architectural risks, and actionable guidance that delivery teams can implement.

Education & Career Experience Requirements

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required. Bachelors degree preferred.
  • Foundational-level industry certification required upon hire.
  • Architect or senior-level industry certification preferred within 12 months of hire.
  • Minimum seven years experience in designing and implementing solutions, including cloud-native, microservices, and event-driven architectures required.

Additional Qualification

  • Ability to influence internal and/or external constituents.
  • Ability to communicate trade-offs and risks to both technical and business stakeholders.
  • Possesses strong technical aptitude.
  • This position requires deep expertise (example cloud-native architectures, zero-trust security, data governance, infrastructure automation).
  • Ability to drive multiple projects to successful completion.
  • Proven experience leading and delivering the architecture for large-scale, complex solutions spanning multiple teams, systems, or Agile Release Trains required.
  • Effective leadership skills.
  • Demonstrated experience mentoring other architects and driving architectural alignment across multiple programs.

Physical Actions

The physical work environment is indoors and climate-controlled with adequate lighting and ventilation. Normal and customary distractions include background noise produced by office equipment and chatter among people, as well as interruptions. Frequently sits for prolonged periods of time, up to a full shift. Occasionally moves about the workplace including, navigating stairs, ramps, and level or uneven surfaces. Occasionally moves, pushes, pulls, lifts, carries, and/or places objects or materials weighing up to 25 pounds without assistance. Frequently performs fine motor tasks such as typing, mousing, or writing, up to a full shift. Rarely performs movements such as bending, stooping, crouching, kneeling, twisting, and reaching overhead or below the knees. Possesses clear vision, with or without correction, to visually read and verify information. Relies on depth perception and peripheral vision to navigate the work environment visually by identifying barriers, changes in terrain and locating objects. Possesses adequate hearing, with or without correction, to communicate with co-workers, respond promptly to auditory signals or alarms, and discern sounds essential for maintaining safety and productivity in the workplace. Job Summary

This position oversees actuarial functions with a focus on financial projections of U.S. product liability cashflows. The role focuses on model development, testing, governance and consistency among various model stakeholders. This position leverages in-depth actuarial knowledge and understanding of the business to solve more complex issues and deliver strategic recommendations that align with business objectives. The position performs work independently while receiving guidance from a direct people leader and guiding more junior staff.

Essential Job Functions

  • Collaborates with stakeholders, teams, and other departments to resolve more complex actuarial issues. Guides the preparation of financial projections to enable leadership to assess financial implications and overall impact of business decisions. Accountable for timely and accurate delivery of actuarial deliverables. Interprets data and formulas to extract valuable insights for management. Analyzes operational performance and presents findings and recommendations for optimization. May represent the actuarial department with external stakeholders.
  • Independently develops and implements solutions to more complex actuarial issues. Oversees project workflows, provides robust feedback to stakeholders and management, and ensures timely and effective completion of work. Delivers on plans and priorities while guiding projects and/or teams to achieve successful outcomes and business objectives.
  • Advocates for improvements to assumption formulas, procedures, and programs. Anticipates the impact of changes and ensures recommendations align with broader business objectives.
  • Oversees the integration of new and updated products into financial projection system. Ensures actuarial modeling systems comply with controls and standards including updates for IT, product, and regulatory changes.
  • Stays informed about industry trends, emerging actuarial practices, and regulatory changes to contribute effectively to work within team, department, or across departments. Acts as a subject matter specialist to mentor and train less experienced actuarial staff by providing guidance on fundamental actuarial principles and practices. Performs other duties as assigned.

Physical Actions

Physical Environment

Public speaking, ability to function and handle high case loads in adversarial or confrontational situations, driving.

Job Summary

IAM Information Security Lead Specialist provides technical and strategic leadership for identity governance, access management, authentication, and IAM modernization initiatives. Collaborates with program sponsors, cross-functional teams, and assigned project managers to plan and develop scope, deliverables, required resources, work plan, budget, and timing for new security initiatives.

Essential Tasks & Leadership Philosophy

  • Lead the deployment, integration, and optimization of enterprise Identity and Access Management (IAM) solutions, ensuring alignment with business, security, and regulatory requirements.
  • Serve as a strategic IAM subject matter expert, identifying opportunities to enhance identity governance, access management, authentication, and authorization capabilities across the organization.
  • Drive the adoption of modern identity security practices, including Single Sign-On (SSO), Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), Privileged Access Management (PAM), and identity lifecycle management.
  • Develops expertise in insurance business operations in order to drive security innovations for a financial services organization.
  • Evaluate emerging IAM technologies and industry best practices to improve security, operational efficiency, and user experience.
  • Develops and implements innovative IAM programs, automation capabilities, and minimum viable products (MVPs) that support the organization's strategic security roadmap.
  • Partner with business leaders, technology teams, and security stakeholders to define IAM requirements, establish priorities, and deliver enterprise-wide identity initiatives.
  • Lead complex IAM projects and programs with broad scope, significant business impact, and cross-functional dependencies.
  • Coordinate activities across multiple IAM, cybersecurity, and technology initiatives to ensure alignment with organizational goals and security objectives.
  • Resolve complex identity, access, and authentication challenges by developing practical solutions that balance risk reduction with business enablement.
  • Develop metrics, dashboards, and executive reporting to communicate IAM program effectiveness, operational performance, compliance posture, and risk trends.
  • Builds and owns relationships that positively influence business outcomes.
  • Influence enterprise adoption of identity governance and access management best practices through effective communication, education, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Partners with business leaders to ensure information security risk findings are reviewed and solutions are implemented.
  • Effectively mentors, coaches and influences peers.

First Year Success Factors

  • Develop and Execute an Enterprise IAM Roadmap: Assess the current IAM, IGA, PAM, SSO, and MFA environment. Identify security gaps, compliance risks, and improvement opportunities. Create a prioritized roadmap aligned to business and security objectives.
  • Strengthen Identity Governance and Access Controls: Improve joiner, mover, and leaver processes. Enhance role-based access controls (RBAC).Implement or mature access certification and periodic access reviews. Reduce inappropriate or excessive access privileges.
  • Advance Identity Security Capabilities: Increase adoption of: Single Sign-On (SSO); Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA); Privileged Access Management (PAM); Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) and Improve authentication security while maintaining a positive user experience.
  • Deliver Major IAM Initiatives Successfully: Lead large-scale IAM projects across business and technology teams. Ensure implementations are delivered on time and within scope. Minimize disruption to business operations.

Education & Career Experience Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree required.
  • Relevant Information Security certification (CISSP, SCC, ISSAP and/or ISACA, etc.) required.
  • 7-10 years related experience in IT Security or identity access management, and Project Management, or comparable base of knowledge/expertise in the field.
  • Strong knowledge of Identity and Access Management principles, including authentication, authorization, identity governance, and access lifecycle management.
  • Deep expertise in Identity and Access Management, Identity Governance and Administration (IGA), authentication, authorization, and access lifecycle management.

Physical Actions

Sits or stands for extended periods of time, up to a full work shift. Occasionally reaches overhead and below the knees, including bending, twisting, pulling, and stooping. Occasionally moves, lifts, carries, and places objects and supplies weighing 0-10 pounds without assistance. Listens to, interprets, and differentiates auditory information (e.g. others speaking) at normal speaking levels with or without correction. Visually verifies and reads information. Visually locates material, resources and other objects. Ability to operate a computer for extended periods of time, up to a full work shift. Physical dexterity sufficient to use hands, arms, and shoulders repetitively to operate keyboard and other office equipment up to a full work shift.

Physical Environment

This position operates in an open office working environment which will include normal and customary distractions, noise, and interruptions.

About this job

Account Manager II at CorVel manages established customer accounts in the workers' compensation and risk management industry, handling accounts with minimum $1m revenue. Responsibilities include consultative service delivery, revenue growth, collections management, client stewardship, and contract renewals.

Good fit if you have a bachelor's degree, account management experience, and proficiency with Microsoft Office and Salesforce.

Full job description

The Account Manager is responsible for interacting with customers on an executive level and acting as an extension of the client; understanding and communicating agreed upon expectations to field offices and increasing the market share of business by providing service that meets and exceeds customer expectations, stewardship reporting, commitment to customer goals, and introducing/selling/implementing additional services.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS & RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Provide consultative customer services for one or more new or established accounts
  • Introduce new services independently or with assistance as needed
  • Handle local or regional accounts
  • Manage accounts with revenue in one region and a minimum revenue amount of $1m per account with a combined revenue for all accounts of over $3m.
  • Revenue growth with existing accounts
  • Accounts Receivable - Responsible for all aspects of collections in conjunction with the respective operations management
  • Client Stewardship- Responsible for conducting regular stewardship meetings and overseeing the integrity and delivery of client specific reports and information; must perform in a consultative role identifying trends and providing CorVel solutions to market and business challenges
  • Client Retention - Maintain continuous communication with customers to ensure that all service expectations are identified and maintained; communicate and engage senior management in account status, challenges and goals; every national account and large account will have an RVP (Regional Vice President) as a senior operations representative assigned to the account
  • Proactively raise concerns or potential issues to appropriate members of the management and executive team to remedy immediate concerns before they become issues; maintain an open items matrix to document all issues and resolution
  • Facilitate and coordinate internal customer set-up and external implementation
  • Coordinate and attend customer meetings; ensure CorVel participants are engaged
  • Discuss, understand, and meet agreed upon standards as mutually determined by CorVel and customer
  • Develop/maintain account service instructions/communicate to service staff and post on the Intranet
  • Manage contract renewals/price increases; coordinate with the AE and/or management team as appropriate
  • Present information to assigned customers in an organized and persuasive fashion for contract renewals, service issue discussions, or additional product sales
  • Regular attendance on the Monthly Account Manager Call
  • Provide monthly account updates and document all new service opportunities in Salesforce.com
  • Additional duties as assigned

KNOWLEDGE & SKILLS:

  • Reliable professional with the ability to achieve balance between customer orientation and a results-driven approach
  • Knowledge of CorVel's services and completion of all CorVel Product Training Modules
  • Business acumen, coupled with enthusiasm and decorum

  • Strong interpersonal skills and commitment to customer service
  • Able to work collaboratively and independently
  • Highly developed organizational abilities as well as analytical and time management skills
  • Must be proficient in Microsoft Office applications and CRM software (Salesforce)

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE:

  • Bachelor's degree, national certification or equivalent in business or sales and marketing
  • Demonstrated experience in account management
  • Training within the insurance industry, managed care or related field preferred

CorVel uses a market based approach to pay and our salary ranges may vary depending on your location. Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $18.00 an hour
  • Schedule: Full-time, includes weekends
  • Location: Louisville, KY
  • Education: High school diploma or GED
  • Benefits: Health insurance, 401(k), tuition assistance

About this job

Remote insurance sales role selling Allstate products to warm leads via phone, chat, and SMS. Base pay of $18/hour plus uncapped performance incentives, paid training from day one, and licensing support provided.

Good fit if you have 1+ year of sales or customer service experience and can obtain a Personal Lines or Property & Casualty Producer license.

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

Allstates sales organization is growing its virtual workforce, and we are looking for highly motivated individuals that thrive in a fast-paced sales environment and enjoy being rewarded for their efforts. At Allstate, we are committed to offering a reputable product suite that protects people from lifes uncertainties so they can realize their hopes and dreams.

As a full-time Insurance Sales Representative, you will:

  • Engage with active insurance shoppers via inbound/outbound calls, live chat, SMS, and more in a work from home call center environment.
  • Use your insurance expertise to uncover customer needs, identify coverage gaps, and recommend tailored solutions from Allstate products and products within the Allstate family of companies.
  • Convert warm leads into customers using a proven consultative sales strategy no cold calling required.
  • Work from home to drive sales growth while delivering an exceptional, customer-first experience.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Base Pay: $18/hour
  • Average Total Compensation: $52,730$76,480/year (base + uncapped performance-based incentives)
  • Incentives are productivity-based and governed by the applicable bonus plan, which is subject to change at Allstates discretion.


Full suite of employee benefits starting day one, including:

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) with company match and pension plan
  • Tuition reimbursement and career development
  • Wellness programs

Additional Benefits

  • Paid training from day one (classroom and hands-on)
  • Licensing support: study materials, exam reimbursement, and assistance
  • Monthly internet reimbursement
  • Home office equipment provided by Allstate

Why Join Allstate

  • No Prospecting: Warm leads delivered directly to you
  • Career Growth: Develop your skills within a dynamic, supportive Fortune 100 company
  • Supportive Culture: Learn from best-in-class leaders and motivated teammates
  • Trusted Brand: Be part of a company with 90+ years of industry experience
  • Diverse & Reputable Product Suite: Sell from a wide portfolio that meets every customers needs

Requirements

  • At least 1 year of experience in sales or customer service (with a sales focus)
  • Active Personal Lines or Property & Casualty Producer license in your state of residence (preferred)
  • If unlicensed, ability to obtain a Personal Lines or Property & Casualty Producer license with Allstates support
  • Sales Representatives are required to obtain and maintain all required resident and non-resident Producer licenses necessary to sell insurance products in any state designated by Allstate. This includes obtaining non-resident Producer licenses in all states as required for the role.
  • If hired, Sales Representative must relinquish all non-Allstate insurance carrier appointments and may not hold active appointments with other carriers while employed in this role, in accordance with Allstate licensing and appointment policies.
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Reliable high-speed internet with wired connection (Ethernet)
  • Dedicated, distraction-free home workspace (equipment provided)
  • Comfortable working evenings and weekends
  • Receptive to feedback and performance coaching
  • Strong communication, critical thinking, and multitasking skills
  • Competitive, highly self-motivated and enjoys being rewarded for your efforts
  • Able to work independently and hold yourself accountable for your performance
  • Ability to navigate multiple computer systems simultaneously


Essential Job Functions

  • Handle inbound and outbound customer calls as the primary method of customer engagement.
  • Maintain availability during assigned work hours to meet call volume and service expectations. This function is particularly crucial during an employees first 90 days of employment.
  • Deliver consultative sales conversations and complete transactions during live customer interactions.
  • Adhere to assigned schedules, including evenings and weekends, based on business coverage needs.
  • Meet established productivity, quality, and performance standards.
  • Navigate multiple computer systems simultaneously while actively engaged with customers.

This position is only available within theUS, but notcurrently available for Puerto Rico, California, New York, Alaska, Hawaii, or Washington state residents.

Candidates who reside in locations where the local minimum wage exceeds the base pay for this position are also not eligible for consideration. This is due to compliance with wage regulations and internal compensation practices.


Reasonable Accommodation Statement

Allstate provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities to enable them to perform the essential functions of their role. During the first 90 days of employment, reasonable accommodations generally do not include removing essential job functions, creating new positions, or lowering performance or productivity standards.

Customer Centricity, Customer Insights, Customer Sales, Digital Literacy, Inclusive Leadership, Learning Agility, Results-Oriented, Sales, Sales Operations, Strategic Selling

Compensation

Base Pay:$18 per hour

Job.JobTitle: Platform Consultant Cyber Platforms, Data, & Tooling
Job.JobDescription:
At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

This role sits within Allstate Cyber Operations & Platforms as part of a set of Digital Product Teams responsible for building and operating a cohesive, scalable Security Operations platform ecosystem. This ecosystem spans:

Agentic Cyber Platforms (ACP): Operationalizing AI as a core cyber capability through shared platforms, orchestration patterns, and governance-by-design.

Security Data & Observability (SD&O): Engineering and managing the Security Operations Data Plane, enabling high-fidelity telemetry, analytics, and AI-ready data.

Tooling & Platform (T&P): Ensuring security tooling is integrated, governed, and aligned as part of a unified platform rather than disconnected solutions. Together, these capabilities enable secure, scalable, and intelligence-driven cyber operations by design.

The Platform Consultant defines and drivesarchitecture patterns, integration standards, and ecosystem strategyacross AI platforms, security data, and tooling. This role ensures the environment evolves as acoherent, reusable, and governed platform ecosystem, enabling safe, scalable adoption through well-defined paved roads.


You will translate operational intent intoenterprise-scale platform design, ensuring interoperability between AI systems, data platforms, and tooling while minimizing fragmentation and maximizing reuse.

Key Responsibilities

Platform Architecture & Standards

  • Define architecture, design patterns, and integration standards across AI, data, and tooling.

  • Establish APIs, data models, security controls, and observability requirements.

Data & AI Enablement

  • Ensure high-quality, structured data for AI (lineage, consistency, readiness).

  • Set standards for safe AI use (explainability, auditability, controlled actions).

Tooling & Integration

  • Design unified integration across tools and platforms.

  • Ensure tools produce consistent, high-quality, AI-ready data.

Paved Roads & Adoption

  • Build scalable, reusable solutions as the default (paved roads).

  • Drive standardization, reduce duplication, andguideadoption.

Strategy & Decision-Making

  • Lead build vs. buy vs. integrate decisions.

  • Ensure solutions are scalable, secure, andgovernance-driven.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Partner across teams (ACP, SD&O, T&P) for platform alignment.

  • Influence teams to drive simplification, reuse, and consistency.

Essential Criteria

  • A minimum of 5 years software engineering experience in at least 3 programming paradigms toinclude: a) Object-oriented (Java &JavaScriptrequiredand at least one other language) b) Procedural / systems (e.g.Go, Rust, C) c) Functional (e.g.F#, Elixir, Clojure, Haskell)

  • Experience using modern development tools (e.g., IntelliJ or VS Code, Git/GitHub, Spring Boot) and designing robust RESTful APIs

  • A minimum of 3 years hands onexpertisein architecting and delivering large scale distributed systems, such as cloud native microservices on Docker/Kubernetes, deployed on modern cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or equivalent), ensuring scalability, high availability, and performance

  • Demonstrated success as a high impact technical advisor to multiple engineering teams, with proven ability to influence architecture direction and mentor engineers in best practices with proven leadership responsibilities.

  • Expert level knowledge of Agile/XP and DevOps methodologies, including paired programming, test driven development (TDD), and CI/CD automation, witha track recordof using these practices to accelerate delivery and improve quality

Desirable Criteria

  • Experience withagentic AI platforms, governance, and safe-action design

  • Familiarity withsecurity operations ecosystems and analyst workflows

  • Experience with:a) Telemetry and observability systems b) Data lineage, metadata, and data quality frameworks c) Canonical data models and analytics-ready datasets

  • Background intooling integration and platform standardization (golden paths/paved roads)

  • Experience aligningAI, data, and tooling strategies into a unified platform vision

Supervisory Responsibilities

  • This job does not have supervisory duties.

#LI-JJ1

Skills

Artificial Intelligence (AI), CI/CD, Cloud Platform, Cross-Functional Leadership, Decision Making, DevOps, IT Solution Design, Java (Programming Language), Platform Architecture, RESTful APIs, Software Engineering, Structured Data, Technical Consulting, Test Driven Development (TDD)

Compensation

Compensation offered for this role is 134,000.00 - 209,750.00 annually and is based on experience and qualifications.

The candidate(s) offered this position will be required to submit to a background investigation.

Job.JobTitle: Direct Sales Agent Specialist (2429) - Direct Auto
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Insurance Sales Representative, Insurance Sales, Insurance Agent
Job.JobDescription:
National General is a part of The Allstate Corporation, which means we have the same innovative drive that keeps us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. We offer home, auto and accident and health insurance, as well as other specialty niche insurance products, through a large network of independent insurance agents, as well as directly to consumers.

Job Description

The Direct Sales Agent Specialist is responsible for driving profitable growth by generating new business, cross-selling existing customers, and building lasting relationships. Job.JobTitle: Attack Surface Management Service Lead Consultant - Exposure Intelligence Team
Job.JobDescription:
At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

Role Scope: Attack Surface Management Service Lead Consultant Exposure Intelligence

Allstate Job Profile & Family: Lead Consultant- Threat & Incident Response


Team and overall work scope

  • The team operates within a newly established Exposure Management function in the broader cybersecurity organization, focused on modernizing how the enterprise identifies, prioritizes, and mitigates security vulnerabilities shifting from traditional patch approaches to a more strategic focus on true business risk and exploitability
  • Individual Contributor/ Lead Consultant roles are designed to bring in deep respective domain expertise (network, endpoint, cloud, identity, infrastructure, Databases & Data Stores, Applications, API's, Attack Surface Management etc.) to bridge the gap between security insights and practical remediation strategies
  • The Lead Consultant Attack Surface Management is the SME responsible for discovering, monitoring, and governing the enterprise's internet-facing attack surface, including unknown and unmanaged assets, external exposures, and third-party and subsidiary footprints. As the founding member of the capability, the role establishes ASM practices, applies CTEM principles to tie external findings to real attack paths, and partners with asset owners to drive remediation that measurably reduces exploitable exposure.

Success Measures

  • Expanded and validated coverage of the external attack surface, with fewer unknown or unowned internet-facing assets.
  • Reduced time from discovery of a new external exposure to an assigned owner and completed mitigation.
  • Higher signal quality in external findings, with fewer false positives and more accurate prioritization.

Key Responsibilities (Core + Domain)


Exposure Intelligence (Core)

  • Translate external attack surface findings into exposure intelligence and exploitability-based prioritization.
  • Identify attack paths that start from internet-facing assets, such as exposed services, misconfigurations, expired or weak certificates, and exposed admin interfaces.
  • Produce clear remediation guidance and partner with asset owners to validate closure.


Attack Surface Management (Domain)

  • Own SME coverage for external attack surface discovery and monitoring using EASM and scanning platforms (e.g., Censys, Qualys).
  • Establish asset governance practices, including attribution, ownership assignment, inventory reconciliation, and detection of shadow IT and orphaned assets.
  • Extend visibility to third-party, subsidiary, and cloud-hosted footprints, and partner with Penetration Testing, Product Security, and Exposure Response to operationalize findings.

Required Qualifications

  • 3+ years in attack surface management, vulnerability management, security operations, or exposure management.
  • Strong understanding of internet-facing infrastructure, including DNS, IP space, certificates, cloud hosting, and common external misconfigurations.
  • Ability to translate technical findings into business risk and practical remediation actions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with Censys or comparable EASM platforms, and with Qualys or similar vulnerability scanning tools.
  • Familiarity with asset inventory/CMDB processes, cloud provider connectors, and third-party risk practices.
  • Ability to build a new capability from the ground up, including processes, metrics, and stakeholder buy-in, as the first person in the function.

Skills Attack Surface Management, External Attack Surface Management (EASM), Asset Discovery, Asset Inventory Management, Cloud Security, Network Security, Third-Party Risk Management, Vulnerability Management, Threat and Vulnerability Management

Skills

Asset Inventory Management, Attack Surface Analysis, Cyber Incident Response, Cyber Threat Hunting, IT Security Operations, Network Security, Penetration Testing, Stakeholder Management, Threat and Vulnerability Assessment, Threat and Vulnerability Management, Vulnerability Management

Compensation

Compensation offered for this role is 100,000.00 - 170,500.00 annually and is based on experience and qualifications.

The candidate(s) offered this position will be required to submit to a background investigation.

Handle escalated property claims involving complex contents damage for Allstate in Atlanta. Use advanced video technology and estimating software to investigate coverage, assess damages, and negotiate settlements with customers.

Good fit if you have 3+ years of property insurance claims experience, know Xactimate software, hold a valid driver's license, and live in Metro Atlanta.

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

A day in the life of a Coordinated Property Adjuster, and what it takes to do the job!

As a Coordinated Property Adjuster, you will be dedicated to providing exceptional service to our policyholders. Your primary responsibility will be handling escalated claims files involving complex contents damage to ensure our customers receive the highest level of support and resolution for these claims.

  • Handle escalated claims files involving complex contents damage.
  • Conduct a thorough coverage investigation of the loss and ensure the policy was applied correctly.
  • Use advanced video technology to collaborate with onsite vendors to identify damages and write a contents damage estimate.
  • Communicate empathetically with customers and help them through their claim process in a fast, fair, and easy manner.
  • Negotiate claim settlements with customers in accordance with business unit standard methodologies.
  • Coordinate with structure and ALE adjusters to ensure holistic handling of the claim file.
  • Use data and analytics to tell a story and influence decision making.
  • If offered the role, you will go through virtual training. You will receive ongoing support, mentoring and coaching as you develop your career.

You'll wear a few hats that will require a level of experience:

  • The Customer Service Expert youll live into Allstates Claims Culture by caring, empowering, and restoring, and you will accomplish that by being compassionate, clear, and a committed partner in each Property claim. You lead with empathy, always.
  • The Investigator youll confidently and independently investigate property claims by performing detailed reviews of damage and interpreting policies to determine coverage.
  • The Effective Communicator youll use phone, emails and sometimes even video chat with customers to help them through a fast, fair, and easy claims process. Youll also incorporate a specific approach to claim handling to offer the customer their preference of communication to efficiently discuss their claim needs and keep them updated on the claim progress.
  • The Negotiator You will evaluate and negotiate claims settlements with customers, vendors, third party carriers and claimants, in accordance with all legal and business standard methodologies. With negotiations, you will incorporate tactics in handling challenging and complex situations.
  • The Problem Solver youll utilize multiple tools to get the job done in a fast-paced environment, including estimate tools, job aids, and additional settlement platforms, all while using your sharp critical thinking skills.
  • The Recorder youll protect the company financially by executing policies along policy agreements, and you keep a clear record of your work in a claims system that you will be trained in. Youll accomplish this by ensuring timely and accurate documentation is completed as you work on each claim.

  • Monday Friday; 8 am - 5 pm.
  • This role involves taking care of customers in their times of need. As a result, you must be willing to work some weekend and extended hours if necessary.

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Houston, TX
