We are seeking a Loss Control Consultant to conduct on-site loss control surveys and virtual meetings of prospective and written commercial lines accounts, within a designated geographic territory, to gain a thorough understanding of their operations.

The territory for this role will mainly be within the state of Alabama. Candidate must reside within the territory (ideally the Birmingham or Montgomery area).

We are seeking an Enterprise Test & Quality Lead to provide end-to-end ownership of testing across development, QA, UAT, and release activities. This role is accountable for defining and governing the test strategy, coordinating testing across multiple concurrent delivery teams, improving environment and test data readiness, and ensuring that releases meet agreed quality and business acceptance criteria. The role is particularly important in a delivery context where shared environments, constrained non-production data, and cross-team dependencies require disciplined planning, strong stakeholder management, and clear operational control.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the end-to-end test management lifecycle across Unit Testing, System Integration Testing, QA, UAT, regression testing, and release readiness.

  • Define and drive a Quality Engineering strategy embedding automated testing across the SDLC including “shift-left” and “shift-right” practices.

  • Define and maintain the overall test strategy, test plans, phase entry and exit criteria, acceptance thresholds, and defect management approach. Work and align with incumbent vendor to align QA to this overall strategy.

  • Define and enforce automated quality gates within CI/CD pipelines.

  • Coordinate testing across multiple concurrent scrum teams, ensuring alignment of delivery schedules, dependencies, and release milestones.

  • Define an environment strategy that enables parallel team execution, minimizes contention, and supports continuous testing.

  • Ownership of Test Data Governance Framework

  • o Ensure adherence and support from DPO / IRM / Privacy

  • Own the approach to Test Data Management, including data readiness, lineage, masking or obfuscation controls, and interim solutions required to support testing safely and effectively.

  • Partner with QA leads to define test scenarios, test cases, regression coverage, and the appropriate level of automation, including use of tools such as Tosca to deliver ROI driven automation, decisions on what to automate and coverage targets.

  • KPI Management of QA vendor

  • SLA tracking

  • Capability and skill matrix optimization.

  • Trend analysis of defect origin (code, data, environment, design) leading to systemic issue elimination

  • Work with Product Owners and business stakeholders to secure UAT participation, define UAT scripts and acceptance criteria, and manage UAT execution to completion.

  • The Test Manager should be a critical input into the release management go / no go stage gate decisions.

  • Manage defect triage, retest cycles, and regression planning to ensure efficient resolution and minimal disruption to completed testing.

  • Provide decision grade insights on test progress, risks, defect trends, environment readiness, and overall release confidence to project and executive stakeholders.

  • Drive continuous improvement in test practices, with a focus on moving from reactive or waterfall-like testing toward a more agile, disciplined, and scalable operating model.

  • Define and oversee post release validation strategies, including observability, monitoring, and production quality feedback loops.

  • Skills and Experience

  • Proven experience in Test Management, QA leadership, or quality engineering leadership within complex technology delivery environments.

  • Strong understanding of end-to-end software testing practices across unit, integration, system, regression, data lineage and user acceptance testing.

  • Experience managing testing in agile delivery environments with multiple concurrent teams and shared environments.

  • Practical knowledge of test automation and engineering led strategy and tooling, ideally including Tosca or comparable platforms, especially AI driven technologies and processes.

  • Strong understanding of environment management and test data management, including handling of sensitive data in non-production environments.

  • Ability to define quality gates, release readiness criteria, and structured defect management processes.

  • Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work across engineering, QA, product, operations, and business teams.

  • Excellent planning, coordination, and communication skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and delivery risk.

  • Experience in regulated or control-conscious environments is highly desirable.

  • Experience of integrating testing into DevOps pipelines and familiarity with release orchestration and production validation techniques.

  • Experience of operating in SAFe (scaled agile) frameworks


Success Measures

  • Improved coordination and predictability across QA and UAT cycles including continuous validation and early user involvement.

  • Reduction in defects caused by environment or data issues rather than true functional failures.

  • Clear and consistently applied phase entry, exit, and acceptance criteria.

  • Increased confidence in release readiness and reduced rework or defect recycling.

  • Greater use of automation and regression coverage to support faster retest cycles.

  • Stronger governance, visibility, and accountability for end-to-end testing outcomes.


Key Interfaces
This role will work closely with Development Leads, QA Leads, Product Owners, Business UAT representatives, Environment and Release Management teams, Data and Privacy stakeholders, and senior programme or technology leadership.
Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related discipline.

  • Relevant testing or quality certifications such as ISTQB Advanced Test Manager or equivalent are desirable.

  • Experience in insurance, financial services, or other highly regulated delivery environments would be advantageous.

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $180,00 - $230,000. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location.

About the Team

AXIS is hiring a Senior Claims Specialist, Excess Casualty, to support its expanding presence in North America's Excess market.

How does this role contribute to our collective success?

You will handle highly complex commercial excess casualty claims by verifying coverage, conducting investigations, developing resolutions, and authorizing disbursements within authority limits. Ensure consistent communication with stakeholders, brokers, and insureds to uphold service excellence. Process, analyze, investigate, evaluate, and resolve claims for accurate settlements. Collaborate with internal teams and external stakeholders to deliver exceptional service and support claims department success.

What Will You Do In This Role?

• Assessing claims within a specialized area to determine coverage, liability, and settlement value.
• Analyzing coverage and drafting coverage correspondence.
• Participating in mediations and attending trials as required.
• Leading initiatives to enhance claims processing efficiency and accuracy within the team.
• Collaborating with legal and investigative teams to resolve complex or contentious claims.
• Providing expert opinions on claims handling best practices during cross-functional meetings.
• Managing costs in collaboration with the Litigation Management and Vendor Management teams
• Participating in professional associations to stay abreast of changes in claims management.
• Communicating with senior executives, brokers, reinsurers, actuaries, underwriters, insureds, and auditors (both external and internal)
• Serving as a mentor to claims professionals, fostering skill development and career progression.

About You

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table, so while there are some qualifications and experiences, we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge might lend itself to fulfilling this role and help us achieve our goals.

What We're Looking For

• Demonstrate the capability to lead process enhancement initiatives within a claims environment.
• Possess the skills to provide expert opinions and insights during cross-functional discussions.
• Be adept at creating and directing the development of training materials relevant to claims processing.
• Show a commitment to continuous professional development in the field of claims management.
• Have the ability to critically review and update claims procedures to maintain regulatory compliance.
• Be capable of mentoring peers and fostering their professional growth within the claims discipline.

Role Factors

This role requires you to be in the office 3 days per week and adhere to AXIS licensing requirements

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. Senior Manager, Quality Assurance and Compliance | North America Claims, Claims Shared Services-

AXIS is seeking a Senior Manager, Quality Assurance and Audit, North America Claims to join the Claims Shared Services team. Reporting to the Head of Quality Assurance and Compliance, Claims Shared Services, this role will lead, oversee, enhance and optimize the North America claim direct handle, manager quality review and TPA oversight audit program. The role will also coordinate, oversee, and enhance the North America Claims SIU and Fraud program.

The successful candidate will plan, coordinate, monitor, and report on audits and quality file reviews across North America Claims, including specialty claim handler audits across multiple lines of business, TPA oversight audits, and leadership quality control file reviews. The role will manage audit execution through internal stakeholders and external audit partners, track findings through closure, report results to leadership, and use audit insights to strengthen claim handling quality, compliance, consistency, and operational performance.

This role is ideal for a claims, audit, quality assurance, or compliance professional with strong technical claims judgment, experience assessing specialty claim handler performance, working knowledge of TPA or outsourced claims partner oversight, and the ability to translate audit and file review results into practical actions that improve claim outcomes.

The successful Candidate will be responsible for:

Claims Audit Program Management
• Lead and report on the North America claim handler audit program, TPA oversight audit program, and leadership quality control file review program across multiple lines of business.
• Manage end-to-end audit execution, including planning, scope, scheduling, sample selection, file collection, stakeholder communications, and audit readiness.
• Coordinate with claim leaders, specialty claim handlers, TPAs, audit vendors, Compliance, Legal, Internal Audit, and Operations to ensure consistent, timely audit delivery.
• Enhance audit standards, questionnaires, scorecards, and methodologies in line with claim best practices, regulatory expectations, and technical excellence standards.
• Review audit observations across coverage, liability, damages, reserving, litigation management, settlement strategy, documentation quality, compliance, and claim handling controls.
• Track findings, action plans, remediation activities, owner accountability, due dates, and closure evidence.

Audit Results, Analytics, and Reporting
• Gather, validate, and analyze audit results, quality assurance data, compliance findings, and technical claim handling trends.
• Develop dashboards, scorecards, and management reports covering quality review results, technical audit outcomes, recurring themes, risk areas, trends, and improvement opportunities.
• Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting for Claims leadership and governance forums, covering claim handler audit results, TPA oversight audit results, and leadership quality control file review outcomes.
• Measure audit effectiveness, remediation progress, transparency, accountability, and control discipline.

Compliance, Controls, and Remediation
• Partner with Compliance, Legal, Internal Audit, Claims Operations, and Claims Leadership to align audit activity with regulatory, governance, and operational risk priorities.
• Monitor findings related to Medicare, regulatory obligations, documentation standards, claim handling controls, and other compliance requirements.
• Maintain action plans that address findings, strengthen controls, and promote consistent claim handling across North America specialty claim teams, TPA claim programs, and leadership quality control file reviews.
• Escalate material issues, recurring trends, control gaps, and remediation delays to appropriate leaders and governance forums.

SIU and Fraud Audit Program
• Enhance, measure, and report on the SIU and fraud deliverable program as part of the North America claims audit program.
• Assess whether SIU and fraud deliverables are timely, complete, consistent, and aligned with claim handling expectations, regulatory obligations, and technical audit standards.
• Identify themes, control gaps, escalation issues, documentation weaknesses, and opportunities to improve fraud identification, referral quality, and SIU oversight.
• Partner with SIU, Compliance, Claims leadership, TPAs, and audit vendors to strengthen execution, reporting, accountability, and remediation follow-through.

Technical Excellence and Continuous Improvement
• Use audit and quality control file review insights to improve technical claim quality, consistency, reserving discipline, litigation management, settlement practices, and compliance execution.
• Support updates to claims guidelines, audit protocols, procedures, workflows, controls, and training materials based on audit trends and root-cause analysis.
• Provide practical recommendations to claim leaders, specialty claim handlers, TPAs, and business partners to improve claim outcomes and audit performance.
• Participate in governance meetings, working groups, and initiatives related to claims quality, audit readiness, and technical excellence.

Stakeholder Management
• Build effective relationships across North America Claims, specialty claim teams, TPAs, Compliance, Legal, Internal Audit, Actuarial, Finance, Operations, and Shared Services.
• Manage day-to-day coordination with external audit vendors, including schedules, deliverables, issue tracking, reporting inputs, and performance expectations.
• Provide audit and quality assurance subject matter support to claim leaders, specialty claim handlers, TPA managers, and governance stakeholders.
• Communicate findings, themes, risks, and recommendations clearly to management and senior leadership.

Skills
• 6–10 years of experience in commercial P&C insurance, reinsurance, specialty claims, claims audit, quality assurance, compliance, operational risk, or a related discipline.
• Minimum 3 years of experience supporting or managing claims audits, quality assurance reviews, compliance monitoring, operational controls, or remediation tracking.
• Experience working with TPAs, outsourced claims partners, audit vendors, or vendor oversight programs.
• Experience auditing specialty claim files across multiple lines of business and supporting technical claim quality reviews.
• Experience developing audit reports, dashboards, metrics, scorecards, or performance analytics for leadership review.
• Strong technical claims judgment and ability to assess claim handling quality across coverage, liability, damages, reserving, litigation, settlement, and documentation practices.
• Strong analytical, communication, project coordination, organizational, stakeholder management, and vendor management skills.
• Ability to identify themes, root causes, risks, control gaps, performance improvement opportunities, and remediation priorities.
• Ability to manage multiple audits, stakeholders, priorities, and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
• Strong proficiency in Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and reporting tools.
• Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree, CPCU, AIC, ARM, CFE, CIA, CPA, JD, or other relevant professional designation preferred.

Additional Information

• Ability to work in a hybrid environment (3 days in office)
• Some travel may be required

About this job

Manager role within Tech & Ops Finance responsible for enterprise-wide sourcing and supplier strategies, governance, and performance management. You will execute work order processes, manage supplier portfolios, oversee resource onboarding, and drive process improvements across assigned business lines.

Good fit if you have experience in sourcing, supplier management, vendor operations, or related procurement roles, and can manage multiple stakeholder relationships.

Full job description

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$99,100.00 - $163,400.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

Member of the Sourcing and Supplier Management team within Tech & Ops Finance responsible for enterprise-wide sourcing and supplier strategies, governance, performance management, risk and operational processes for Travelers' global sourcing and supplier relationships.

As a Manager, Sourcing Strategy, Management and Governance, you will play a critical role in executing work order processes across assigned business lines and area-specific strategic sourcing strategies, including sourcing model design, supplier selection, and alignment of suppliers to business needs across our professional services and outsourcing partner portfolio. You will serve as a key point of contact on execution of sourcing strategy, workforce demand, and supplier performance across assigned lines, partnering closely with business stakeholders to track activity, resolve issues, and identify opportunities to improve how the team operates. This position does not manage others.

What Will You Do?

  • Work Order/Vendor Management and Sourcing Strategy: Manage a defined set of supplier work orders or portfolio activities across multiple assigned lines, including intake, modifications, closures, data-driven analysis, and process and tool optimization. Serve as a proactive sourcing advisor to LOB stakeholders, providing counsel on sourcing model selection, supplier performance, and workforce demand planning. Apply enterprise sourcing models and rate card structures to work being requested, advising stakeholders on right model, right supplier, right rate.*      
  • Onboarding and Team Support: Oversee resource onboarding and monitor engaged resources for quality, progress, and team dynamics. Own resource onboarding end-to-end, including understanding the skills required for the work being engaged, validating skill requirements with LOB stakeholders, and driving Technical Assessments. Cultivate ongoing, trusted relationships with the owners of the work, including engagement managers and LOB stakeholders, staying close enough to the business to anticipate needs, flag risks early, and bring forward solutions before issues escalate. Partner with Circle Leads on resource and team alignment needs.     
  • Proactivity and Risk Management: Monitor assigned vendor performance data and flag early indicators of risk or control gaps, addressing delivery issues as they arise and escalating when appropriate. Analyze work order data, supplier capability changes, and sourcing market conditions to identify business continuity risks, surface insights, and deliver proactive recommendations to leadership. Maintain deep understanding of assigned business lines to anticipate workforce needs, monitor internal demands, and inform sourcing strategy.    
  • Internal and External Stakeholder Engagement: Build and sustain trusted relationships with business stakeholders, finance partners, and assigned supplier contacts to surface risks, resolve delivery concerns and budget variances, and support governance interactions, performance discussions, and sourcing process coordination. Provide data and updates supporting ELT visibility for assigned lines on execution of sourcing strategy, workforce demand, and supplier performance.      
  • Work Transition and Migration: Own the operational execution of work transitions when sourcing decisions result in a change of supplier, sourcing model, or workforce composition. This includes coordinating the migration of work from internal resources to external suppliers, managing supplier transitions, supporting onboarding of new supplier teams, and ensuring continuity of delivery throughout the transition period. Partner closely with LOB stakeholders, DFRs, and the S&SM Strategy team to sequence and execute transitions in alignment with enterprise sourcing strategy and workforce plans.      
  • Process Optimization: Identify and implement process improvements and automation opportunities, including AI-enabled workflow enhancements. Optimize like work across assigned lines, standardizing repeatable processes, eliminating redundancy, and driving consistency across the Sourcing Delivery and Execution team. Champion the use of Travelers' AI tooling to streamline reporting, automate recurring workflows, and improve the quality and speed of work.      
  • Rate Card Adherence: Ensure compliance with established enterprise sourcing models and rate card structures. Partner with the S&SM Strategy team to validate that work being requested aligns to the appropriate rate card, role designation, and sourcing model, and assist stakeholders in understanding and adhering to rate card guidelines.
  • Track and report on sourcing footprint, role utilization, team composition, and premium role usage across assigned lines. 
  • Manage sourcing activity across multiple assigned lines or areas. Bring cross-line perspective to sourcing decisions, identify patterns and efficiencies across the portfolio, and ensure consistent application of enterprise sourcing strategy regardless of line-specific variation. 
  • Monitor work order alignment to budget; proactively flag variances and partner with DFRs to resolve. 
  • Contribute to the preparation of Business Review materials and Monthly Operating Review (MOR) data for assigned lines, supporting leadership visibility into supplier performance, workforce trends, and sourcing activity across the portfolio. 
  • Partner cross-functionally with LOB stakeholders, DFRs, and Procurement to support sourcing and contracting activity, ensure alignment on budget and resource plans, and facilitate resolution of issues that span organizational boundaries. 
  • Engage with and learn Travelers' AI tooling, applying these capabilities to improve the speed and quality of recurring work such as reporting, data analysis, and workflow management. 

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience required.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in sourcing, workforce strategy, supplier management, or a related field.
  • Experience with Fieldglass, ACS, and workforce planning tools strongly preferred.
  • Experience supporting or managing work transitions, supplier migrations, or sourcing model changes preferred.
  • Familiarity with rate card structures, role modernization concepts, and supplier performance principles.
  • Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships with senior LOB or technology leaders.
  • Experience identifying and implementing process improvements or automation opportunities.
  • Familiarity with AI-powered tools and large language models (e.g., Claude); demonstrated ability or willingness to integrate AI capabilities into day-to-day work processes preferred.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite, including Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Strong working knowledge of sourcing models: managed services, staff augmentation, GSO, POD/catalog models, and rate card structures.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage complex, ambiguous situations and drive to resolution with senior stakeholders.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to evaluate sourcing data, identify trends, and translate findings into actionable recommendations for business partners.
  • Process improvement and automation orientation, with experience identifying and implementing operational efficiencies.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills, comfortable engaging with senior LOB leaders and building trusted advisor relationships.
  • Demonstrated initiative in identifying and adopting tools, technology, and process improvements that increase team efficiency and output quality, including AI-enabled solutions.
  • Demonstrated proficiency or willingness to actively develop proficiency with AI-powered tools, including large language models such as Claude; ability to apply these tools to sourcing workflows, reporting, and operational tasks to improve efficiency and output quality.
  • Ability to operate effectively through change and ambiguity, adapting approaches as the function evolves.

The Role at a Glance

We are excited to bring on an Excel/VBA Annuity Modeling Specialist to join our Retail Solutions organization in a hybrid work environment. We are open to candidates in the following key city locations: Charlotte (NC), Fort Wayne (IN), Greensboro (NC), Hartford (CT), Omaha (NE) and Radnor (PA).

Background Details

As the Excel/VBA Annuity Modeling Specialist, you will contribute to the development of benchmark test tools for our annuity illustration, administration, and other product platforms. Working under general supervision and following established guidelines, you will apply working knowledge of Excel and VBA to build and maintain spreadsheet models that verify the accuracy of our systems. This position supports analysis for stakeholders across the Annuities group while delivering on routine assignments within its assigned area. The incumbent also serves as a resource for annuity product technical questions and supports other ad hoc annuity analytical initiatives as needed.

What you'll be doing

  • You will support the development and implementation of Excel-based testing models for Variable, Fixed, Indexed, Immediate and Deferred Income Annuities to ensure the accuracy of our illustration system(s), digital platform(s), administration system(s), and any other supporting system(s), including but not limited to: adding new products to existing spreadsheet models, creating new spreadsheets for new products, and updating existing spreadsheets for product changes.

Position Summary

With limited supervision, translates near-term and long-term business needs of moderate to high complexity into (technical) initiative solution options across multiple portfolios. Provides enterprise-level context to the architecture team to enable team members to focus, mature domains, and create future-state architectures. Provides leadership visibility on complex initiatives by facilitating discussions, leading conceptual and high level design sessions, capturing the results in artifacts, and ensuring the architectural design is realized through delivery for multiple enterprise stakeholders.


What You'll Do

As a Senior Solutions Architect – Data, you'll play a key role in shaping ERIE's enterprise data strategy. You'll design and implement scalable, modern data architectures that ensure accuracy, consistency, and accessibility across the organization. You'll collaborate closely with data engineering, analytics, and business partners to align data initiatives with enterprise goals and deliver trusted, high-quality data solutions that power decision-making.

Your expertise will guide the design and integration of enterprise data systems—connecting traditional on-premises environments with modern, cloud-based ecosystems that support ERIE.


Preferred Experience & Skills

  • Hands-on experience designing and implementing enterprise data architectures that promote data quality and consistency.
  • Proficiency with Master Data Management (MDM) tools such as Informatica MDM, Reltio, SAP MDG, or IBM InfoSphere.
  • Strong understanding of data integration, governance, metadata management, and data stewardship principles.
  • Experience with data modeling, APIs, ETL design, and modern cloud data platforms (AWS, Azure, or similar).
  • Proven ability to collaborate across disciplines to define strategy and deliver scalable data solutions.
  • Familiarity with AWS services such as S3, Glue, or Redshift is a plus.


What Makes You Stand Out

You're a strategic thinker with a builder's mindset. You connect architecture vision with practical delivery—creating data systems that drive measurable business value. You balance innovation and structure, ensuring ERIE's data assets are both trusted and transformative.

You stand out because you:

  • Combine deep MDM expertise with practical cloud architecture experience.
  • Have a track record of integrating on-premises and cloud data environments.
  • Foster strong partnerships between IT and business, translating data strategy into real outcomes.
  • Bring curiosity, adaptability, and a continuous improvement mindset to every challenge.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Serves as the single point of accountability for architecture function to portfolio owner customers and technology leadership.
  • Provides architectural guidance on initiatives of moderate to high complexity across multiple enterprise portfolios, while managing multiple customers with differing priorities on the organization's most strategic initiatives.
  • Provides full-stack architectural options that enable business objectives while ensuring long-term technology goals for all aspects of a solution.
  • Collaborates with team members for technical validation during design and planning phases.
  • Informs aspects of portfolio maturity regarding technology and ability to achieve target technology alignment, while facilitating a minimum viable architecture.
  • Monitors large-scale project execution and considers and interprets architectural tradeoffs occurring during delivery. Escalates for appropriate context sharing and decision making, as necessary.
  • Proactively enables portfolio owners to see technical debt clearly, provides appropriate context to inform plans to achieve elimination of technical debt in a comprehensive plan across multiple portfolios, delivery teams, programs, or projects.
  • Serves as a mentor for other members of the team, builds an environment for analysts, engineers, architects, and other technology leaders to grow and have high impact.
  • Directs and drives closure on investment decisions within the enterprise while also identifying cross-portfolio impacts on significant delivery initiatives.
  • Serves as a subject matter expert for multiple portfolios, providing actionable recommendations via consultation services, adapted to stakeholder context, to technology leadership and organizational stakeholders.
  • Collaborates with architects, portfolio owners, and other job families to achieve an enterprise view; provides project and program level views to project and program teams in context of enterprise strategies and directions with light supervision.
  • Supports business agility through agile engagement across multiple delivery operations.
  • Interprets business needs, assesses solution choices, applies technology, and provides project guidance within a long-term enterprise lens.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Product Owner plays a pivotal role in driving the successful development and delivery of innovative products that meet the needs of our customers and aligns with the company's strategic goals. This role acts as the bridge between business stakeholders, development teams and end-users, ensuring clear communication and effective prioritization of features and enhancements throughout the product lifecycle.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Maximizes the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum team.

  • Defines and communicates product vision, overall strategy and growth opportunities to business and IT stakeholders, with guidance from leadership and other Product team members.

  • Drives the continuous refinement of the product vision, roadmap, and strategy to drive optimum business value.

  • Works closely with business stakeholders across the organization to convert product ideas into a prioritized backlog according to business value or return on investment (ROI).

  • Participates in agile ceremonies such as sprint planning, iteration reviews, and retrospectives to ensure continuous improvement and iterative development.

  • Facilitates Product Grooming Backlog sessions to align priority & strategy for better cross functional collaboration.

  • Validates roadmap items prior to starting development work with guidance from business stakeholders as needed.

  • Remains accountable for each stage of the development process and the final product, evaluating progress and performance at each iteration and deciding whether the team can move on to the next steps.

  • Works closely with Technical Product Managers and Scrum master to ensure the successful execution of the product roadmap.

  • Anticipates product's future needs by maintaining user personas and journey maps.

  • Owns and drives user-centric product outcomes collaboratively with business and IT leadership.

  • Researches and analyzes market trends and user needs to develop and shape the roadmap for the product.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position has no supervisory responsibility.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university is required with a major or emphasis in Business, Finance, Computer Science, Engineering, or related field. Minimum 6 years of related experience inclusive of leading technical teams, collecting business needs, and translating requirements to a technical audience. Experience in the insurance industry highly desired. Minimum 3 years of experience as a Product Owner, Product Manager, or similar role, with a track record of successfully launching and managing products or platforms.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Certified Product Owner (CPO) required, SAFe preferred.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

Knowledge of Agile processes and principles. Understanding of the Insurance industry. Ability to map value stream across business lines. Company Details

As an elite Excess and Surplus Lines market, Nautilus Insurance Group offers commercial property and casualty insurance solutions to appointed wholesale surplus lines producers countrywide. We have specialized in providing these solutions for more than 35 years.

We have more flexible policy terms and premium rates on a non-admitted basis. Our focus is small to medium Property and Casualty risks on both an admitted and a non-admitted basis.

Our offerings are distributed through partnerships with appointed wholesale surplus lines producers. Our relationships are defined by mutual success, speed to market, customer-centric focus and an expanded appetite.

Coverage placed by Nautilus Insurance Group is provided by Nautilus Insurance Company and Great Divide Insurance Company, both W. R. Berkley Corporation members with A.M. Best (Superior) A+ XV ratings.

Responsibilities

The Litigation Specialist's job function includes efficiently and effectively handling advanced-level, primarily litigated, commercial third-party general liability losses in a “paperless” environment. An ability to communicate both verbally and in written form in a prompt, courteous and professional manner is essential.

This role can be located in our Scottsdale AZ office, or remotely for a highly qualified candidate.

  • Reviews and sets up new loss assignments in a timely manner in compliance with Department guidelines and best practices.
  • Establishes appropriate initial loss and expense reserves and continues to regularly evaluate the file for adequacy, accuracy and adherence to reserving guidelines.
  • Analyzes and interprets policy language in conjunction with specific loss facts to reach appropriate coverage decisions.
  • Drafts frequent and complex coverage correspondence, including reservation of rights and coverage disclaimers in compliance with various state statutes and regulations.
  • Composes a variety of other detailed correspondence to insureds, claimants, attorneys, agents and Regulatory agencies.
  • Proactively manages primarily litigated claim files from inception to closure, including identification and investigation of coverage, liability and damage issues, determination and efficient execution of an appropriate plan of action, and prompt, economical file resolution, in compliance with Department guidelines and best practices.
  • Appropriately and clearly documents all claim file activity, including current strategy, plan of action and exit plan in file notes.
  • Consistently demonstrates comprehensive coverage analysis, investigation, evaluation and negotiation skills at an advanced level.
  • Directs and controls the activities and costs of numerous outside vendors including defense counsel and coverage counsel, experts and independent adjusters.
  • Effectively presents and discusses loss facts and issues in roundtable discussions to peers and members of management at all levels.
  • Composes and transmits on a regular and timely basis frequent Large Loss Reports and other detailed reporting documents as appropriate.
  • Manages and monitors file caseload through the use of various resources.
  • Obtains all required state adjuster licenses and maintains them as required via compliance with mandatory continuing education requirements.
  • Other duties may be assigned.
  • Serves as a technical resource within the Department through mentoring and knowledge-sharing, whether one-on-one, in small groups, or presentations to larger groups.

Sustainability Manager, Carbon Accounting and Performance

Purpose: The Sustainability Manager will lead the company's greenhouse gas inventory and carbon accounting program for AIG's operations, ensuring accurate data, strong governance, regulatory alignment, and readiness for external reporting and assurance. The role will also track sustainability performance, support climate strategy, manage cross-functional programs, and translate technical topics into clear business insights and stakeholder communications. The ideal candidate brings strong sustainability and GHG expertise, analytical and project management skills, and the ability to collaborate effectively across the organization.

Key Responsibilities

GHG Inventory Governance & Operations Oversight – 50%

  • Own the annual operations GHG emissions inventory, including methodology, boundaries, assumptions and emissions factors and maintain a transparent, consistent and well-documented Inventory Management Plan that is ready for external reporting and assurance.
  • Manage the company's carbon accounting platform vendor, including system performance, data quality, enhancements and issue resolution.
  • Partner with the Operations lead and Sustainability Controller to establish clear roles, requirements, timelines, review protocols and documentation standards.
  • Partner with the Operations lead, sustainability data providers and third-party vendors to ensure timely, accurate and complete data collection and reporting.
  • Review and validate inventory results, including data quality, reasonableness, year-over-year changes and significant assumptions.
  • Oversee tracking, monitoring and reporting of GHG emissions regulatory requirements across legal entities and review legal entity GHG reporting for consistency and alignment with Group.
  • Partner with the Sustainability Controller to support GHG reporting controls, documentation, audit evidence and external assurance.
  • Monitor evolving GHG accounting standards and reporting expectations, assess their implications and improve the efficiency, consistency and governance of carbon accounting processes.

Sustainability Performance Management – 20%

  • Build cross-functional partnerships to align sustainability priorities, targets and performance measurement with business objectives.
  • Develop dashboards, scorecards and other tools to track sustainability performance and support reporting, communications and decision-making.
  • Evaluate the effectiveness of sustainability programs against business goals, stakeholder expectations and relevant industry benchmarks.
  • Apply credible frameworks, emissions pathways and industry methodologies to support the company's climate strategy and net zero commitments.
  • Provide subject-matter expertise to Sustainability Working Groups and help business and functional teams identify opportunities to advance sustainability and decarbonization priorities and integrate sustainability in business decision-making processes.
  • Monitor emerging sustainability developments, industry practices and stakeholder expectations to inform strategy and performance benchmarks.

Engagement and Program Delivery – 20%

  • Manage the development and execution of the company's sustainability engagement strategy.
  • Guide and support Sustainability Working Groups, business champions and the Employee Sustainability Network in advancing shared priorities.
  • Support the identification and management of external partnerships with industry groups, NGOs, academic institutions and other organizations aligned with the sustainability strategy.
  • Translate sustainability strategy and technical topics into clear, business-relevant messages, recommendations and actions.
  • Develop events, thought leadership, sponsorships and engagement initiatives that strengthen the Sustainability Office's visibility and support stakeholder expectations.
  • Measure the reach and impact of sustainability engagement activities and recommend improvements.
  • Manage cross-functional projects from planning through delivery, coordinating contributors, timelines, risks, deliverables and senior-management updates.

Additional Responsibilities – 10%

  • Develop clear presentations, disclosures and other materials that communicate sustainability priorities, performance and progress internally and externally (e.g., leadership meetings, CDP Climate Change Questionnaire, Ecovadis, content for annual sustainability report, ad-hoc requests)
  • Lead research and analysis on priority topics, including materiality, climate and GHG reporting, and present actionable insights to senior stakeholders.
  • Promote the Sustainability Office's visibility across the enterprise.
  • Support additional sustainability priorities and special projects as business needs evolve.

Qualifications

  • Minimum of five years of corporate sustainability experience.
  • Strong knowledge of GHG emissions accounting, methodologies and reporting requirements, and decarbonization strategies including renewable energy procurement.
  • Familiarity with evolving sustainability regulations and disclosure frameworks and standards, such as the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB), Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHGP), Science-based Target Initiative Standards (SBTi), RE 100.
  • Demonstrated project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, adapt plans and deliver high-quality work on time.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret complex information and present clear, actionable insights to senior management and executive audiences.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to simplify complex technical topics for diverse stakeholders.
  • Proven ability to build relationships and collaborate effectively across business lines, functions and stakeholder groups.
  • Experience with ESG data providers (e.g., MSCI, ISS, CDP, Sustainalytics, Ecovadis) and carbon accounting and management software.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, SharePoint and Teams.
  • Experience with Watershed (or similar carbon accounting platform) and Workiva strongly preferred
  • Experience improving processes, supporting change and working independently with sound judgment and initiative.
  • Strong attention to detail and consistent follow-through in a fast-paced environment.
  • Experience in insurance or financial services a plus

Education:

  • Bachelor's degree in Sustainability or Environmental-related field, Business or other discipline that aligns with corporate sustainability initiatives preferred. A master's degree in a similar field is desired.

Job Description

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Claims Specialist to play your part in that transformation. It's an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Claims


Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair, and professional service with empathy and efficiency.


How you will create an impact

Picture yourself building a successful career at AIG working alongside other talented, highly motivated individuals committed to reaching our goal of becoming the world's leading insurance provider. We believe that our success depends on building a world class team. If you would like to be a part of our team, we invite you to consider putting your talents to work with the AIG Claims department.


We are seeking an experienced Casualty Claims Adjuster to investigate, evaluate, negotiate, and resolve Commercial Auto Liability and Commercial General Liability claims. The ideal candidate will have a strong foundation in liability analysis, injury evaluation, coverage interpretation, and litigation management, with the ability to independently handle a moderate to complex caseload from initial notice through resolution. This role requires sound judgment, strong analytical skills, and the ability to balance customer service, financial stewardship, and technical claim expertise. The adjuster will work closely with insureds, claimants, attorneys, brokers, and internal business partners to deliver timely, fair, and compliant claim outcomes. You'll be responsible for:


Claim Investigation, Evaluation and Negotiation

  • Conduct prompt, thorough investigations to determine coverage, liability, damages, and compensability.
  • Gather and evaluate evidence, including statements, police reports, medical records, expert reports, and other relevant documentation.
  • Analyze coverage issues and prepare reservation of rights, denial, and other coverage correspondence as appropriate.
  • Evaluate bodily injury, property damage, and exposure-related claims to determine appropriate resolution strategies.
  • Independently negotiate settlements within established authority levels.
  • Develop and execute proactive claim resolution strategies that achieve timely and cost-effective outcomes.
  • Identify and mitigate claim exposure through effective investigation, evaluation, and negotiation.
  • Ensure accurate claim documentation supporting all decisions and actions taken throughout the life of the claim.

Litigation Management

  • Manage litigated files and coordinate with defense counsel to develop case strategies.
  • Review pleadings, discovery responses, deposition summaries, and legal evaluations.
  • Monitor litigation budgets and legal expenses to ensure efficient claim handling.
  • Participate in mediations, settlement conferences, and other dispute resolution proceedings as necessary.

Financial and Regulatory Stewardship

  • Establish and maintain accurate indemnity and expense reserves with documented rationale.
  • Continuously evaluate reserve adequacy throughout the life cycle of the claim.
  • Ensure compliance with company guidelines, statutory requirements, and regulatory standards across all applicable jurisdictions.
  • Maintain diary and workload management systems to effectively prioritize and resolve assigned inventory.

Customer and Stakeholder Management

  • Deliver exceptional customer service through professional, timely, and empathetic communication.
  • Build strong working relationships with insureds, brokers, claimants, attorneys, and internal stakeholders.
  • Communicate claim status, strategy, and exposure effectively to management and business partners.

What you'll need to succeed:

  • Bachelor's degree preferred or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 4 years + Commercial Auto Liability and/or Commercial General Liability claims handling experience.
  • Demonstrated experience handling bodily injury claims involving moderate to significant exposure.
  • Experience interpreting policy coverage and drafting coverage position letters, reservation of rights letters, and denial letters.
  • Experience managing both litigated and non-litigated claims.
  • Excellent analytical, investigative, and critical-thinking skills.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Active Property & Casualty Adjuster License preferred; must obtain required state licensing within six months of hire.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Litigation management experience.
  • Multi-state claims handling experience.
  • Experience handling serious bodily injury claims.
  • Professional designations such as AIC, CPCU, ARM, or SCLA.
  • Prior experience with commercial insurance carriers handling middle-market or large commercial accounts.

Job Description

Broker I, National Casualty

The National Casualty Practice is a premier team of casualty brokerage professionals with extensive experience in representing buyers of primary and umbrella/excess liability. We are looking to add a broker to our Primary Casualty team!

We are considering applicants in Dallas and Houston, Texas!

This is a hybrid role with at least three days a week in the office.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

How this opportunity is different

Our primary brokers are experts in their field and handle a variety of clients and program structures. You'll work closely with a diverse team of seasoned brokers, accounts executives, and risk analysts, each bringing a wealth of knowledge and experience to the table. This position offers you a unique opportunity to develop professionally, expand your expertise, and make an impact in the world of primary casualty. Thank you for your time and consideration.

What the day will look like

  • Thorough analysis of current risk transfer programs to include coverage and cost analysis and a graphical representation of the program.
  • Insurance program structure planning and design of alternatives.
  • Provide benchmarking analysis related to limits and coverage terms.
  • Prepare all marketplace insurance submissions, coordinate and conduct market meetings and negotiations as appropriate in coordination with Account Executives. May include some travel.
  • Finalize all quotes and complete a thorough comparison of program options as part of the client proposal presentation. Comparison to include changes in exposures, losses, collateral, coverage terms and conditions and cost of risk.
  • Serve as a primary or secondary market contact as assigned and in accordance with established policy.
  • As part of a team, you are expected to educate and advise fellow team members on coverage issues, markets, and related developments.
  • Serve as team member for Aon's broking library and periodically contribute to the library and related best practices.

Skills and experience that will lead to success

  • Casualty broker with 2+ years of experience working in primary placements and/or in casualty. Will be asked to work directly with clients as lead broker or secondary broker to build primary casualty programs, as well as participate on new business opportunities.
  • Attention to detail, ability to multi-task, exceptional organizational skills, ability to make and communicate difficult decisions.
  • An experienced primary casualty broker or underwriter with a solid understanding of and relationships with insurance company management and underwriting teams/personnel.
  • Strong written and communication skills necessary to communicate in a professional manner with clients and the marketplace.
  • A strong team player who understands the roles and responsibilities of other Aon professionals on the team, assumes responsibility for the timely delivery of a professional work product in accordance with assigned roles, and facilitates communication among team members.
  • Promote creativity in presenting new ideas and approaches for clients or prospects; promote a positive attitude in always trying to improve a program.

Education:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent years of industry experience.
  • Property and Casualty Brokers License is required (can be attained on the job)

For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances.

Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon's discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Job Description

Natural Resources Chief Commercial Officer

Aon is a global leader in providing insurance and risk management solutions within the natural resources industry. We design and place innovative risk mitigation, risk capital and alternative finance solutions to protect organizations of all sizes and complexity, empowering them to make better decisions. 

This leadership role is responsible for driving the success and growth of our business in the region by expanding revenue through sales leadership, ensuring strong client satisfaction in partnership with the Natural Resources Leader, developing a cohesive and high-performing local leadership team focused on growth, and planning and managing the sales pipeline across Natural Resources.

This is a hybrid role that requires working onsite for 2-3 days a week from a local Aon office.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

  • Drive Aon's US Natural Resources growth plan prioritizing growth of core businesses and leads execution of growth priorities, and works with N. America Executive team to deliver results
  • Lead consistent execution of Global Standards; Growth Planning, Articulating Value, Client Feedback, Bid and Pursuit, and Client Outreach
  • Own revenue forecasting (with finance team support) and pipeline management
  • Collaborate with Natural Resources Leaders (Energy, Power & Renewables) to lead regional growth (4x US Regions: Northeast, South, Midwest, West) plans
  • Prioritize growth opportunities and allocate resources (people, marketing) for Natural Resources clients and prospects that address both market opportunities and unmet client needs
  • Develop Risk Capital (Commercial Risk + Reinsurance) opportunities to create new products, capacity and solutions across risk capital group
  • Participate in N. America and US Risk Capital Leadership groups and liaise with other Specialty CCO's (Construction, Transportation & Logistics, M&A, Credit Solutions)
  • Lead teams in managing and winning RFPs both offensive and defensive
  • Provide input and direction to Marketing to develop and understand industry aligned thematic client needs to drive marketing and sales, ensuring activity is prioritized according to agreed US revenue generating opportunities and quality standards
  • Develop industry symposiums, client councils, product and capability demonstrations
  • Guide Strategy and Innovation Group to identify and prioritize opportunities for product development and new business growth
  • Use professional network to personally develop business - individual sales
  • Represent Natural Resources Practice
  • Maintain key relationships with Aon broking centers and global partners
  • Recruit broking and account management talent to the firm
  • Maintain and develop market relationships with key stakeholders

How this opportunity is different

We offer a collaborative work environment, opportunities for career growth, and a commitment to celebrating successes at every level. If you're a dynamic leader who thrives in a fast-paced and results-oriented environment, we invite you to join our team and make a lasting impact.

Skills and experience that will lead to success

  • Required Natural Resources Insurance knowledge within a brokerage/carrier or equivalent experience
  • 10+ years proven experience in a leadership role within the Natural Resources industry, with a track record of driving financial performance and operational success.
  • Strong understanding of budgeting, forecasting, P&L management, and financial reporting.
  • Exceptional talent management skills within multiple locations, including recruiting, performance management, and developing high-performing teams.
  • Strong client-facing and relationship management abilities, with a focus on long-term partnerships.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and implement strategic initiatives and manage growth effectively.
  • Knowledge of Natural Resources industry trends, challenges, and best practices.
  • Excellent communication, leadership, and problem-solving skills.

Job Description

North America Health Chief Actuary

This is a hybrid role with the flexibility to work both virtually and from any Aon office.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

The NA Health Chief Actuary sets the strategic direction for actuarial and financial services across U.S. Health and partners closely with Health leadership to advance business objectives and support profitable growth. The Chief Actuary serves as one of Aon's senior authorities on healthcare financial trends, regulatory developments, and industry dynamics, providing thought leadership internally and externally while ensuring actuarial insights are translated into commercially relevant solutions for clients. The role also drives change aligned to the Target Operating Model (TOM).

  • People & Talent
    • Embed commercial discipline in talent and resource decisions, ensuring the team's capabilities and capacity support revenue growth, client retention, and margin objectives.
    • Ensure staffing model aligns with client needs and profitability objectives, in partnership with client leaders and Health leadership.
    • Define career paths and capabilities that support talent retention, succession, and long‑term organizational health.
    • Lead and develop the client-facing Actuarial and Financial team, fostering a high-performing culture grounded in accountability, collaboration, and continuous development.
    • Ensure risk mitigation through peer review, actuarial credentialing, best practices, and continuing education.
  • Industry Engagement & Thought Leadership
    • Serve as Aon's senior authority on actuarial trends and healthcare financial trends, including employer and regulatory impacts.
    • Translate complex healthcare data and market dynamics into clear, actionable insights for clients, colleagues, and the broader market.
    • Monitor regulatory, industry, and marketplace developments to inform strategic decision‑making and external positioning.
    • Deliver external, market-facing representation of Aon's actuarial findings, recommendations, and points-of-view.
  • Actuarial & Financial Analysis and Strategic Client Consulting
    • Set and oversee actuarial and financial strategy supporting client healthcare, financial, and broking decision‑making.
    • Lead or oversee complex actuarial and financial consulting engagements at scale, including large employers, insurers, and high‑risk client situations.
    • Partner with client leaders to identify opportunities where actuarial and financial insights can strengthen client relationships, expand solutions, and contribute to profitable growth.
    • In partnership with Analytics, shape and govern tools and models required to deliver market leading actuarial and financial consulting services.

  • Innovation and Product/Solution Development

    • Collaborate with cross-functional leaders to support product and solution development, commercialization, and strategic initiatives.
    • Guide commercialization of new or enhanced actuarial solutions by connecting market needs, client value, delivery feasibility, and financial return.

Job Description

Are you a surety professional who thrives at the intersection of client service, underwriting strategy, and operational execution? Join a high-performing team and take on a meaningful role managing and delivering surety bond solutions for many clients!

Partners closely with clients to facilitate timely issuance of surety obligations. Reports to the regional Surety Operations leader. (Director or Team Lead).

  • Operates with a high degree of autonomy and judgment across complex or strategically significant accounts and in dealing with markets.
  • Takes primary accountability for handling selected key accounts, including coordination of large bond programs and sophisticated underwriting submissions.
  • Possesses strong, in-depth knowledge of surety bonds, including contract and commercial surety, indemnity structures, and market dynamics.
  • Serves as a technical lead within the team; assists in training, mentoring, and developing internal team, and contributes to improvement in execution initiatives.

  • Collaborates daily with clients on complex needs. Completes Consents of Surety, Prequalification Letters, Riders, and other client required obligations per State requirements.   • Maintains appropriate Producer license
  • Is proficient in all required technology platforms, including AonBondLink, Bridge, and Outlook, and utilizes these systems to manage data, analyze bond portfolios, and support decision-making.

Education and licensing requirements: A Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience is preferred for this position. Maintain Notary Public designation and hold the appropriate Property and Casualty license.

  • BA/BS or equivalent experience preferred
  • Seven plus years of entertainment industry and product line experience

  • P&C Insurance License required

Summary:

Are you a strategic employee benefits professional who enjoys building trusted client relationships and influencing business decisions? As an Employee Benefits Consultant, you'll serve as the primary advisor for a portfolio of clients, helping employers design, manage, and optimize their employee benefits programs. You'll lead client strategy, renewal planning, and ongoing consulting initiatives while partnering with internal teams to deliver outstanding service! This role blends relationship management, benefits expertise, financial analysis, and problem-solving, offering the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on both client success and business growth. This position is ideally based in Austin, Texas, where team members participate in a hybrid work environment that balances in-person collaboration with flexibility. However, we are open to considering exceptional candidates outside the market for a fully remote arrangement.

Key Responsibilities:

Client Management

  • Responsible for ongoing client satisfaction. Ensure clients receive timely and effective solutions to their needs, fostering long-term relationships.
  • Be accountable to retain clients, ensuring their continued satisfaction and loyalty. Implement strategies to maintain high client retention rates and address any issues promptly.
  • Focus on growing current clients, making sure their needs are fulfilled and looking for opportunities to expand. Absorb new clients into the book, providing them with exceptional service and support.
  • Serve as the main strategic point of contact, addressing their needs and concerns. Provide clients with consistent and reliable support, ensuring their satisfaction and loyalty.

Strategic Planning

  • Take charge of accounts within the book of business, making strategic decisions to optimize benefits for clients. Develop and implement innovative approaches to enhance client benefits and satisfaction.
  • Identify and drive opportunities for client expansion, exploring new benefit options and solutions. Proactively seek ways to improve client offerings and add value to their benefit plans.

Financial Management

  • Be responsible for running a book of $500k-5 million dollars of annual revenue. Ensure financial targets are met and optimize revenue streams through effective client management.

Team Collaboration

  • Collaborating with the Account Manager Team on annual execution of core work, ensuring all deliverables are met.
  • Coordinate and lead all aspects of the completion of key projects and initiatives throughout the year.
  • Collaborate closely with the Managing Consultant and Producer to ensure the success of each account. Work together to align strategies and goals, ensuring seamless service delivery.

Industry Knowledge

  • Stay informed about industry trends, new strategies, and cutting-edge solutions. Continuously update knowledge to provide clients with the latest and most effective benefit options.
  • Provide thought leadership and innovative solutions to clients, positioning the company as a leader in the industry. Share insights and expertise to help clients navigate complex benefit landscapes.

Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities:

  • Strong understanding of benefits administration, industry trends, and carrier products and services.
  • Proven track record to manage client relationships and anticipate client needs.
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and oral.
  • Advanced Excel and PowerPoint skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Passion for developing and building strength and capabilities in a team.

Education and/or Experience:

  • 6+ years of experience in employee benefits or a related field. Preferably a bachelor's degree.

Certificates, Licenses, Registration:

  • Life & Health Insurance License

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. The employee is occasionally required to stand and walk. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and distance vision.

What We Offer:

We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $90,000 – $150,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Principal Duties and Responsibilities / Essential Functions:

Lead the platform architecture and build

  • Own the design, build, and ongoing maintenance of our Microsoft Fabric medallion architecture (Bronze → Silver → Gold), ensuring data flows optimally from raw ingestion through conformed, analytics-ready models.
  • Make and document key architectural decisions around ingestion patterns, storage, the serving layer, orchestration, and performance — balancing speed, reliability, and cost.
  • Establish the engineering practices that keep the platform healthy as it scales: version control, testing, CI/CD, monitoring, and documentation.

Lead and grow the team

  • Guide a small team of data engineers — setting coding and design standards, running code reviews, and unblocking day-to-day work.
  • Mentor engineers and help grow their technical skills, giving the team a clear sense of how “good” is defined.
  • Help shape hiring and team structure as the function grows.

Build and maintain the data pipelines

  • Develop and operate ingestion pipelines from multiple sources — pharmacy claims, eligibility, formulary, contract data, rebate and actuarial data, and public reference APIs (e.g., NADAC, NCPDP, CMS, 340B).
  • Normalize and conform data across differing PBM file specifications, formularies, and claims layouts so that downstream models are consistent and trustworthy.
  • Design and evolve the conformed data model and star schema that serve as the analytical source of truth.

Serve the business

  • Ensure the platform reliably feeds downstream consumers: Power BI, Excel reporting, internal web applications, and AI/Copilot-ready data services.
  • Serve as a point for complex reporting and data issues, guiding to resolution across reporting and data teams
  • Own data quality, governance, lineage, performance, and cost optimization end to end.
  • Partner with the platform architect, analytics, clinical, and product teams to align the technical roadmap with business and client priorities, and translate ambiguous requirements into concrete data solutions.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional leaders to prioritize initiatives and allocate resources

Minimum Requirements for Education, Experience, and Certifications/Licenses:

  • 7+ years in data engineering, including 2+ years leading, mentoring, or acting as tech lead for other engineers.
  • Deep experience building lakehouse / medallion architectures. Microsoft Fabric strongly preferred; comparable experience with Azure Synapse, Databricks, or similar platforms will be considered.
  • Strong SQL and hands-on proficiency in Python and/or PySpark for large-scale data transformation.
  • Dimensional modeling expertise — you can design and maintain star schemas that hold up as reporting needs grow.
  • BI analytics fluency, including an understanding of the semantic/serving layer that makes BI performant and trustworthy.
  • A track record of taming messy data — ingesting and conforming heterogeneous sources and file formats into clean, reliable models.
  • Solid engineering fundamentals — data governance, data quality frameworks, and CI/CD for data pipelines.
  • Strong communication skills — able to explain technical tradeoffs to non-technical stakeholders and collaborate across teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with pharmacy, PBM, healthcare claims, or payer data.
  • Familiarity with pharmacy data standards (NCPDP, claims file layouts) and healthcare reference data.
  • Experience enabling AI/Copilot or MCP-based data access on top of a data platform.
  • Broader Azure ecosystem experience (Azure SQL, data pipelines, security/RBAC, cost management).
  • Experience standing up a data platform or engineering function in an early or growth-stage environment.

What We Offer:

Job Description

Representations & Warranties M&A Insurance- Vice President

The San Francisco office of Aon is seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Vice President to join its market-leading M&A and Transaction Solutions team. This is an outstanding opportunity for a corporate attorney with 3-5 years of M&A experience to transition from private practice into a client-facing advisory role supporting some of the most sophisticated private equity and strategic clients in the market.

This role is a hybrid role, with the flexibility of working both virtually and form our San Francisco office.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

How this opportunity is different

As a Vice President you will work alongside senior and junior brokers, underwriters, private equity sponsors, corporate clients and leading law firms to structure and place Representations & Warranties Insurance (RWI) on domestic and cross-border transactions. We will provide hands-on experience, industry-leading training and mentorship in a collaborative environment.

This position offers a broad range of responsibilities and will allow candidates to remain deeply involved in complex corporate transactions while developing commercial negotiation and client relationship skills in a fast-paced M&A environment.

We value continued growth and learning, collaboration and pride in delivering exceptional work. If you are looking to take the next step in your career and gain hands on MA& transaction insurance experience, we encourage you to reach out and explore this opportunity!

Key Responsibilities:

  • Advise private equity sponsors, strategic buyers and their advisors on transactional risk insurance solutions.
  • Review purchase agreements, disclosure schedules, diligence reports and transaction documentation to identify underwriting considerations and coverage issues.
  • Coordinate the underwriting process with leading insurance carriers from initial marketing through policy binding.
  • Analyze legal and commercial risks associated with mergers and acquisitions across a broad range of industries.
  • Draft and negotiate policy terms and facilitate discussions between insurers and transaction parties.
  • Manage multiple transactions simultaneously while meeting demanding deal timelines.
  • Build and maintain relationships with law firms, investment bankers, private equity firms and corporate clients.
  • Support business development initiatives and participate in client presentations, industry conferences and educational seminars.
  • Collaborate with colleagues across Aon's global Transaction Solutions platform on domestic and international transactions.

Qualifications:

The ideal candidate must have a strong academic record, excellent analytical and oral communication skills. In addition, the candidate must be a proven self-starter willing to take on a good deal of responsibility with the ability to problem solve and advise clients involved in complex transactions.

  • J.D. from an accredited law school.
  • 3-5 years of experience practicing corporate/M&A law at a nationally recognized law firm.
  • Strong experience negotiating and drafting acquisition agreements and supporting private M&A transactions.
  • Effective presentation, reporting and interpersonal skills.
  • Excellent analytical skills with exceptional attention to detail.
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment while managing multiple active transactions as part of a team and with minimal direction.
  • Strong commercial judgment and an interest in developing relationships within the TS team and wider Aon, as well as developing trust and confidence with clients as well as carrier partners.
  • Collaborative, proactive and entrepreneurial mindset.
  • Skilled in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Ability to attain a Broker's License within 90 days of employment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience representing private equity sponsors and strategic buyers.
  • Exposure to cross-border transactions.
  • Interest in insurance, risk management or financial services.

Why Join Aon Transaction Solutions?

Aon's Transaction Solutions practice is one of the industry's leading advisors on transactional risk insurance. Our professionals work on many of the largest and most complex M&A transactions globally, partnering with premier private equity firms, Fortune 500 companies and top-tier law firms.

This position provides the opportunity to leverage your legal training while building a long-term career in a dynamic, client-facing advisory business that combines law, finance, insurance and M&A strategy. You will gain:

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS & RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Receives claims, confirms policy coverage and acknowledgment of the claim
