  • Investigates claims and handles Auto and/or General Liability claims
  • Establishes reserves and authorizes payments within reserving authority limits
  • Communicates claim status with the customer, claimant, and client
  • Adheres to client and carrier guidelines and participates in claims review as needed
  • Collaborates with team members on more complex or problematic claims as necessary
  • Additional duties as assigned

KNOWLEDGE & SKILLS:

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to learn rapidly to develop knowledge and understanding of claims practice
  • Ability to identify, analyze and solve problems
  • Computer proficiency and technical aptitude with the ability to utilize Microsoft Office including Excel spreadsheets
  • Strong interpersonal, time management, and organizational skills
  • Ability to meet or exceed performance expectations
  • Ability to work both independently and within a team environment

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE:

  • Five (5) or more years' experience handling General Liability claims, including high exposure and/or litigated claims
  • Two (2) or more years' experience handling Auto Liability claims
  • Bachelor's degree or a combination of education and related experience
  • Current Adjuster's License in state of operation is required
  • Multi-State license is preferred
  • Municipality experience is a plus

PAY RANGE:

CorVel uses a market based approach to pay and our salary ranges may vary depending on your location. Pay rates are established taking into account the following factors: federal, state, and local minimum wage requirements, the geographic location differential, job-related skills, experience, qualifications, internal employee equity, and market conditions. Our ranges may be modified at any time.

For leveled roles (I, II, III, Senior, Lead, etc.) new hires may be slotted into a different level, either up or down, based on assessment during interview process taking into consideration experience, qualifications, and overall fit for the role. The level may impact the salary range and these adjustments would be clarified during the offer process.

Pay Range: $15.61 - $23.82 per hour

A list of our benefit offerings can be found on our CorVel website: CorVel Careers | Opportunities in Risk Management

ABOUT CORVEL:

CorVel, a certified Great Place to Work® Company, is a national provider of industry-leading risk management solutions for the workers' compensation, auto, health and disability management industries. CorVel was founded in 1987 and has been publicly traded on the NASDAQ stock exchange since 1991. Who We Are:

Wealthspire is a leading wealth management, retirement advisory, and business management firm serving individuals, families, endowments, and institutions across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. We provide a comprehensive platform that brings together wealth management, institutional consulting, business management, family office, and retirement plan advisory services—empowering clients to navigate complexity with clarity and confidence.

With over $580B in assets under advisement, and more than 1,200 employees across 40+ offices, we deliver insights and solutions grounded in deep research, advanced technology, and decades of expertise. Wealthspire Advisors LLC, Fiducient Advisors LLC, Wealthspire Retirement, LLC, dba Wealthspire Retirement Advisory, and certain other affiliates are separately registered investment advisers.

Client Services is the connective tissue of the firm. Our CS professionals own the client relationship end to end, partnering daily with advisors and their teams to deliver a seamless, high-quality experience for every client we serve.

We are building a CS leadership team that holds the standard for service excellence across the organization. That means developing and managing CS professionals who take ownership, setting and enforcing service standards, and working closely with advisory teams, compliance, technology, and data operations to ensure clients receive informed, consistent service at every touchpoint.

We are looking for experienced client services professionals who bring deep operational knowledge, strong people leadership, and a genuine commitment to the client experience. If that describes you, we want to hear from you.

What We Look For:

Client Experience and Service Standards

  • Commitment to delivering a consistent, high-quality client experience across every interaction and touchpoint
  • Ability to set, communicate, and enforce service standards with teams, holding staff accountable to the client experience the firm expects
  • Understanding of what clients need at each stage of the relationship and how CS professionals can own that experience proactively
  • Track record of building teams that take ownership rather than execute tasks, with the judgment to act on behalf of advisors and clients independently

Advisor and Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Ability to build strong working relationships with advisors and their teams, serving as a trusted partner on client service matters
  • Experience collaborating across functions, including investment, compliance, technology, and operations, to resolve issues and deliver on client needs
  • Comfort representing Client Services in cross-functional settings and communicating the team's work, standards, and needs to leadership and partners
  • Skill in managing competing priorities across advisory teams while maintaining consistent service delivery standards
  • Experience supporting advisor integrations or onboarding, including familiarity with the operational workflows, timelines, and coordination required to bring an advisory team onto a new platform and service model

Operational Expertise

  • Expert-level knowledge of custodial platforms: Schwab, Fidelity, and Pershing, including account structures, transaction processing, and escalation management
  • Deep understanding of RIA client service operations: account onboarding, money movement, and regulatory requirements
  • Familiarity with alternative investment subscription document processing, including outside manager requirements, account eligibility, and access across custodial and private investment portals
  • Proficiency in Salesforce and CRM systems, including workflow design and reporting

Leadership and People Development

  • Demonstrated experience managing client services teams with accountability for performance, development, and service delivery standards
  • Ability to develop managers and frontline staff, through structured coaching, feedback, and individual development planning
  • Give direct feedback, and address performance issues constructively
  • Track record of building accountability structures and holding teams to consistent standards across locations or functions
  • Collaborative working style with the credibility to influence peers and cross-functional partners without direct authority.
  • Experience building and delivering training programs for client services staff

Strategic and Operational Thinking

  • Ability to identify systemic gaps, design solutions, and drive implementation across teams or regions
  • Project management capability: experience running structured, multi-phase programs with defined milestones, owners, and reporting cadences
  • Data-driven approach to performance management: able to interpret metrics, identify trends, and translate findings into action
  • Experience contributing to or leading firm-wide initiatives that required cross-functional coordination
  • Experience owning or contributing to an operational playbook, including building integration frameworks, training curricula, process templates, and handoff standards that scale across engagements
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent initiatives with overlapping timelines, maintaining quality and accountability across each

Communication and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to represent Client Services to advisors, leadership, and external partners
  • Comfort with difficult conversations at the team, peer, and senior stakeholder level
  • Ability to present complex operational topics clearly and with authority
  • Experience engaging founders, senior advisors, or executive stakeholders with credibility, communicating the CS model, service standards, and integration expectations in a way that builds confidence and trust

Qualifications:

  • Minimum 10 years of experience in financial services with significant client service operational expertise
  • Minimum 5 years of people management experience, including demonstrated ability to manage managers and oversee teams across multiple locations or functions
  • Track record of leading strategic initiatives and driving process improvement across a client services function
  • Expert proficiency across major custodial platforms and CRM systems required
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent directly related experience; advanced degree preferred)

What We Offer:

Wealthspire is proud to offer a comprehensive rewards package that includes a competitive salary, paid time off and holidays, a 401(k) plan with company match, exclusive discount programs, and robust health and wellness benefits. Our culture is rooted in putting people first - nurturing lasting relationships with our employees and fostering a workplace where everyone feels supported and valued.

The base salary range for this position is $130,000 to $175,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives.

Posting Description

Who We Are:

NFP, an Aon company, is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. Position Overview

NFP is seeking an experienced Account Executive, Broker (P&C) for its South Central region. This position is responsible for broking new and renewal business for a varied portfolio of energy and non-energy clients, including middle-market and large, complex accounts. The broker will handle all aspects of the placement from strategy development through policy delivery, ensuring client needs are promptly and accurately addressed, deadlines are met, and service standards are achieved.

This is a full-time, hybrid position based in Austin or Houston, Texas. Regular in-office presence is required to support collaboration and strong partnerships across teams.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

  • Lead marketing for a book of energy and non-energy P&C clients in the South Central region, partnering with account teams and clients to align on strategy, timelines, and execution.
  • Execute national and regional broking strategies to support optimal client outcomes, retention, and profitable growth.
  • Develop strategies for at-risk accounts and identify book-of-business optimization opportunities.

Operational Process

  • Drive placement strategy and execution, including client needs assessment, program design, carrier negotiation, and marketing execution.
  • Coordinate complete and timely submissions, respond to carrier questions, analyze quotes, and present clear recommendations to clients.
  • Determine appropriate coverage based on the client's risk profile, business objectives, and risk appetite.
  • Develop creative solutions for complex placement scenarios and manage the placement cycle in accordance with NFP's service standards and timelines.
  • Use NFP's strategic carriers, panels, and preferred wholesalers to secure appropriate coverage, terms, and pricing.
  • Prepare proposals, coverage and policy comparisons, and related client materials; review binders and policies for accuracy.
  • Use data and analytics to provide meaningful program insight and support informed placement decisions.
  • Support prospect activity, retention, and appropriate cross-sell and up-sell opportunities.

Talent Development

  • Promote consistency in broking standards and client delivery across the region.
  • Educate account executives and account managers on market dynamics, carrier trends, and how those factors affect clients and placement strategy.
  • Partner with account executives, account managers, and service teams to resolve client needs promptly.

Carrier Relationships

  • Build and maintain trusted relationships with carrier and wholesale partners to enhance placement outcomes and market access.
  • Stay current on carrier appetites, market dynamics, and terms and conditions to ensure the right markets are approached for each risk.
  • Share relevant market insight with clients and internal partners to support informed risk-transfer decisions.
  • Operate as a steward of the broader NFP while engaging in the marketplace.

Qualifications

  • Five or more years of commercial P&C broking experience with middle-market, large-account, or similarly complex business.
  • Demonstrated success leading marketing discussions, negotiating with carriers and wholesalers, and managing complex new and renewal placements.
  • Strong technical knowledge and creativity in developing effective property and casualty solutions.
  • Strong client-facing, carrier-facing, communication, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • TX P&C insurance license required.
  • Energy industry experience is preferred but not required; candidates with strong non-energy commercial P&C experience will also be considered.
  • Experience with Epic, the agency management system, is a plus but not required.
  • Ability to travel as required for client, prospect, and industry events.

What We Offer

We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. Job.JobTitle: Sr. Director, Internal Consulting, Op Model Transformation
Job.JobDescription:
Job Description

We are seeking a Sr. Director of Internal Consulting to lead central initiatives for Aon. The role starts with building and carrying out a multi-year strategic overhaul of our Operating Model. Reporting to the leadership team of Aon Business Services (ABS), this role leads internal consulting and program management teams. It involves crafting, orchestrating, and scaling the transformation of the enterprise operating model at Aon. The goal is to improve how we deliver value to clients, colleagues, and other interested parties. This role will engage with senior leaders across Solution Lines, Regions, and Functions. It will also lead a cross‑functional group of internal advisors, project managers, and subject matter experts to deliver measurable performance outcomes.

This role is open to a Virtual or Hybrid colleague based in Central or Eastern Time Zone.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Vision

  • Partner with ABS leadership as well as business leaders, key collaborators, and cross-functional partners to advance the vision, objectives, and scope related to operating model transformation efforts
  • Translate strategic priorities into a clear transformation roadmap with defined business outcomes, benchmarks, and value realization targets
  • Apply structured consulting methodologies (e.g., problem framing, analytical reasoning, benchmarking, argument development) to advise recommendations
  • Develop and validate arguments for operating model changes, including financial, operational, and qualitative benefits

Operating Model Design & Alignment

  • Lead the end‑to‑end diagnostic, build and transition of the target operating model across Aon's Business Units, geographic areas, and departments
  • Translate enterprise strategy into detailed organizational framework components, including capabilities, organizational structure, roles and responsibilities, governance models, and cross functional interaction patterns
  • Be responsible for phased implementation, including pilots, scaling strategies, and stabilization, ensuring alignment with regional and solution line needs
  • Build and maintain operating model blueprints, ensuring all components (capability models, interaction models, RACIs, team structures, decision rights, important metrics) integrate across the enterprise

Stakeholder Engagement & Program Leadership

  • Act as a trusted advisor to senior executives. Provide insight on opportunities, trade-offs, and risks related to the operating model. Ensure agreement and engagement in strategy and roadmap.
  • Shape and deliver a compelling change narrative that articulates the “why,” “what,” and “how” of the transformation for different audiences
  • Work closely with executive sponsors and the PMO to establish and maintain robust governance, decision‑making, and blocking issue mechanisms
  • Partner with Change & Communications teams to define implications of design changes, highlight required behavior shifts, and identify points of resistance or adoption needs
  • Facilitate executive and working‑level forums to align decisions, resolve conflicts, and maintain momentum

People Leadership & Capability Building

  • Recruit, develop, and mentor a high‑performing team members with capabilities in strategy, transformation, operations, change, and analytics
  • Lead a team of internal consultants and business analysts to diagnose current‑state challenges, define solutions, and support implementation
  • Build consulting capabilities within the broader organization by sharing methodologies, tools, and guidelines
  • Promote a culture of collaboration, transparency, and continuous improvement
  • Bring together and embed lessons learned into subsequent waves of organizational build changes

Skills and experience that will lead to success

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Operations, Technology, or related field; advanced degree (MBA or equivalent) strongly preferred
  • Proven experience in management consulting, internal strategy/consulting or equivalent internal consulting function, including significant experience at the Director level or above
  • Demonstrated experience leading sophisticated, multi‑workstream operating model or large‑scale transformation programs in a global, matrixed organization, including design, process transition and governance framework setup
  • Experience working in or with professional services, insurance, or financial services environments is highly desirable

Skills & Competencies

  • Demonstrated ability to build and coach high‑performing, complementary teams and work effectively across cultures and geographies
  • Ability to operate as a generalist across strategy development, organizational framework building, and execution support
  • Ability to roll up the sleeves and problem solve
  • Strong strategic and conceptual abilities; able to connect enterprise strategy to detailed building and implementation
  • Expertise in building operating frameworks, process re‑engineering, and organizational development
  • Excellent collaborator management and influencing skills, including experience engaging C‑suite and senior executives
  • Outstanding ability to present complex topics clearly and build engaging narratives and materials
  • Strong analytical and problem‑solving capabilities; comfortable with data, financial modeling, and performance metrics
  • Growth mindset toward emerging technologies, with the ability to incorporate AI into daily work and support others in embracing new digital tools with confidence and ease. Proficiency in MS

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $92,000 to $130,000 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Chicago, IL
  • Experience: 3+ years

About this job

Engineer and support Privileged Access Management solutions with focus on CyberArk Cloud. Work with engineering and architecture teams to onboard applications, maintain access policies, automate processes and deliver secure, scalable identity and access solutions.

Good fit if you have 3+ years of PAM or identity security experience and hands-on CyberArk implementation background.

Full job description

Job Description

Aon is looking for a Privileged Access Management (PAM) Engineer to help strengthen and evolve our identity and privileged-access security capabilities.

In this role, you will engineer, implement and support PAM solutions, with a strong focus on CyberArk Cloud. You will work with engineering, architecture and business partners to onboard applications, maintain access policies, automate processes and deliver secure, scalable solutions.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one engaged team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

  • Engineer, implement and support security technologies focused on Privileged Access Management.
  • Implement and integrate PAM solutions, with a strong focus on CyberArk Cloud, and support endpoint privilege capabilities using technologies such as BeyondTrust or CyberArk EPM.
  • Onboard applications, accounts and credentials into PAM platforms while maintaining appropriate access controls and security policies.
  • Maintain and enhance CyberArk policies and support endpoint privilege policies for workstation environments.
  • Contribute to the architectural design of access controls, user entitlements, application credentials and user access policies.
  • Partner with architecture and engineering teams to advance the Identity and Access Management strategy and related roadmap.
  • Develop automation using scripting languages such as PowerShell or Python to improve privileged-access processes and capabilities.
  • Configure and support API or programmatic access to managed credentials.
  • Troubleshoot PAM, authentication and access issues, identify root causes and implement practical solutions.
  • Use relevant security and SIEM data to support troubleshooting, monitoring and informed decision-making.
  • Keep technical documentation current as platforms, configurations and environments evolve.
  • Contribute to new PAM capabilities and product features while working within an Agile delivery environment.
  • Communicate technical concepts clearly and collaborate effectively with engineering, architecture and business partners.

How this opportunity is different

You will help protect critical systems and identities by improving how privileged access is designed, managed and secured. Through thoughtful engineering, automation and collaboration, you will help make PAM capabilities more secure, scalable and effective for the teams that rely on them.

Skills and experience that will lead to success

  • 3+ years of relevant experience in privileged access, identity security or related security engineering.
  • Hands-on experience implementing, developing or supporting CyberArk, with experience in CyberArk Cloud strongly preferred for this role.
  • Experience with PAM operational activities such as credential onboarding, access administration, policy configuration and API-based credential access.
  • Experience with endpoint privilege management technologies such as BeyondTrust EPM or CyberArk EPM.
  • Hands-on experience supporting Windows and/or Linux infrastructure.
  • Working knowledge of Active Directory, including users, computers, groups, Group Policy and trusts.
  • Understanding of broader Identity and Access Management concepts such as authentication, access certification and public key infrastructure.
  • Experience developing automation with scripting tools such as PowerShell, Python or comparable languages.
  • Familiarity with SIEM technologies and querying security data.
  • Understanding of web traffic and the ability to troubleshoot authentication flows.
  • Experience contributing to technical projects in an Agile environment.
  • Ability to create clear technical documentation and communicate effectively with technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience with both CyberArk and BeyondTrust technologies.
  • Exposure to emerging privileged-access use cases involving non-human identities (NHI) or AI-related security scenarios.
  • Broader experience across Identity and Access Management platforms and security technologies.

Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent years of relevant industry experience.

Full job description

Job Description

IAM Engineer- Authentication

Are you passionate about building secure, seamless authentication experiences? Do you enjoy solving complex identity challenges while partnering across technology and the business?

Join Aon and help design, enhance, and support identity and access management solutions that strengthen security while creating a reliable experience for colleagues and clients.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one engaged team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

In this role, you will help design, implement, and support authentication capabilities across Aon's identity environment. You will partner with technology and business stakeholders to develop practical solutions that balance security, reliability, and user experience.

You will:

  • Design, integrate, test, and support Identity and Access Management (IAM) authentication solutions, with a focus on Single Sign-On (SSO) and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).
  • Partner with technology, security, and business stakeholders to understand authentication needs, recommend appropriate IAM patterns, and guide solution implementation.
  • Configure and maintain authentication platforms such as Okta and Microsoft Entra, including policies, workflows, and integrations.
  • Help ensure authentication platforms remain secure, reliable, current, and well supported through effective monitoring, maintenance, and patching.
  • Design and refine SSO and MFA policies and controls that strengthen security while supporting a seamless user experience.
  • Develop and extend identity-platform capabilities using REST APIs, JSON, and customizable settings.
  • Analyze authentication and authorization logs to diagnose issues, identify root causes, and implement effective solutions.
  • Create clear IAM documentation, architecture diagrams, and process flows that support solution design and ongoing operations.
  • Identify opportunities to improve authentication controls, processes, and platform capabilities while balancing security, reliability, and user experience.

How this opportunity is different

This role gives you the opportunity to work at the intersection of identity, cybersecurity, technology, and user experience. Your work will directly contribute to protecting Aon's technology environment while enabling secure and reliable access for colleagues and clients.

You will serve as an IAM subject-matter resource and trusted partner, collaborating across teams to solve complex authentication challenges and continually improve identity capabilities.

Skills and experience that will lead to success

  • Professional experience designing, implementing, or supporting IAM solutions.
  • Experience implementing and integrating SSO and MFA technologies for workforce and/or external user environments, including platforms such as Okta or Microsoft Entra.
  • Working knowledge of identity and authentication standards and protocols such as SAML, OAuth/OIDC, SCIM, LDAP, RADIUS, and Kerberos.
  • Experience analyzing authentication and authorization logs and troubleshooting complex identity issues.
  • Working experience with REST APIs and JSON.
  • Familiarity with applicable security and compliance frameworks, such as GDPR, SOX, ISO 27001, and SOC 2.
  • Analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify root causes and develop practical solutions.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts to varied audiences.
  • Ability to collaborate across technology and business teams, manage competing priorities, and contribute effectively in a team environment.
  • Ability to create clear technical documentation, diagrams, and process flows.
  • 3 + years of relevant professional experience designing and implementing IAM solutions, including experience with SSO and MFA technologies.
  • Equivalent combinations of relevant experience, skills, and education may also be considered

Education

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent relevant industry experience.

Summary:We are seeking a strategic and hands-on Compensation Manager to lead the design, execution, and governance of our compensation programs. This role will partner closely with HR and business leaders to ensure competitive, equitable, and data-driven pay practices that support organizational growth and talent strategy.

What You'll Do

Own Compensation Strategy & Program Design

  • Partner with the CPO to define and evolve the company's compensation philosophy and pay practices.
  • Design, implement, and continuously refine compensation structures including base pay, incentive plans, bonus programs, and special pay arrangements.
  • Develop and maintain salary structures, pay grades, and job architecture frameworks.
  • Conduct market benchmarking and external salary survey analysis to ensure competitiveness and alignment with business strategy.
  • Evaluate and recommend enhancements to compensation programs based on workforce trends, market conditions, and organizational growth.

Lead Annual Compensation Cycles

  • Own the end-to-end annual merit, bonus, and promotion cycles — including planning, modeling, budgeting, system configuration (Workday), manager enablement, and final approvals.
  • Develop compensation modeling scenarios and provide executive-ready analytics and recommendations.
  • Ensure timely and accurate implementation of approved changes within HRIS and payroll systems.
  • Partner with Finance on budget alignment and accrual forecasting.

Ensure Pay Equity & Governance

  • Conduct internal equity analyses to prevent compression and ensure fairness across functions and levels.
  • Analyze compensation data to identify disparities, trends, and risk areas; provide data-driven recommendations.
  • Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, including pay transparency requirements.
  • Maintain documentation and governance standards for compensation processes and decisions.
  • Establish internal controls to mitigate risk and ensure consistency in pay decisions.

Support Talent Acquisition & Offer Governance

  • Partner with Talent Acquisition and HR Business Partners to evaluate offers, sign-on bonuses, and promotional increases.
  • Review and approve compensation packages to ensure alignment with internal equity and market positioning.
  • Provide guidance on job leveling, salary bands, and offer strategy.
  • Verify compensation-related components of offer letters and ensure accurate system entry.

Oversee Compensation-Related Payroll & Adjustments

  • Partner with Payroll to ensure accurate processing of compensation changes, where applicable.
  • Review payroll data to validate compensation-related changes prior to final disbursement (e.g, mass merit uploads)
  • Collaborate with HR and Legal on severance modeling and payment processing.

Deliver Data-Driven Insights

  • Develop executive-level reporting and dashboards related to compensation trends, budget utilization, pay equity, and workforce analytics.
  • Conduct scenario modeling to support workforce planning and strategic decision-making.
  • Maintain data integrity within Workday and ensure alignment between HRIS and payroll systems.

Drive Process Excellence & Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to streamline compensation workflows and enhance automation within Workday.
  • Develop SOPs and documentation to ensure consistency and audit readiness.
  • Stay current on compensation best practices, regulatory changes, and emerging market trends.
  • undefined

What You'll Need

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Finance, Business, or related field preferred.
  • 10+ years of progressive compensation experience, including ownership of compensation cycles.
  • Experience designing and managing salary structures and incentive programs.
  • Strong expertise in market benchmarking and salary survey analysis.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting pay equity and internal compression analyses.
  • Advanced analytical skills with strong Excel and data modeling capability.
  • Experience working within Workday Compensation module or similar HRIS platforms preferred.
  • Strong understanding of payroll processes and compensation compliance requirements.
  • Exceptional discretion and ability to manage highly confidential information.
  • Ability to operate independently as a function-of-one while influencing senior stakeholders.

Nice to Have:

  • CCP (Certified Compensation Professional)
  • PHR/SPHR or SHRM-CP/SCP

What We Offer:

Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others.

About this job

Support treasury and banking systems for Aon's North America operations, managing Kyriba configurations, system testing, and integrations. Role includes process automation, reporting and analytics development, and participation in treasury transformation initiatives.

Good fit if you have treasury or finance systems experience, know Treasury Management Systems like Kyriba, and understand internal controls and bank connectivity.

Full job description

Job Description

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

Treasury systems ownership and support

  • Act as the primary contact for day‑to‑day issues for Treasury and Banking applications for North America and support other team members with global issues.
  • Maintain system configurations, reference data, user profiles, roles, and permissions in accordance with internal controls and segregation‑of‑duties requirements.
  • Coordinate and perform system testing (unit, regression, and user acceptance testing) for upgrades, patches, new modules, and configuration changes.
  • Develop and maintain system documentation, user guides, training materials and job aids for Treasury and Finance users.

Process and control enhancement

  • Partner with Treasury operations, cash management, debt, investments and risk teams to understand business requirements and translate them into system and process solutions.
  • Identify opportunities to automate manual processes (e.g., bank statement processing, cash positioning, payments, intercompany settlements, forecasting) and improve data quality and control.
  • Support the design and execution of key controls around treasury system access, payments, interfaces, and reconciliations; assist with internal and external audit requests related to treasury systems.

Kyriba / banking connectivity and integrations

  • Support implementation and maintenance of bank connectivity (SWIFT, host‑to‑host, APIs) within Kyriba and related tools.
  • Monitor and help resolve issues with payment files, bank statements, and other interfaces between Kyriba, banks, ERP systems, and downstream applications.
  • Collaborate with IT and external vendors on integration design, testing, incident resolution, and enhancement work.

Reporting, analytics and data management

  • Build and maintain standard reports and dashboards in Kyriba and related tools to support cash visibility, liquidity management, and operational performance.
  • Assist in the production and enhancement of recurring Treasury reporting (e.g., daily cash positions, liquidity and investment reports, bank fee and account analytics).
  • Ensure data integrity across systems; identify and remediate data quality issues in master data (banks, accounts, entities, counterparties, instruments, etc.).

Projects and transformation

  • Support on Treasury and Finance transformation initiatives (e.g., new country roll‑outs, bank rationalization, payment factory implementations, netting solutions, system migrations).
  • Contribute to business case development and benefits tracking for treasury systems initiatives.
  • Stay current on Kyriba and market best practices and bring ideas forward to enhance Aon's Treasury technology and processes

Skills and experience that will lead to success

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, IT, or related field, or equivalent work experience.
  • Several years of experience in a corporate Treasury function and/or in systems/business analysis supporting finance/treasury processes.
  • Hands‑on experience with at least one Treasury Management System (TMS); familiarity with payment formats (SWIFT MT / ISO 20022), bank connectivity and standard treasury processes.
  • Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills with demonstrated ability to understand end‑to‑end processes and their technology enablers.
  • Solid understanding of internal controls, risk and compliance considerations in a Treasury environment.
  • Proficiency with Excel and comfort working with data from multiple systems.

Preferred

  • Direct, practical experience configuring or supporting Kyriba (e.g., core cash, payments, bank connectivity, cash forecasting, debt and investments modules).
  • Experience working in a large, global organization with complex banking and entity structures.
  • Exposure to ERP systems (such as SAP, Oracle, Workday, etc.) and integrations between TMS and ERP.
  • Experience participating in or leading system implementation, upgrade, or process‑reengineering projects.
  • Familiarity with basic scripting, data tools, or BI/reporting tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau, SQL) is a plus.

Key Competencies

  • Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to communicate clearly with both technical and non‑technical audiences.
  • High attention to detail and a control‑minded approach, with a focus on data quality and operational risk mitigation.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and deliver high‑quality work in a fast‑paced, global environment.
  • Collaborative team player who is comfortable working across functions, regions, and time zones.
  • Commitment to continuous improvement, learning, and leveraging data and technology to support better decisions.

Full job description

Job Description

The Organizational Change & Transformation Manager plays a meaningful role in enabling successful enterprise transformation by ensuring operating model changes are understood, adopted, and sustained. This role partners closely with Enterprise Transformation Planning & Execution Leads and Transformation Strategy Analysts to translate target-state designs into clear change, communication, and adoption strategies. The role applies structured change methodologies to assess impact, readiness, and resistance, and works with senior leaders and cross-functional teams to drive behavioral and capability shifts required to realize intended business outcomes.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world!

As an organization, we are united through trust as one engaged team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

Core Responsibilities

  • Apply a structured, enterprise-defined change management methodology to support operating model transformation initiatives end to end.
  • Conduct change impact and readiness assessments across capabilities, roles, processes, and governance to inform adoption strategies.
  • Partner with Enterprise Transformation Planning & Execution Leads to surface change implications, adoption risks, and sequencing considerations embedded in operating model designs.
  • Identify, assess, and proactively manage resistance by developing targeted mitigation, engagement, and reinforcement strategies.
  • Develop actionable change strategies, communication, and training plans aligned to enterprise milestones and workstream priorities.
  • Support senior leaders and workstream sponsors with tailored messaging, talking points, and engagement approaches to reinforce change objectives.
  • Define success metrics for adoption and behavior change; monitor progress and recommend corrective actions as needed.
  • Track change-related risks, issues, and dependencies; raise concerns with clear impact articulation and recommended paths forward..

Skills and experience that will lead to success

  • 7 or more years of proven experience leading change management efforts for large-scale, multi-workstream transformations.
  • Strong business insight with the ability to understand operating model build decisions and translate them into adoption implications.
  • Demonstrated ability to partner effectively with senior leaders, cross-functional collaborators, and transformation teams.
  • Exceptional communication skills, including executive-level presentations and concise, decision-ready materials.
  • Ability to influence without authority and align diverse collaborators around shared outcomes.
  • Experience developing change, communication, and training content using tools such as PowerPoint and Excel. MS Project, Azure DevOps and JIRA is a plus.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, including root-cause analysis of adoption challenges and resistance drivers.
  • Comfort operating across strategy, design, and execution phases of transformation work.
  • Growth mindset toward emerging technologies, including the use of AI to enhance change enablement and ways of working.
  • Familiarity with transformation governance, operating model frameworks, and enterprise program environments.

Job Description

Aon is looking for a Property Risk Consultant for our Property Consulting Group

We currently have an exciting career opportunity for a Property Risk Control Consultant. This position will support Aon's Property Risk Consulting Group.

The successful candidate can expect to work with colleagues and clients to develop an understanding of the many property risks posed by fire, earthquake, flood, and other Natural Catastrophes.

This is a remote opportunity but there will be some travel involved.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like:

  • The successful applicant should be familiar with the following:
  • Assembly of Construction, Occupancy, Protection and Exposure (COPE) Data.
  • Brokerage submission information
  • Data assembly
  • Summary documents
  • Broker renewal support
  • Attendance & participation at carrier meetings
  • Vendor management
  • Recommendation review & analysis

Complete property risk control surveys and develop property underwriting reports for a variety of occupancies:

  • Conduct Nat Cat surveys and populate primary and secondary modeling characteristics for modeling.
  • Review of available data to determine natural catastrophe exposure at client locations. Use of available online tools to analyze flood exposures in accordance with NIFP and FEMA guidelines.
  • Coordination of vendor RFPs
  • Knowledge of B&M Jurisdictional inspection requirements
  • Development and review of Maximum Foreseeable (MFL), Probable Maximum (PML) and Normal Loss (NLE) estimates.
  • Hazards associated with a variety of occupancies including manufacturing, warehousing, soft occupancies, etc.
  • Problem solving using the application of Client Standards, NFPA, FM Global or other best practices to resolve technical fire protection issues.
  • 30 to 40% travel will be involved as you may have to visit client sites.

Skills and experience that will lead to success

  • 8 to 10 years with a Highly Protected Risk insurance carrier or vendor.
  • Technically proficient in understanding, interpreting, and applying NFPA and/or FM Global standards; and, evaluating fire protection systems (automatic sprinklers, special extinguishing systems, etc.)
  • Ideal candidate is self-sufficient, organized, and has good written and oral communication skills.
  • Must be physical fit and able to climb ladders and stairs and transition to and from ladders or stairs to access building roof areas and upper or lower floors within a customer site during surveys.
  • Ability to work from home.

Education: Bachelor's degree in Engineering or equivalent years of industry experience and professional certifications.

  • Fire protection certification preferred but not required.

For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances.

Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate.

Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time.

Pay Transparency Laws:

The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $137,000 to $160,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant's education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant's geographic location.

This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon's annual incentive plans to receive [an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan.

A summary of all the benefits offered for this position:

Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon's discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies.

Full job description

Job Description

Posting Description

Who We Are:

NFP, an Aon company, is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. To learn more, please visit: https://www.NFP.com.

This role serves as a strategic connector between carrier partners, broking teams, and business leaders, driving profitable growth and market optimization across the Property & Casualty portfolio. The Portfolio Leader develops and executes carrier relationship strategies, analyzes portfolio performance to identify growth opportunities and risks, and enables producers and brokers with market intelligence, carrier access, and specialized resources. Acting as a key liaison between regional offices, carrier partners, and National Carrier Management, this role helps navigate operational challenges, improves market access, and advances portfolio initiatives that enhance client outcomes, retention, and profitability. Success in this position requires strong relationship management, data-driven decision-making, cross-functional influence, and the ability to lead strategic initiatives.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

1. Carrier Engagement and Relationship Strategy

  • Own and coordinate regional carrier relationship plans in alignment with National Carrier Management priorities and enterprise strategy.
  • Build productive, multi-level relationships with carrier leaders and connect the appropriate regional, broking, industry, risk practice, and specialty resources.
  • Plan and facilitate carrier meetings, appetite reviews, book analyses, growth discussions, and follow-up actions; maintain a consistent and unified message to carrier partners.
  • Curate and distribute current carrier appetite guides, underwriting updates, contact information, market access guidance, and other relevant intelligence.
  • Identify gaps in carrier connectivity or capability and create practical plans to improve engagement, access, and utilization.

2. Portfolio Strategy and Opportunity Identification

  • Analyze the P&C portfolio using internal data, carrier feedback, and market intelligence to identify actionable opportunities and risks.
  • Develop regional portfolio strategies that support profitable growth, retention, margin improvement, client value, and effective market utilization.
  • Identify and advance opportunities involving market consolidation, direct-market access, preferred wholesalers, panels, programs, industry and risk practices, cross-sell, up-sell.
  • Translate portfolio insights into prioritized opportunity pipelines with clear owners, next steps, and measures of progress.
  • Monitor results and communicate trends, barriers, opportunities, and recommended actions to regional and national leadership.

3. Broking Enablement and Practice Connectivity

  • Enable producers, account teams, and broking leaders with carrier intelligence, relationship access, portfolio insights, and enterprise resources.
  • Partner early with broking leaders to align portfolio and carrier strategy before placement activity begins, particularly for priority opportunities and complex issues.
  • Connect teams to industry and risk practice expertise, specialty capabilities, programs, wholesalers, MGAs/MGUs, London and Aon resources, and other relevant solutions.
  • Promote consistent use of approved broking strategies, tools, knowledge repositories, and portfolio initiatives across assigned regions.

4. Carrier Operations Navigation and Escalation

  • Serve as the liaison between regions and National Carrier Management for carrier-related operational needs, including appointments, producer or office codes, portal access, market access, and related support.
  • Help offices identify the correct process, owner, and escalation path; coordinate follow-through when issues span regional, national, carrier, or operational teams.
  • Maintain transparency into recurring access or operational barriers and recommend scalable process, communication, or training improvements.
  • The Portfolio Manager facilitates and navigates support but does not replace the teams accountable for completing operational transactions.

5. Leadership, Governance, and Communication

  • Influence across a matrixed organization without relying on direct authority; establish trust through responsiveness, sound judgment, and follow-through.
  • Create clear priorities, operating cadences, dashboards, and executive updates that make progress and accountability visible.
  • Partner closely with regional P&C leadership, National Carrier Management, national and regional broking leadership, industry and risk practice teams, operations, analytics, and other enterprise partners.
  • Demonstrate the highest standards of integrity, professionalism, confidentiality, and regulatory and compliance awareness.
  • Contribute to the development of portfolio management talent, common practices, tools, and national consistency.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Deep knowledge of commercial P&C distribution, carrier structures, broker operating fundamentals, and the placement lifecycle.
  • Strong portfolio management, carrier relationship management, and consultative problem-solving capabilities.
  • Ability to analyze quantitative and qualitative information, recognize patterns, prioritize opportunities, and convert insights into action.
  • Ability to lead through influence across regional, national, and cross-functional teams in a matrixed environment.
  • Operational judgment sufficient to navigate appointments, codes, market access, portals, and support pathways without assuming transaction ownership.
  • Comfort with data visualization, dashboards, CRM and agency management information, knowledge repositories, and Microsoft 365 tools.

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and proven experience required; advanced degree or professional designation is a plus.
  • Minimum of ten years of commercial insurance, brokerage, carrier management, broking, underwriting, portfolio management, or related experience.
  • Experience using data and market intelligence to shape strategy, improve execution, or identify growth opportunities.
  • Broad exposure to commercial P&C products, carrier capabilities, distribution channels, specialty resources, and brokerage operations.
  • Prior people leadership or team development experience preferred for leadership-level assignments.

Network Architecture & Engineering

Security & Compliance

Carve-Outs & M&A

  • Graduate of accredited school of nursing.
  • Current RN Licensure in state of operation.
  • Certification as a CCM, CIRS, or other Case Management certifications are preferred.
  • A valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and ability to travel to assigned locations is required.

CorVel, a certified Great Place to Work® Company, is a national provider of industry-leading risk management solutions for the workers' compensation, auto, health and disability management industries. Job Description

Senior Account Executive

We are looking for a leader who is responsible for the overall strategy as well as the day-to-day, account management of Aon's relationships with assigned clients as their primary role. You will lead client service teams to identify and meet client needs and thereby retain and grow a profitable book of business. Through service, pricing, consultation, and reporting, you will promote the value Aon delivers to clients.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

  • Retains and grows Aon's business, cultivating relationships with senior-most client decision-makers in the client organization as well as with day-to-day client contacts.
  • Drives the renewal process, assembling the appropriate team to develop and implement the client-specific renewal strategy.
  • Coordinates with Brokers in the development and delivery of renewal strategies.
  • Facilitates critical relationships between clients, Aon and insurers.
  • Ensures client service team understanding of client needs, service delivery methods, and the economic framework relevant to services delivered.
  • Leads stewardship planning and delivery.
  • Ensures overall account profitability with a value-based approach for the scope of service and costs associated with the Client Promise Plan.
  • Arranges Aon compensation for services, whether fee or commission-based, accordingly.
  • Educates clients in risk management, risk transfer, market issues and relevant trends including appropriate data and analytics.
  • Marshals appropriate Aon resources to support clients in unusual circumstances such as large claims, etc.
  • Involves others across geographic (including international), functional and business unit boundaries to define interdependent responses to opportunities to grow the business.
  • Manages input to and follow-up on invoicing and receivables process for assigned clients, ensuring timely collections.

Skills and experience that will lead to success

  • Must have a minimum of 15 years of appropriate risk insurance experience coupled with project and account management experience on large accounts.
  • Strong sales skills
  • Organizational, interpersonal, and project management skills with an ability to multi-task and prioritize workload with attention to detail.
  • Critical thinking skills with the ability to clearly express thoughts and concepts at various levels.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite products such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook
  • Must have an active Property & Casualty license.

Education: Bachelor's degree preferred or equivalent years of industry experience.

Compensation:

The salary range for this position is $250,000 – $325,000 annually. This salary range is an estimate and the actual salary will vary based on applicant's education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant's geographic location.

This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon's annual incentive plans. The amount of the incentive varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan.

How we support our colleagues

Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon's discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance. Various other types of leaves of absence; paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies.

In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce. Plus, our agile environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions for our colleagues as well.

Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant, and more valued.

Aon values an innovative and inclusive workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. Aon is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

Job Description

Aon Is Looking for Interns for the Health Analytics Team

Locations Include:

Chicago, Illinois

As part of an industry-leading team, you will help empower results for our clients by delivering innovative and effective solutions.

Launch Your Career in Health Solutions

We are looking for a Health Analytics Intern to help translate complex health data into clear insights and recommendations for clients.

This role is part of Aon's Health Analytics team within Aon's national Health practice. Our professionals include consultants, data engineers, data scientists, reporting analysts, statisticians, and actuaries who bring unique skills and perspectives to our work. As a core analytics hub, we partner with many high‑visibility Aon business units to bring data‑driven insight into client decisions. Within Health Analytics, you'll work alongside colleagues across key solution areas — Reporting & Analytics, Data Science and Measurement, New Solution Development, Network Analytics, Data Warehouse, Strategic Initiatives, and Data Management & Engineering — all operating as one integrated team. We use robust health data, AI, and deep analytics expertise to turn complex information into clear, actionable insights that enhance consulting and actuarial strategy, differentiate Aon through innovation, and elevate the client experience.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

Recently voted one of the Best Employers for New Grads by Forbes, we are a leading global professional services firm providing a broad range of risk, retirement and health solutions. Our 50,000 colleagues in 120 countries empower results for clients by using proprietary data and analytics to deliver insights that reduce volatility and improve performance.

Your Impact as a Health Analytics Data Intern

Health and Benefits Consulting

Employer-sponsored health and welfare benefit programs form the foundation of the U.S. health care system. These programs have evolved over time as employers have attempted to manage the changing needs of employees, rising program costs and the impact of new legislation while supporting their human resource and business strategies.

What You Will Do:

You will have the opportunity to work on a variety of assignments during your internship. As a Health Analytics intern, you will partner with consultants to shape short- and long-term health and benefits strategies for employers, translating complex data and market insights into clear, compelling presentations and reports.

You will contribute to strategic assessments of the health care market, analyze key trends and help identify innovative solutions for employers' health and benefits challenges. This role is well-suited for someone who enjoys team interaction, can balance multiple priorities and is interested in working with large data sets and using data-driven insights to inform health and benefits strategy. Typical job responsibilities include:

  • Be part of a dynamic team focused on healthcare data and innovation
  • Observe and learn effective client interaction alongside experienced team members
  • Prepare consulting deliverables with the use of charts, visualization tools and reporting automation to communicate end-results of technical analyses to a non-technical audience
  • Work on multiple projects and manage timelines, achievements, and delivery efficiently
  • Work with large health claims and risk datasets such as eligibility data, medical claims and prescription drug claims data from multiple different sources
  • Develop understanding of medical claims reporting and billing for inpatient and outpatient services
  • Support the use and maintenance of data warehouses by organizing data and assisting with data validation and data quality to ensure information is structured for efficient reporting.
  • Assist client teams and actuaries with ad-hoc data related requests by producing reports.
  • Work in data analytics tools and assist in developing data automation processes and R/Python-based data pipelines for data ingestion, cleaning, preparation, and version-controlled workflows.

Aon's Internship Program

Interns within Aon will gain valuable experience assisting our teams supporting both client and internal projects. Interns will work with a cross-functional team to increase exposure across a broad segment of clients. The 10-week summer program includes weekly spotlights delivered by Aon business leaders, a community outreach event and networking opportunities with fellow interns and colleagues.

  • 10-week paid program
  • Challenging work on significant client projects
  • One-on-one internship mentoring
  • Formal and informal feedback throughout the program
  • Significant on the job training and firsthand experience
  • Participation in formal training program taught by Aon's industry professionals

What are we looking for?

Collaborators, analytical experts, problem solvers, clear communicators, relationship-builders and future leaders.

We aim to recruit a group of professionals who offer varying experiences, backgrounds and strengths to ensure we can continue to offer the most innovative solutions to our clients. Additionally, we take into consideration the following:

  • Leadership engagement in extracurricular activities, demonstrating strong interpersonal skills, collaboration and the ability to work effectively in teams.
  • Demonstrates interest in healthcare, life sciences, and employee benefits, with curiosity about industry trends and emerging solutions.
  • Interest in using data and analytics to inform business decisions and support client strategies.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor messages to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office products such as Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook and SharePoint.
  • Experience with data visualization tools to present findings clearly and effectively.
  • Strong quantitative and analytical skills, including the ability to structure problems, interpret results and translate insights into actionable recommendations
  • Relevant coursework or internship experience in consulting, presenting, innovation, or data analysis, particularly in client-facing or project-based settings. Exposure to statistics, computer science, data science, engineering, actuarial science, or other quantitative fields is a plus.
  • Familiarity with modern AI tools and workflows and curiosity about integrating them into analytics solutions is a plus
  • Exposure to Python or R to support data analysis is a plus
  • Foundational understanding of data lakes, data warehouses and integrating data from multiple sources is a plus
  • Familiarity with Databricks for data storage, processing and analytics is a plus
  • Exposure to quantitative analysis, statistical methods, exploratory data analysis, and database or data modeling concepts is a plus.

Applicants for this role, which is part of the Aon Summer Internship Program, should graduate between December 2027 – June 2028 and have a GPA of 3.0 or above.

Job Description

The Head of Employment Law, North America (“NA”), is a Law and Compliance position responsible for partnering with the People Organization, setting and executing Aon's NA employment law strategy in line with Aon's people risk management strategy.The position serves as the company's senior legal advisor on all NA employment law matters for the enterprise. The role provides strategic counsel for NA executive leadership and the People Organization, oversees complex and sensitive internal investigations, and ensures the company's employment practices align with legal requirements, ethical standards, and business objectives across the jurisdictions in which Aon operates. The role also plays a critical role in protecting the company's reputation, culture, and workforce.The role will lead a NA team of employment lawyers and specialists, working closely with functional law support where necessary, ensuring that Aon's People Organization supports business objectives, reinforces Aon's values, and complies with applicable laws and regulations worldwide.This is a hybrid role, based in Chicago or New York, with an expectation of at least three days per week in the office to enable close collaboration with senior stakeholders and key functional partners.Aon is in the business of better decisionsAt Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.What The Day Will Look LikeEmployment Law Leadership, Strategic Advisory and Governance

  • Lead North America employment law strategy in partnership with the NA People Organization, aligned to business priorities, risk appetite, and enterprise transformation goals.
  • Advise on all aspects of employment law, including hiring, performance management, discipline, executive and other terminations, compensation and benefits, incentives, equity plans, accommodations, wage and hour compliance, workplace safety, wellbeing, equal employment obligations, cross border mobility, expatriate arrangements and employee relations.
  • Oversee the development, implementation, and periodic review of NA employment policies, handbooks, and training programs, ensuring compliance across jurisdictions.
  • Advise on the use of AI in talent-related initiatives, ensuring compliance with employment laws and ethical guidelines.
  • Support the People Organization on workforce strategy, organizational design, and change‑management initiatives (e.g., restructurings, global capability centers, reductions‑in‑force, M&A integration).
  • Support employment, restrictive covenant and trade-secret‑related litigation, claims, and agency matters, including strategy, budgeting, and oversight of outside counsel.
  • Serve as a trusted adviser to senior leadership and the People Organization on complex, high‑impact employment law issues affecting NA.
  • Design and maintain NA employment law governance frameworks (policies, standards, escalation protocols).
  • Support and maintain risk assessment and monitoring processes with the People Organization to identify, evaluate, and mitigate employment law risks in NA.

People Leadership & Team Management

  • Lead, develop, inspire and mentor a NA team of employment lawyers and professionals across multiple jurisdictions.
  • Build a high-performing, collaborative culture that emphasizes practical, business‑oriented advice and accountability.
  • Set team objectives, manage budgets, allocate resources effectively and efficiently, while ensuring that the NA employment law team operates in line with the Global Law and Compliance operating model.
  • Drive continuous improvement and an innovative culture around employment law practices including utilization of AI tools.

Training, Culture & Capability Building

  • Design and deliver training in NA for the People Organization, managers, and leaders on key employment law topics and emerging risks.
  • Partner with the People Organization and Compliance to embed a strong culture of respect and ethical conduct in the NA workplace.
  • Lead horizon‑scanning and internal briefings on new legislation, case law, and regulatory expectations affecting employment in NA.
  • Foster an AI-centric culture within the NA Employment law team, staying on top of emerging AI applications, adopting AI to automate routine tasks, boosting productivity and effectiveness of the team.

Experience That Will Lead To Success

  • Law degree (JD or equivalent) and admission to practice in at least one key Aon jurisdiction.
  • 12+ years of post‑qualification experience in employment law, including significant in‑house experience with a highly regulated organization, or top‑tier law firm experience with multinational clients.
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex employment issues.
  • Demonstrated understanding of key NA employment markets
  • Experience with:
  • M&A and other strategic transactions, including employment aspects of due diligence and integration.
  • Restructurings and reorganization projects
  • Restrictive covenant disputes and/or litigation
  • Senior executive employment and compensation matters
  • Discrimination, harassment, and whistleblowing claims

Skills & Competencies

  • Strategic mindset – Translates legal and regulatory developments into clear business implications and strategies that support Aon's priorities. Proven ability to operate effectively in a fast‑paced, matrixed, and highly regulated environment.
  • Business acumen – Understands commercial drivers, critical markets, and the broader risk and regulatory landscape.
  • Executive communication – Communicates complex legal issues clearly and concisely to senior, non‑legal stakeholders.
  • Decision-making & judgment – Balances legal risk with commercial objectives; comfortable making recommendations under uncertainty.
  • Influence & collaboration – Builds strong relationships with the People Organization, business leaders, and functional partners across regions.
  • Change leadership – Supports and enables major firm and functional strategic initiatives (including M&A and transformation) and drives change in policies, processes, and culture.
  • Cultural agility – Operates effectively across multiple cultures, legal systems, and time zones.
  • Integrity & confidentiality – Demonstrates the highest ethical standards, discretion and sound professional judgment.
  • Inspirational and Collaborative leader- experience managing and inspiring high performing teams and influencing senior leaders. Calm under pressure, especially when handling sensitive or high‑stakes matters. Empathetic and skilled at building trust across diverse teams.

Plus, our agile environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself.
